Pa Sa Kumar.b: P. S. Kumar (Pa Sa Kumar) is the current President of the Karnataka Lalithakala Academy and is based in Bengaluru. He is well-known for his illustrations in many notable Kannada literary works, including stories and poems. His artwork not only enhances the beauty and meaning of these pieces but also helps readers connect with them on a deeper level.

M. S. Murthy.b: M.S. Murthy (born 1960) is a renowned Bengaluru-based artist, painter, sculptor, muralist, and author known for his work in gestural abstraction and Buddhist themes. He holds a Diploma from Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath and a Doctorate from Kannada University. A former Chairman of the Karnataka Lalithkala Academy (2015-2017), his art often explores spirituality, silence, and themes like the 'Bowl' or 'Buddha'.

B. S. Lingadevaru.b: B. S. Lingadevaru is a producer and film director who primarily works in the Kannada film industry. He is a recipient of both State and National Film Awards. He is best known for his acclaimed films Naanu Avanalla... Avalu, Mouni, and Kaada Beladingalu.

Shivadhwaj Shetty.b: Shivadhwaj Shetty is a multifaceted creator, director, and performer known for his cinematic artistry across Kannada, Malayalam, Tulu, and Konkani films. With over 40 films to his credit, he has portrayed diverse roles, both lead and supporting, showcasing his versatility. Transitioning to directing, he revealed his true passion. His debut, Gaggara (Tulu), earned a National Award, marking his emergence as a filmmaker of purpose. Naa Puttuna Mannu (Kodava) won the Karnataka State Award, while E-Mannu (Kannada, 2020) received accolades for Best Social Awareness Film and Best Lyrics. In 2022, Koramma garnered a Special Jury Mention at the Bangalore International Film Festival and selections at international festivals, highlighting his commitment to impactful storytelling. His latest work, Imbu, delves into the intersection of modern communication technologies and rural life, exploring how technology shapes confined worlds. Through his narratives, Shetty invites audiences to reflect on the complexities of their own realities.

Pooja Gandhi.b: Pooja Gandhi, who was born in Meerut, India, is an actress and former model who worked predominantly in the Kannada film industry. She rose to fame with her breakout performance in the highly successful film Mungaru Male (2006). Following its success, she became one of the most popular and recognized actresses in Kannada cinema.

Ajay Warrier.b: Ajay Warrier is a renowned playback singer, composer, and live performer, celebrated for his soulful voice and exceptional versatility. Trained in Carnatic classical music, he has recorded thousands of songs across multiple Indian languages for films, devotional albums, and television. Over the years, he has shared the stage with legendary musicians and performed at prestigious concerts in India and abroad. His enduring passion for music, artistic excellence, and captivating stage presence have established him as one of Karnataka's most distinguished musical personalities.

Ravindra Bhat.b: Ravindra Bhat is the Executive Editor of Prajavani, one of Karnataka's leading Kannada newspapers. A journalist since 1990, he has been associated with Prajavani since 1995, serving in various editorial roles across the publication. With a wide range of interests spanning diverse fields, Ravindra Bhat is widely recognized for his investigative reporting and thought-provoking articles. His contributions to Kannada journalism have earned him a reputation for editorial excellence, in-depth analysis, and impactful storytelling.

Nagaraj Vastarey.b: Nagaraj Vastarey is a resident of Bangalore and is an architect by profession. He is also a very well known writer in Kannada and English. He heads the architecture firm called ” Pragrup Amoorthsiti,” and his articles in architecture are published in the reputed national design magazines. As an academician Shri Vastare has spearheaded many studies and academic projects. He also renders his services as a visiting professor at architecture colleges.   Following his passion for literature he writes in both Kannada and English. His writing in Kannada is noticed for its unique style and approach. His writing has a special fan following for its urban flair. He has written several short stories, novels, historical fiction and novella. His stories have been published in many popular periodicals and he has also been a columnist in Kannada Prabha and Udayavani.

Gururaj Kodkani.b: Gururaj Kodkani is a renowned Kannada horror and thriller novelist, columnist, and translator from Yellapur in Uttara Kannada district, currently based in Bengaluru. He began his literary journey as a columnist for Hi Bengaluru and Himagni weekly magazines before establishing himself as a prominent voice in Kannada fiction. Known for his gripping narratives and engaging storytelling, Gururaj Kodkani has earned a dedicated readership in the genres of horror and thriller literature.

P. Sheshadri.b: P Sheshadri is an Indian film director and producer, specifically associated with Kannada feature films. He has made several Kannada feature films and eight of them have won the prestigious National Film Awards. He holds a Master’s degree in Kannada Literature and a Diploma in Journalism. After a short stint as a journalist, he entered the world of television and films.

Nagathihalli Chandrashekar.b: Nagathihalli Chandrashekar is a distinguished Kannada author, storyteller, novelist, columnist, filmmaker, educator, publisher, and cultural thinker. Widely admired for his multifaceted contributions to literature, cinema, and public discourse, he has established himself as one of Karnataka's most influential creative voices.   Fondly known as "Meshtru" (Teacher) by his readers, students, and admirers, Chandrashekar has made a lasting impact through his work as a film and television director, literary mentor, and organizer of cultural initiatives. His writings and creative pursuits reflect a deep engagement with rural life, social realities, and contemporary Kannada culture.   Through his diverse body of work spanning literature, cinema, education, and community leadership, Chandrashekar continues to inspire audiences with his unique storytelling and unwavering commitment to enriching Kannada's literary and cultural landscape.

Kaushik Koodurasthe.b: Kaushik Kuduraste is a prominent Kannada novelist, widely acclaimed for his gripping detective and suspense fiction. Hailing from Kuduraste village in Sakleshpur taluk of Hassan district, he has emerged as one of the notable voices in contemporary Kannada popular literature.   A filmmaker by profession, Kaushik serves as an Assistant Director while pursuing his passion for writing. He is the author of more than 17 suspense and thriller novels, captivating readers with his fast-paced narratives, intricate plots, and compelling storytelling. Through his distinctive style, he has built a dedicated readership and continues to make a significant contribution to the Kannada thriller and detective fiction genre.

Na. Someshwara.b: Na. Someshwara is a distinguished physician, author, and celebrated quiz master from Bengaluru. A medical graduate (MBBS), he has successfully combined his career in medicine with a prolific literary journey, earning widespread recognition for his contributions to Kannada literature, science communication, and public education.   He is best known as the creator and host of the iconic Kannada television quiz show That Anta Heli, which has inspired generations of viewers through its engaging blend of knowledge and entertainment. As the author of more than 30 books, including Anantadedige, O Nanna Chetana, and Namma Dinanityada Aahara, Dr. Someshwara has made complex subjects accessible to readers through his lucid and engaging writing.   His outstanding contributions to literature and public education have been recognized with several prestigious honours, including the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Award. Through his writing, television work, and public engagements, Dr. Someshwara continues to inspire curiosity, learning, and a lifelong love for knowledge.

Narahalli Balasubramanya.b: Narahalli Balasubramanya is a distinguished Kannada literary critic, scholar, and retired professor, widely regarded as one of the foremost voices in contemporary Kannada literary criticism. Through his insightful scholarship and engaging style, he has made complex literary theories and critical concepts accessible to a broad readership.

Girish Kasaravalli.b: Girish Kasaravalli is one of India's most celebrated filmmakers and the foremost pioneer of the New Wave movement in Kannada cinema. Internationally acclaimed for his artistic vision and socially conscious storytelling, he has redefined Indian parallel cinema through films that combine cinematic excellence with profound literary and cultural depth.   A graduate of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, Girish Kasaravalli has directed several landmark films, including Ghatashraddha, Tabarana Kathe, Thaayi Saheba, and Dweepa, many of which have received national and international acclaim. His remarkable body of work has earned him multiple National Film Awards, including several Golden Lotus Awards, as well as the prestigious Padma Shri in recognition of his outstanding contribution to Indian cinema.   Through his work as a filmmaker, documentarian, educator, and mentor, Kasaravalli continues to inspire generations of filmmakers and audiences, leaving an enduring legacy in Kannada and Indian cinema.

Ananya Kasaravalli.b: Ananya Kasaravalli is an acclaimed Kannada filmmaker, actress, and theatre artist whose work seamlessly blends artistic expression with social and cultural narratives. Best known for her award-winning directorial debut Harikatha Prasanga (Chronicles of Hari) , she has earned recognition at national and international film festivals. Through her work as a filmmaker and educator, she continues to champion meaningful storytelling and contemporary Indian cinema.

Vasudhendra.b: Vasudhendra is one of the most celebrated voices in contemporary Kannada literature, acclaimed for his distinctive storytelling and profound exploration of human relationships and social themes. An award-winning author, he has written extensively across genres, with his works translated into numerous Indian languages as well as English and Spanish, earning him a wide national and international readership.   A pioneering and influential literary figure, Vasudhendra is also recognized as one of the first openly gay writers in Kannada literature, whose writings have contributed meaningfully to conversations on identity, inclusivity, and human experience. As the founder and publisher of Chanda Pustaka, he has spent over two decades nurturing emerging literary talent and enriching Kannada publishing. Through his writing and publishing initiatives, Vasudhendra continues to play a vital role in shaping contemporary Kannada literary culture.

G.N.Mohan.b: G. N. Mohan is a distinguished Kannada poet, author, columnist, and media commentator whose contributions have significantly enriched contemporary Kannada literature and journalism. Renowned for his insightful writing and cultural commentary, he has authored acclaimed works spanning poetry, travel writing, and essays.   His award-winning travelogue Nannolagina Haadu Cuba received the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Award and has been included in the curricula of several universities, reflecting its literary and academic significance. In 2007, he founded Avadhi, one of Kannada's most influential literary and cultural digital platforms, which has become a vibrant space for writers, readers, and intellectual discourse.   In recognition of his enduring contributions to Kannada literature, G. N. Mohan has also been honoured with the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi's Sahityashri Award. Through his writing, journalism, and literary initiatives, he continues to shape and inspire Kannada's contemporary literary landscape.

Rajaram Tallur.b: Rajaram Tallur is a freelance journalist and a translator by profession. He has over 25 years of work experience in print and web media. Healthcare, science and developmental journalism are among his areas of interest.

N. S. Madhavan.b: N. S. Madhavan is a leading writer of contemporary Malayalam literature, whose short stories, novels, and travel articles enjoy a wide readership in Malayalam speaking areas of India. He is also a columnist and a former civil servant. During the course of his post-graduation, he began writing and in 1970 he won the top prize for his first published short story Sisu. Madhavan`s novel Lanthanbatheriyile Luthiniyakal was translated into English by Rajesh Rajamohan under the title Litanies of Dutch Battery. It was selected for the Man Asian Literary Prize long list, and was the winner of the 2010 Vodafone Crossword Book Award (Fiction Translation). He has won many awards and accolades including Padmarajan Award (Thiruthu), Odakkuzhal Award (Higuita), Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Story (Higuita), Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Novel (Lanthan Batheriyile Luthiniyakal) and Kerala Sahitya Akademi Fellowship. His recently published book is titled Bheemachan

Ramesh Aravind.b: Ramesh Aravind is a celebrated Kannada actor, filmmaker, writer, television host and motivational speaker. With a career spanning several decades, he has made significant contributions to Indian cinema through his work across Kannada, Tamil, Telugu and Hindi films. Known for his versatility and distinctive screen presence, he has acted in over 140 films and directed several acclaimed movies. Beyond cinema, Ramesh Aravind is widely recognised for his work as a writer, television presenter and speaker. His popular television programmes, including Weekend With Ramesh , have connected him closely with audiences across Karnataka. Through his films, books and public engagements, he continues to inspire audiences with his perspectives on creativity, life, success and human relationships.

Subodh Sankar.b: Subodh Sankar is a Bengaluru-based entrepreneur and cultural curator, best known as the co-founder of Atta Galatta, an independent bookstore, bakery, and vibrant community arts space that has become a prominent part of Bengaluru’s literary and cultural landscape. After moving away from a corporate career in Information Technology, Subodh Sankar pursued his passion for literature, arts, and community-building. Through Atta Galatta, he has helped create a dynamic space for authors, readers, artists, and cultural practitioners to come together, fostering meaningful conversations and celebrating diverse forms of creative expression.

Anita Agnihotri.b: Anita Agnihotri is an acclaimed Indian author, poet, and former Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer, widely regarded as one of the leading voices in contemporary Bengali literature. A prolific writer, she has authored more than 50 books, including novels, short stories, poetry, essays, and children's literature, earning widespread recognition for her powerful narratives and social insight.   Alongside an illustrious literary career, Agnihotri served in the Indian Administrative Service for over three decades, holding several key leadership positions before retiring as Secretary to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. Her extensive public service and deep engagement with issues of social justice have profoundly influenced her literary work.   Through her writings, Anita Agnihotri continues to explore themes of identity, inequality, displacement, and human resilience, establishing herself as one of India's most respected literary and intellectual voices.

Arunava Sinha.b: Arunava Sinha is one of India's most celebrated literary translators, acclaimed for bringing Bengali, Hindi, and English literature to readers across the world. A prolific translator, he has translated more than 100 books, spanning classic, modern, and contemporary fiction, non-fiction, and poetry, making a significant contribution to the global appreciation of Indian literature.   A multiple award-winning translator, Sinha has received numerous prestigious honours, including the Crossword Translation Award, Muse India Translation Award, Kalinga Literary Festival Book Award for Translation, and the Banaras Literature Festival Rabindranath Tagore Award for Translation. His translations have also been shortlisted for several international literary prizes, earning widespread critical acclaim and global readership.   He is currently Professor of Practice in the Department of Creative Writing at Ashoka University and serves as Co-Director of the Ashoka Centre of Translation. Through his scholarship, translations, and teaching, Arunava Sinha continues to play a pivotal role in fostering cross-cultural literary exchange and expanding the global reach of Indian languages and literature.

B. Jeyamohan.b: B. Jeyamohan is one of India's most distinguished contemporary writers, literary critics, and screenwriters, renowned for his contributions to Tamil and Malayalam literature. Celebrated for his profound philosophical insights and masterful storytelling, he has authored numerous acclaimed novels, essays, and works of literary criticism that have shaped modern Indian literature.   He is best known for Venmurasu, an extraordinary 26-volume reimagining of the Mahabharata, widely regarded as one of the longest and most ambitious literary works in modern literature. His landmark novels, including Vishnupuram and Ezhaam Ulagam, have earned widespread critical acclaim for their intellectual depth and narrative brilliance.   Beyond literature, Jeyamohan is a highly regarded screenwriter who has contributed to several acclaimed films, including Ponniyin Selvan and 2.0. Through his writing across literature and cinema, he continues to influence contemporary Indian thought, culture, and storytelling, earning recognition as one of the country's foremost literary voices.

K.R. Meera.b: K. R. Meera is one of the most acclaimed voices in contemporary Malayalam literature, celebrated for her powerful novels, short stories, and essays. After beginning her career as a journalist in 1998, she transitioned to full-time creative writing, earning widespread recognition for her compelling narratives that explore themes of identity, gender, power, and social justice.   Her outstanding literary contributions have been honoured with several of Malayalam literature's highest accolades, including the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award and the Odakkuzhal Award. Widely admired for her distinctive voice and literary excellence, K. R. Meera continues to be one of the most influential authors in modern Indian literature.

Shruti Ramachandran.b: Shruti Ramachandran is an acclaimed Indian actress, writer, and filmmaker, best known for her work in Malayalam cinema. Recognized for her nuanced performances and creative storytelling, she has established herself as a versatile talent in the Indian film industry.   In addition to acting, Shruti co-wrote the "Ilamai Idho Idho" segment of the acclaimed Tamil anthology film Putham Pudhu Kaalai (2020), showcasing her skills as a screenwriter. She was also honoured with the Kerala State Film Award for Best Dubbing Artist in 2020 for her performance in Kamala.   Through her work across acting, writing, and filmmaking, Shruti Ramachandran continues to contribute to contemporary Indian cinema with creativity, sensitivity, and artistic excellence.

Francis Thomas.b: Francis Thomas is an acclaimed Indian screenwriter, copywriter, and creative director known for his contributions to advertising and cinema. A graduate in Visual Communication from Loyola College, Chennai, with a Master's degree in Advertising and Marketing from Xavier College, Mumbai, he has built a distinguished career at the intersection of storytelling and creative communication.   Before entering the film industry, Francis held leadership roles at some of India's leading advertising agencies, creating award-winning campaigns that earned national recognition. He made his screenwriting debut with the acclaimed Malayalam film Anveshanam (2020) and later gained widespread appreciation for Putham Pudhu Kaalai (2020).   Blending cinematic storytelling with years of creative expertise, Francis Thomas continues to be a prominent voice in contemporary Indian cinema and advertising, celebrated for his compelling narratives and innovative creative vision.

Darshan Puttannaiah.b: Darshan Puttannaiah is an Indian politician, technology entrepreneur, and social activist, currently serving as the Member of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly (MLA) representing the Melukote Assembly constituency. Elected in 2023, he represents the Sarvodaya Karnataka Paksha (SKP), a political party rooted in Karnataka's farmers' movements and committed to sustainable development, rural empowerment, and social justice.   Blending experience in technology with grassroots public service, Darshan Puttannaiah has emerged as a prominent advocate for agrarian issues, environmental sustainability, and people-centric governance. Through his work in public life, he continues to champion inclusive policies and community-driven development, earning recognition as one of Karnataka's emerging political leaders.

Keshava Guha.b: Keshava Guha is an Indian novelist, journalist, and literary agent. Known for his sharp, introspective fiction and commentary on contemporary Indian society, he is a prominent voice in modern Indian English literature

Perumal Murugan.b: Perumal Murugan is one of the most celebrated contemporary Tamil authors, scholars, and literary critics, renowned for his profound exploration of rural life, identity, and social realities. Deeply rooted in the culture and history of the Kongu Nadu region, his writings have earned widespread acclaim for their literary depth, authenticity, and human insight.   The author of twelve novels, along with acclaimed collections of short stories, poetry, and works on language and literary studies, Murugan has made an enduring contribution to modern Tamil literature. His notable works include Madhorubhagan (One Part Woman), Pookkuzhi (Pyre), Fire Bird, Thiruchengodu, Mayam, and Neer Vilaiyattu.   His works have received national and international recognition through acclaimed English translations. One Part Woman, translated by Aniruddhan Vasudevan, earned the Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize, while Pyre was longlisted for the International Booker Prize. His novel Fire Bird received the prestigious JCB Prize for Literature, further cementing his reputation as one of India's foremost literary voices.

Paul Zacharia.b: Paul Zacharia is one of the most distinguished voices in contemporary Malayalam literature, acclaimed as a novelist, short story writer, essayist, and public intellectual. Renowned for his bold, unconventional storytelling and incisive social commentary, his works are celebrated for their wit, narrative innovation, and fearless engagement with political and cultural issues.   A prolific author whose writings have been translated into English and several other languages, Zacharia is widely regarded as one of India's foremost literary figures. His uncompromising literary vision and thought-provoking essays have made him an influential voice in public discourse as well as modern Indian literature.   His outstanding contributions have been recognized with prestigious honours, including the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Katha Award. His works are also part of the Library of Congress collection, reflecting their enduring literary significance and international recognition.

Mallika Prasad.b: Mallika Prasad is an accomplished Indian actor, writer, director, educator, and voice specialist whose work spans theatre, film, television, and performance training. With advanced training from the National School of Drama (NSD) and Goldsmiths, University of London, she has built an acclaimed career across multiple languages and artistic disciplines.   She gained nationwide recognition for her powerful performance as Amma in Mardaani 3 (2026). Her notable screen credits include the National Award-winning Kannada film Kanooru Heggadathi, Devi Ahilya Bai, Almost Pyaar with DJ Mohabbat, Killer Soup, and Aspirants. As a filmmaker, she wrote and directed For My Ela (2025), which has received international acclaim at film festivals.   Mallika is the Founder and Artistic Director of Actors Ensemble India Forum and the founder of Vachika Voicework. A respected actor, director, and voice teacher, she also serves as Associate Teacher and South Asia Regional Head for the Fitzmaurice Voice Institute. Through her work in performance, education, and filmmaking, she continues to make a significant contribution to contemporary Indian theatre and cinema.

T.M.Krishna.b: T. M. Krishna is one of India's most distinguished Carnatic vocalists, acclaimed author, and public intellectual. Renowned for his exceptional artistry and progressive vision, he has played a transformative role in reimagining the relationship between music, culture, and society through performance, scholarship, and public engagement.   His acclaimed book, A Southern Music: The Karnatik Story, offers a groundbreaking exploration of the philosophy, aesthetics, and socio-political dimensions of Carnatic music and received the Tata Literature Live! First Book Award for Non-Fiction. A passionate advocate for inclusivity and cultural dialogue, Krishna has founded and supported several initiatives dedicated to expanding access to music and the arts.   In recognition of his outstanding contributions to culture and social change, he was awarded the prestigious Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2016. Through his music, writing, and activism, T. M. Krishna continues to inspire conversations on art, equality, and the transformative power of culture.

Arundhati Ghosh.b: Arundhati Ghosh is a distinguished Indian writer, cultural practitioner, and social activist based in Bengaluru. With over three decades of experience in the arts and culture sector, she is widely recognized for her leadership in cultural philanthropy and her commitment to fostering inclusive and independent artistic practices across India.   A thoughtful and compelling contemporary writer, Ghosh's work explores themes of identity, intimacy, relationships, and the complexities of modern life with sensitivity and nuance. Through her writing, public engagement, and cultural leadership, she has made significant contributions to shaping conversations around art, society, and creative expression.   Her work continues to inspire artists, writers, and cultural institutions, establishing her as one of India's leading voices in the intersection of literature, culture, and social change.

Ba Na Subramanya.b: Ba. Na. Subramanya is a veteran Kannada journalist and film critic known for his significant contributions to cinema writing and criticism. With a keen understanding of Kannada cinema, his work reflects a thoughtful engagement with films, filmmakers, and the evolving landscape of Indian cinema. His contribution to film writing was recognized at the 69th National Film Awards, where he received a Special Mention for Best Writing on Cinema in 2023. Through his journalism and critical writing, Subramanya Badoor continues to contribute meaningfully to Kannada film discourse.

Uday kumar Irvathur.b: Uday Kumar Irvathur is a distinguished academician and writer hailing from Karkala, Udupi district. Following a dedicated career in higher education, he recently retired as the Principal of the University College in Hampankatta, Mangaluru. Deeply rooted in the region's literary and cultural landscape, Dr. Irvathur remains highly active as a prominent Kannada writer, insightful columnist.

Vasundhara Bhupathi.b: Vasundhara Bhupathi is well-known as a doctor, writer, organizer, social activist, and columnist. More than 75 of her works have been published across various genres, including medical literature, short stories, plays, poetry, and book editing.

Vikram Hathwar.b: Vikram Hathwar is a noted Kannada writer from Kundapur who received the Yuva Sahitya Puraskar for his debut short story collection. He has carved a distinct place for himself in contemporary Kannada literature through his creative and thought-provoking writing. His notable works include Zero Mattu Ondu, Akshi Enditu Vruksha, Nee Maayeyolago, and Hamara Bajaj.

Meghana Sudhindra.b: Meghana Sudhindra is a writer and technology professional from Jayanagar, Bengaluru. She holds an M.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence and Signal Processing from a university in Barcelona and currently writes the “Megha Male” column on Book Brahma.

Ajay Kumar Singh.b: Ajay Kumar Singh, former Director General of Police (DGP), Karnataka, is widely recognized for leading the investigation into the 2005 terrorist attack at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), an experience he has described as the most challenging of his distinguished career. Beyond his professional accomplishments, Dr. Singh is a committed Gandhian and an avid lover of poetry. In a candid conversation with Aksheev Thakur, he offers a rare glimpse into the person behind the khaki, revealing the values, reflections, and passions that have shaped his life.

Angela Thomas.b: Angela Thomas, is a lawyer and public policy professional working at theintersection of technology, law, and policy, with a focus on digital rights, privacy, dataprotection, free speech, and net neutrality. At SFLC.in, a digital rights organisationbased in India, she leads the organisation’s work on free speech and artificialintelligence, while contributing to broader research and advocacy on how technologyregulation shapes fundamental rights. Her work involves engaging withpolicymakers, conducting research, and developing policy recommendations onplatform accountability, online speech, and emerging AI governance frameworks.

Sandhyarani.b: Sandhyarani is a journalist, author, and film critic from Bangarapet in Karnataka's Kolar district. She contributes as a columnist to several Kannada digital publications and is known for her insightful writing on literature, society, and cinema.   Her notable works include Yake Kadutide Summane (a collection of columns), Thumbe Hoo (a biography), and Poorvi Kalyani (a play). She also wrote the screenplay for the National Award-winning Kannada film Nathicharami. Through her work across literature, journalism, and cinema, Sandhyarani has established herself as a distinctive and respected creative voice in contemporary Kannada culture.

Madhumita Kumar Rajan.b: Madhumita Kumar Rajan is a lawyer and member of the Free Libraries Network (FLN).FLN is a collective of community-owned and free libraries across India working toadvance the right to read and equitable access to books. FLN is also demanding lawand policy that recognizes reading as a right and a framework for free public librariesthat are inclusive and serve all.A graduate of the National Law School of India University, Madhumita has worked inthe publishing, industry, including as Head of Legal at publishing houses. Sheadvises authors, publishers, and non-profit organizations on issues relating topublishing, copyright, and access to knowledge.

Laxmi Murthy.b: Laxmi Murthy is a journalist and researcher based in Bangalore. She hasworked in senior editorial positions at the Women’s Feature Service, HimalSouthasian and the International Federation of Journalists. She has specialistexpertise in the areas of press freedom; gender and media; journalists’ rights andconflict reporting. Laxmi has worked with feminist publishing house, Zubaan Books,New Delhi on research on sexual violence an impunity, and initiatives on feministarchiving. Laxmi is one of the founder-members of the Network of Women in Media, India, aforum for women media professionals across India. She is also co-founder editor ofthe Free Speech Collective, a platform for journalists and free speech advocates toprotect and promote the right to free speech and expression.

Rachita Taneja.b: Rachita Taneja is an award-winning Indian cartoonist, satirist, and artist, best known as the creator of Sanitary Panels , a widely acclaimed political webcomic. Through her distinctive stick-figure-style comics, she offers sharp, insightful, and often humorous commentary on current affairs, social justice, and contemporary political issues from a distinctly feminist perspective. Her work has garnered a substantial audience across digital platforms, including Instagram, Facebook, and X, where she publishes under the handle @sanitarypanels . Recognized internationally for her courageous and impactful satire, Rachita Taneja was honoured with the prestigious Kofi Annan Courage in Cartooning Award 2024 . Through her art and storytelling, she continues to provoke thought, encourage dialogue, and challenge societal norms, establishing herself as one of India’s most influential contemporary satirical voices.

Shobha Malavalli.b: Shobha Malavalli is a distinguished journalist with over 26 years of experience in the media industry. Widely respected for her contributions to journalism, she is equally admired for her deep appreciation of literature and culture, her spiritual outlook, and her warmth, humility, and integrity.   Known for her thoughtful engagement with literary and cultural discourse, Shobha Malavalli has earned a reputation as a respected voice in Karnataka's media and literary circles.

Ramu Patil.b: Ramu Patil is a senior journalist known for his excellent communication skills, strong leadership, and insightful reporting.   He is an alumnus of the International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP) conducted by the U.S. Department of State and has also completed the BBC Journalists' Training Programme.   Ramu Patil is a recipient of the Karnataka Media Academy Award. In 2012, he received the prestigious Press Institute of India (PII) – International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) Award for Best Humanitarian Reporting in Indian Print Media, in recognition of his reports from Baghdad and other parts of Iraq.

D. Umapathi.b: D. Umapathi is a senior journalist and columnist known for his impactful reporting and insightful political commentary. He has served as the New Delhi correspondent for Prajavani, Kannada Prabha (The New Indian Express Group), and ETV, earning recognition for his incisive coverage of national affairs.   Over the course of his career, he has contributed columns to leading Kannada publications, including Andolana, Raitha Chaluvali, Vijaya Karnataka, Prajavani, Samyukta Karnataka, and Vartha Bharati. He is the author of two acclaimed books, Delhi Nota and Padakusiye Nelavilla, which reflect his keen observations on politics

H. N. Arathi.b: H. N. Arathi is a poet, journalist, and television presenter. She is the daughter of renowned scholar Hampa Nagarajaiah and acclaimed writer Kamala Hampana. Arathi is best known for conceptualizing and directing the immensely popular Doordarshan quiz show That Anta Heli!?, which successfully completed over 2,500 episodes.   A contemporary poet with a distinctive literary voice, Arathi's work engages deeply with the social and cultural realities of our times. In addition to her original writing, she is an accomplished translator and has published several works across literature and journalism. Her poems have been translated into English, Slovenian, and six other languages, reflecting the broad appeal of her literary contributions.

S. Nataraja Budalu.b: S. Nataraja Budalu is an acclaimed Kannada writer, researcher, and cultural thinker, widely recognized for his contributions to literature and intellectual discourse. His writings thoughtfully bring the rich philosophical traditions of Buddhism and the Shramana movement into contemporary Kannada literature, making these timeless ideas accessible to modern readers.   A distinguished translator and scholar, Dr. Budalu received the Sahitya Akademi Award (2020) for his acclaimed Kannada translation of Sarahapada, a landmark work that reflects his deep engagement with India's literary and philosophical heritage.

Basavaraj Kalgudi.b: Dr. Basavaraj Kalgudi is a distinguished Kannada writer, critic, poet, and scholar whose work has significantly shaped contemporary Kannada literary criticism. A former professor of Kannada and an acclaimed public intellectual, he has authored numerous books on literature, culture, and aesthetics. Known for his insightful literary analysis and advocacy of Indian language literature, he has represented Kannada literature at national and international forums and currently serves as the Convener of the Kannada Advisory Board of the Sahitya Akademi

Subhash Rajamane.b: Subhash Rajamane is a distinguished Kannada writer and translator, originally from Kusanal village in Athani taluk of Belagavi district, Karnataka. He holds a bachelor's degree from Bangalore University, a master's degree in Kannada from the University of Mysore, a Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) from Mangalore University, and a Doctorate from Kannada University, Hampi.   Widely recognized for his contributions to Kannada literature and translation, Dr. Rajamane's work reflects a deep engagement with language, culture, and literary scholarship. Through his writing and translations, he has made significant contributions to enriching contemporary Kannada literary discourse.

Krishnamurthy Hanur.b: Krishnamurthy Hanur is a renowned Kannada folklorist, author, and academic with over four decades of experience teaching folklore, ancient Kannada literature, and novels. Based in Mysore, he is known for his work on the "Encyclopaedia of Folk Culture in Karnataka" and for highlighting narratives from marginalized communities.

M.S. Ashadevi.b: M.S Ashadevi is a feminist writer and prominent critic in Kannada. Her research study on Feminism and 12th Century Women Writers is considered to be a path breaking work in feminist studies. Her prominent awards include Sahitya Akademi Award, MM Kalburgi National Award, Akkamahadevi Award, etc. She teaches Kannada in Maharani Cluster University of Bengaluru.

Shyamsundara Bidarakundi.b: Shyamsundar Bidarakundi is a Kannada poet, critic, author, and retired professor based in Hubballi. A prominent figure in literary and cultural circles, he has written extensively under the pen names Sarvajit, Jwalanta, and Priyamvada. He has authored several books and contributed significantly to Kannada literature through his writings and cultural engagements.

H.N. Muralidhara.b: H. N. Muralidhara is a distinguished Kannada author, literary scholar, and academic, renowned for his significant contributions to Kannada literature and education. A respected professor of Kannada, he has devoted decades to the study and promotion of Kannada literary traditions, with particular expertise in Kannada literature, Dasa Sahitya, and value-based education.   Through his scholarship, teaching, and literary works, Prof. Muralidhara has played a pivotal role in advancing Kannada literary studies while fostering a deeper appreciation of Karnataka's rich cultural and intellectual heritage.

M.R.Dattathtri.b: M. R. Dattathri is an acclaimed Kannada and English author, poet, and columnist, as well as a seasoned information technology professional with extensive experience in leading multinational companies in India and the United States. A novelist at heart, he is celebrated for his compelling storytelling and nuanced exploration of contemporary themes.   His body of work includes critically acclaimed novels, poetry, and essays, several of which have received prestigious literary honours and have been translated into Telugu, extending his readership beyond Karnataka. His English novel What's Your Price, Mr. Shivaswamy?, published by Penguin Random House India, is a translation of his award-winning Kannada novel Ondondu Talegū Ondondu Bele.   Dattathri is the recipient of numerous literary accolades, including the Masti Prashasti (2019), Book Brahma Best Novel of the Year Award (2023), Vardhamana Prashasti (2023), and the Sunanda Belgaokar Award (2025), among several others. Through his novels, poetry, and columns, he continues to make a significant contribution to contemporary Kannada literature.

Kiran Upadhyaya.b: Kiran Upadhyaya is a Kannada author, translator, and cultural ambassador whose work reflects a deep engagement with literature, language, and the global Kannada community. Originally from Kumta in Uttara Kannada district and educated in Sirsi, he began his professional career as a civil engineer, working with leading industrial organizations before relocating to the Gulf, where he has lived and worked in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain for over three decades.   He is the author of more than five books, including the translated work Aastikate and the acclaimed titles Vishwatomukha, Videshavasi, Paradeshavasi, Horadeshavasi, and Dooradeshavasi. He also serves as an international correspondent for Vishwavani daily, bringing global perspectives and international developments to Kannada readers.

Ajay Varma Alluri.b: Ajay Varma Alluri is a bilingual writer, poet, and literary translator working across Telugu, Kannada, and English. A graduate of the University of Hyderabad , he is deeply engaged in Indian language literature, translation, and comparative literary studies. His work focuses on bridging linguistic and cultural boundaries by translating significant literary works and promoting dialogue between regional literary traditions. Ajay has been recognized for his contributions to translation, including the Kuvempu Bhasha Bharathi Annual Book Award for his Kannada translation of Volga's Vimuktha . He continues to contribute to literary publishing, editing, and cultural initiatives that celebrate multilingual literature.

T. G. Srinidhi.b: T. G. Srinidhi is a distinguished technology writer, engineer, and science communicator who has made significant contributions to promoting technology and digital literacy in Kannada. An engineering graduate with advanced qualifications, he has successfully bridged the gap between technology and regional language communication through his extensive writings and public outreach.   A prolific author and columnist, Srinidhi has written thousands of articles and several acclaimed books that make complex concepts in science and technology accessible to Kannada readers. His work has demonstrated that technology can be effectively communicated in Kannada without compromising depth or clarity. In recognition of his contributions, he has received the Karnataka Science and Technology Academy Award, while his Kannada technology blog e-Jnana has earned national recognition as one of India's best blogs.   Alongside his literary pursuits, Srinidhi is an accomplished IT professional with an international technology organization. He is a regular invitee to present papers at the India International Science Festival and is widely recognized for his efforts to popularize science and technology education in Kannada. Through the e-Jnana Trust, he promotes reading among underprivileged children, supports educational initiatives, and advocates the effective use of technology for the growth and preservation of the Kannada language. His pioneering work continues to inspire a new generation of readers, learners, and technology enthusiasts.

K.E. Radhakrishna.b: K. E. Radhakrishna is a distinguished Indian educationist, writer, playwright, musicologist, columnist, and public intellectual. With a Master's degree in English Literature and an LL.B. from Bangalore University, he has built a multifaceted career spanning literature, education, music, and public affairs.   Renowned for his insightful writings and thought-provoking contributions to public discourse, Radhakrishna has made a lasting impact through his work as an author, dramatist, and columnist. His scholarship and cultural engagement reflect a deep commitment to the advancement of literature, education, and the arts, earning him recognition as one of Karnataka's respected literary and intellectual voices.

Nithyananda B. Shetty.b: Nithyananda B. Shetty is a Professor of Kannada Studies at Tumkur University and a distinguished scholar of Kannada literature and culture. He holds a Ph.D. from Mangalore University for his research on Kannada Samskruti Vangmaya (Cultural Discourse in Kannada).   His academic interests include Kannada Studies, Cultural Studies, Film Studies, Philosophy, and Kannada–Tulu literature. He has published extensively in the fields of cultural history and humanities and has served as the Editor of the UGC-CARE listed journal Loka Jnana. He is the author of Maarganveshane, a book on Kannada literary research and methodology, and has edited the Kannada edition of the four-volume Kalatatvakosha, an encyclopaedia of fundamental concepts in Indian arts.

Poornima Malagimani.b: Poornima Malagimani is an emerging Kannada author, novelist, and creative writer whose work spans literature, technology, and leadership. An Electronics and Communication Engineering graduate from S.J.M.I.T., Chitradurga, she began her professional career as an officer in the Aeronautical Engineering Department of the Indian Air Force, where she served for six years. She later worked as a Joint Deputy Director in a Government of India organization and currently serves as the Chief Operations Officer at Metiskill Global Solutions, Bengaluru.   A prolific writer, Poornima has authored several novels, short stories, and literary works. Her technical and literary articles have been widely published in leading Kannada newspapers and online journals. Recognized for her literary excellence, she has received numerous honours, including the Kannada Sahitya Parishat Datti Prashasti.   Poornima is also a sought-after speaker and panelist at literature festivals, Kannada literary conferences, International Women's Day events, and academic institutions. Through her writing and public engagements, she continues to inspire readers by bringing together contemporary thought, literary creativity, and professional experience.

Jayaram Patil.b: Jayaram Patil is a cultural activist and arts administrator closely associated with legendary theatre personality B. V. Karanth. He serves as the Managing Trustee of the Babukodi B. V. Karanth Trust and the Ram Govind Trust, both of which are dedicated to promoting theatre, art, and cultural activities. Through his leadership, he has made significant contributions to preserving and nurturing Karnataka's rich cultural heritage.

Akshara K.V..b: Akshara K. V. is a distinguished Kannada theatre practitioner, director, teacher, author, and publisher, widely recognized for his outstanding contributions to Kannada theatre and cultural discourse. Educated in literature at Sagara, he received professional theatre training at the National School of Drama, New Delhi , and earned a Master’s degree in Theatre Arts from the Workshop Theatre, University of Leeds, United Kingdom . He has been closely associated with the Ninasam group of organizations as a theatre teacher, director, and administrator, playing a pivotal role in shaping generations of theatre practitioners and enriching Karnataka’s cultural landscape. He also heads Akshara Prakashana , one of the most prominent publishing houses in Kannada. Akshara K. V. has written and directed numerous Kannada plays, taught theatre extensively, and presented papers at various national and international seminars. He has authored more than fifteen books on drama, theatre, cinema, culture, and society, and has translated significant essays and books from English into Kannada. His literary and theatrical contributions have earned him several prestigious honours, including three Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Awards and the Karnataka Nataka Akademi Fellowship .

Abhimanyu Bhupathi.b: Abhimanyu Bhupathi is a theatre director, actor, singer, and founder of the Bengaluru Theatre Ensemble. A prominent voice in contemporary Kannada theatre, he has directed and performed in several acclaimed productions, blending classical traditions with modern storytelling. His work spans theatre, music, and performance, reflecting a deep commitment to nurturing innovative stagecraft and promoting Kannada performing arts.

Rashmi S.b: Rashmi S is a senior journalist, writer, and translator. Born and raised in Bidar, she holds a Master's degree in Journalism and began her career as a Sub-Editor at Prajavani. She is currently the Editor of Sudha Weekly and serves as a Member of the Karnataka Media Academy.   She is the author of several books, including Ankura (translation), Mathu Kathiyadaga, Midumaatu, Ee Pic Yaar Click, Bisilina Adeshto Tunukugalu (translated from Amrita Pritam), and Oorembo Ooru Ooru Usabari. She has received numerous honours, including the Karnataka State Book Authority Award, the Avva Award, and the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Karnataka Working Journalists' Association.

C. Somashekhara.b: C. Somashekhara is a retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Karnataka cadre. During his distinguished administrative career, he served in several key leadership positions, including Managing Director, Commissioner, Secretary, Director, and Deputy Commissioner across various departments of the Government of Karnataka.   Known for his extensive experience in public administration and governance, his final assignment was as Secretary, Department of Co-operation, Government of Karnataka, from November 2013 to June 2014.

T.P.Ashoka.b: T. P. Ashoka is a distinguished Kannada literary critic, scholar, and educator, widely respected for his lifelong dedication to literature and cultural thought. Recognized as one of the leading voices in Kannada literary criticism, he has made significant contributions through his insightful analyses, scholarly writings, and unwavering commitment to the study and appreciation of Kannada literature.   A former professor, T. P. Ashoka has been closely associated with Ninasam, where he has played a pivotal role in literary and cultural initiatives, workshops, and intellectual discourse. His extensive body of work—including books, essays, and newspaper columns—reflects a profound engagement with Kannada's rich literary heritage. Rather than pursuing novelty for its own sake, his writings illuminate the enduring relevance of classic and contemporary Kannada literature, guiding readers toward deeper understanding and appreciation.   Through decades of teaching, research, writing, and cultural leadership, T. P. Ashoka has inspired generations of students, writers, and readers, establishing himself as one of the most influential literary thinkers in contemporary Kannada.

S.R.Vijayashankar.b: S. R. Vijayashankar is a distinguished Kannada literary critic, educator, journalist, and communications strategist, widely respected for his contributions to Kannada literature and public discourse. With an accomplished career in corporate communications, including leadership roles at leading global technology companies, he has successfully bridged the worlds of industry and literature.   A prolific writer and insightful critic, Vijayashankar has contributed extensively to leading Kannada publications and literary forums. He is closely associated with Ninasam, where he has served for many years as a resource person at its renowned literary camps and festivals, mentoring readers, writers, and students alike. Through his thoughtful criticism, lectures, and essays, he continues to enrich contemporary Kannada literary thought and inspire meaningful engagement with literature.

Vikram Visaji.b: Vikram Visaji is a distinguished Kannada poet, literary critic, translator, researcher, and academic whose contributions have earned him a prominent place in contemporary Kannada literature. A professor and research guide, he has mentored postgraduate and doctoral students while actively contributing to literary scholarship and creative writing. His published works include the poetry collections Neeveke Kattala Kade, Tamasha, and Goodu Kattuva Chitra; Huchchu Dalimbe Gida, a translation of Greek poetry; Belagina Mukha, a work of literary criticism; Nadagalu Nudiyagali, a research publication; and an edited volume on the plays of Dr. Chandrashekhara Kambara. Dr. Visaji has received numerous prestigious literary honours, including the Bharatiya Bhasha Parishad Young Writer Award and the Kannada Sahitya Parishat's Sri Vijaya Award, in recognition of his outstanding contributions to Kannada literature. Through his writing, research, and teaching, he continues to inspire a new generation of readers, scholars, and writers.

Sridhar Balagar.b: Sridhar Balagar is an acclaimed Kannada author, short story writer, novelist, and academic from Uttara Kannada. A professor at Kamala Baliga College of Education, Kumta, he is widely recognized for his distinctive literary voice and significant contributions to contemporary Kannada fiction.   His acclaimed works include Adhomukha, Mukhantara, Ile Emba Kanasu, and Aadukala, which explore the complexities of human relationships, society, and rural life with remarkable depth and sensitivity. A two-time recipient of the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Book Award, Balagar's writings have been translated into several Indian languages and are prescribed in university curricula, reflecting their enduring literary and academic significance.   Through his creative writing and academic engagement, Sridhar Balagar continues to enrich Kannada literature and inspire readers, students, and fellow writers alike.

K. Satyanarayan.b: K. Satyanarayana is a distinguished Kannada author, novelist, short story writer, essayist, literary critic, and columnist whose multifaceted contributions have enriched contemporary Kannada literature. Alongside a distinguished career in the Indian Revenue Service, where he served as Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, he built an exceptional literary legacy spanning fiction, essays, memoirs, travel writing, and literary criticism.   The author of numerous acclaimed works across diverse genres, Dr. Satyanarayana has been honoured with several prestigious literary awards, including multiple Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Awards, the Masti Award, the M. V. Seetharamiah (MVC) Award of the B. M. Sree Foundation, and an Honorary Doctorate from Bangalore University. His insightful writing, marked by intellectual depth and social sensitivity, has established him as one of the leading voices in modern Kannada literature.

Guruprasad Kantalagere.b: Guruprasad Kantalagere is a promising Kannada short story writer and educator from Kantalagere in Tumakuru district. Widely appreciated for his evocative storytelling, he draws inspiration from everyday life and social realities, crafting narratives that resonate with authenticity and emotional depth.   His literary works have earned recognition in prestigious short story competitions conducted by Prajavani and Vijaya Karnataka. His acclaimed short story collection Govina Jaadu received the Ananya Award in 2017, establishing him as one of the notable young voices in contemporary Kannada literature.   Through his writing and teaching, Guruprasad Kantalagere continues to contribute to the growth of Kannada literature while inspiring readers with stories rooted in human experience and social insight.

Deepa Hiregutti.b: Deepa Hiregutti is a distinguished Kannada author, columnist, and cultural thinker, widely recognized for her insightful writings on literature, society, and personal development. An educator by profession, she has established herself as a prominent voice in contemporary Kannada literary and intellectual discourse. A prolific writer, her articles and columns have appeared in leading Kannada newspapers and magazines across the state. Her well-known column "Naanu, Neevu Mattu..." has earned appreciation for its thoughtful reflections on everyday life and society. Her notable publications include the poetry collection Parimalavillada Hoogala Madhye and the acclaimed books Phoenix – Solisabahudu Solanne!, Brand Builders – Bitti Belesi BeLedavaru, and Solemba Belaku. Deepa Hiregutti has received numerous literary honours, including the Gudibande Poornima Datti Award, the Ratnamma Hegde Award, and the prestigious Mayura Varma Award from the Karnataka Sahitya Parishat. Through her writing, teaching, and cultural engagement, she continues to inspire readers with her thoughtful perspectives and literary excellence.

Gopal Krishna Pai.b: Gopal Krishna Pai is a distinguished Kannada novelist, short story writer, and screenwriter whose contributions have significantly enriched both Kannada literature and cinema. Renowned for his evocative storytelling and literary craftsmanship, he has earned widespread acclaim for works that explore history, culture, and the human condition.   His celebrated novel Swapna Saraswata received the prestigious Sahitya Akademi Award, has been translated into several Indian languages, and continues to be the subject of academic research. As a screenwriter, he has collaborated on acclaimed films directed by Girish Kasaravalli, with his screenplays earning both National and Karnataka State Film Awards.   Through his enduring contributions to literature and cinema, Gopal Krishna Pai has established himself as one of the most respected and influential voices in contemporary Kannada culture.

Indrakumar H.B.b: Indrakumar H.B. is a government school teacher and a noted Kannada writer. He has published five short story collections and four novels. He has received several prestigious literary honours, including two Book Brahma Awards, the Kuvempu Prize, U.R. Ananthamurthy Prize, G.S. Shivarudrappa Prize, Besagarahalli Ramanna Story Prize, H. Shantharam Prize, Basavaraja Kattimani Prashasthi and Aralu Prashasthi. He has also won a gold medal in the Gulbarga University story-writing competition. His stories have been translated and published in Marathi and Malayalam, and his story Soojidaara has been adapted into a film. He has served as a state-level resource person for developing school textbooks and training manuals. His 1,500-page novel Innu Samudra... is among his notable literary works.

Nagendra Shah.b: Nagendra Shah is a Kannada film actor known for his contributions to the Kannada film industry. Recognized for his compelling screen presence and versatile performances, he has appeared in several notable films, earning appreciation from audiences and critics alike.

Purushottam Bilimale.b: Purushottama Bilimale is a distinguished Kannada scholar, folklorist, author, and academic, widely recognized for his significant contributions to Kannada literature, folklore studies, and cultural scholarship. A former Professor of Kannada at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi, he has played a pivotal role in advancing the study of Kannada language, literature, and folk traditions at the national level.   A prominent voice in the Bandaya and Dalit literary movements, Dr. Bilimale's writings combine scholarly insight with a deep commitment to social and cultural discourse. His notable works include Dalita Jagattu, Karavali Janapada, Koodukattu, and Bahuroopa, all of which have made lasting contributions to Kannada literary and folkloric studies.   His outstanding contributions have been recognized with several prestigious honours, including the Karnataka Janapada Academy Award and the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award, cementing his place among Karnataka's most respected literary scholars and cultural thinkers.

Madhu Y. N..b: Hailing from Tumakuru district, Madhu Y. N. is a celebrated voice in contemporary Kannada literature who masterfully bridges the worlds of modern technology and profound storytelling. An engineer by profession with degrees from the Global Academy of Technology and BITS Pilani, he began his career at Infosys and currently works with IBM in Bengaluru. His literary journey gained major recognition when his debut short story collection, Karehannu, won the prestigious Ee Hottige Short Story Collection Award in 2019. Since then, he has pioneered new genres in Kannada, authoring acclaimed works like the tech essay collection Dark Web, the experimental short story collection FIFO, and the non-fiction guide Artificial Intelligence - In Simple Kannada. His acclaimed novels, Kanase Kadumallige and Inti Poorvi, belong to the bildungsroman genre—a rarity in Kannada literature. He is also a passionate science communicator who pens the popular "TechPost" column for Vijaya Karnataka.

N. Manu Chakravarthy.b: N. Manu Chakravarthy is an academician, professor, writer, and cultural critic based in Bengaluru. A distinguished scholar of cultural studies, film theory, feminist thought, and literary criticism, he has made significant contributions to the study of art, cinema, and contemporary culture.   His writings critically examine the intersections of literature, media, identity, gender, and postcolonial thought, offering fresh perspectives on the social and political dimensions of culture. Through his research and publications, he continues to enrich contemporary discourse on aesthetics, cultural theory, and creative expression.

Vidyarashmi Pelathadka.b: Vidyarashmi Pelathadka is a distinguished Kannada poet, writer, and senior journalist, originally from Pelathadka village on the Karnataka–Kerala border. With a strong presence in both literature and journalism, she has established herself as an important voice in contemporary Kannada writing. She currently serves as the Chief of the Magazine Section at Vijaya Karnataka, one of Karnataka’s leading Kannada daily newspapers. Through her literary work and long-standing engagement with journalism, Vidyarashmi Pelathadka continues to contribute significantly to Kannada literature and the media landscape.

O. L Nagabhushana Swamy.b: Prof. O. L. Nagabhushana Swamy is an eminent Kannada literary critic, translator, educator, and author with over six decades of contribution to literature and academia. Having authored more than 60 books, he has played a pivotal role in enriching Kannada literary criticism and bringing world literature to Kannada readers through acclaimed translations. A recipient of the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award and Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Award, he continues to be one of Karnataka's most respected literary voices

Subbu Holeyar.b: Subbu Holeyar (H. K. Subbaiah) is a distinguished Kannada poet, author, and television presenter, widely recognized for his evocative poetry and contributions to Kannada literature and media. Trained in theatre at Ninasam, Heggodu, he has seamlessly combined literary expression with performance and public engagement.   He currently serves as a presenter on Doordarshan Chandana and is the author of acclaimed poetry collections, including Soojigatrada Kolaveyinda Manushyanobban Haadu and Ellara Beralalloo Antikonda Dukhave. His autobiographical work Dana Kayadavanu was adapted into the feature film Kariya Kanbitta, further extending the reach of his literary work.   A recipient of the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Award and several other prestigious literary honours, Subbu Holeyar continues to be a significant voice in contemporary Kannada literature, celebrated for his sensitive portrayal of human experiences and social realities.

L. N. Mukundaraj.b: L. N. Mukundaraj is a renowned writer of the new generation, a Kannada MA holder who has served in various government degree colleges. He has published poetry collections like Desh Kosha Dasavala, Nirankusha, plays like Vaishampayana Thira, Ego Panjara Ago Mugilu, Sangrama Bharata, many biographies and translated works. He has also participated in and acted in All India Radio and Doordarshan programs. Apart from participating in many poetry gatherings, he has also worked as the editor of Talented Parliamentary Writers' Book Series and Suvarna Sambraham. He has worked as a leader of teachers' organizations, founder of many organizations, and convener of the PU Curriculum Board. He has received awards such as the Karnataka Sahitya Academy, Visvesvaraya Award, Kempegowda Award.

Indudhara Honnapura.b: Indudhara Honnapura is a prominent Kannada writer, investigative journalist, and social activist who co-founded the historic Dalit Sangharsh Samiti (DSS) in Karnataka, India. A pioneer of Dalit protest literature, he voiced systemic struggles through influential works like his poem "Kappu Manujaru" and served as the first editor of the anti-caste magazine Shoshita. Honnapura further strengthened alternative media by founding and editing the Kannada weekly newspaper Suddi Sangaati while contributing heavily to mainstream investigative journalism through Prajavani.

Allam Rajaiah.b: Allam Rajaiah is a noted Telugu writer, and critic, widely recognized for his progressive and socially conscious literary contributions. Emerging from the tradition of revolutionary and left-oriented literature in Andhra Pradesh, his works reflect deep engagement with Marxist thought, people’s struggles, and the complexities of rural and working-class life. Rajaiah’s writings—spanning poetry, short stories, and critical essays—are marked by clarity, sharp political insight, and empathy for marginalized voices. He has been instrumental in shaping Telugu subaltern and Marxist literary discourse, often highlighting exploitation, inequality, and the quest for justice. Beyond creative writing, he is also respected as a critic who provided intellectual grounding to people’s literature movements in Telugu. His association with literary organizations and people’s movements has enriched his perspective, making him both a cultural activist and a literary figure. Through his works, Allam Rajaiah continues to inspire readers and fellow writers to view literature as a tool for social transformation.

Nandini Sidda reddy.b: Nandini Sidda Reddy is an eminent Telugu poet, professor, and activist who championed the Telangana statehood movement. He co-founded the Manjira Rachayitala Sangam to foster regional literature and later served as the historic first Chairperson of the Telangana Sahitya Akademi.Renowned for writing the iconic cultural anthem "Nageti salalo", his poetry deeply captures rural life and social struggles. He won the prestigious National Sahitya Akademi Award for his poetry collection Animesha, which poignantly details human isolation and labor hardships. His powerful literary legacy continues to inspire generations, cementing his status as a true people's poet.

Naresh Kumar Sufi.b: Naresh Kumar (Naresh Kumar Soofee) I am Naresh Kumar, known in Telugu literary circles as Naresh Kumar Soofee. I come from a small village in Peddapalli district, Telangana, that was wiped off the map by Singareni coal mining. I currently live in Hyderabad, where I work as a book designer and editor. I have been writing for nearly a decade. My literary journey began with poetry, and over the years my work has explored social realities, love, politics, history, and human relationships. My published poetry collections are Nisshabdam (2019) and Anamakuni Aathmageetham (2024). My short story collections include Peruleni Vennela (2023) and Memories of Mangalipalle (2024). My novels are Hidimbi (2025) and Mukkonapu Premakatha (2026). I have also translated the internationally acclaimed novel Jamilya from English into Telugu. Beyond my work as a writer, I am actively involved in book design, editing, and publishing, contributing to contemporary Telugu literature through the making of books as well as writing them. I believe that literature is my way of discovering myself amidst people, history, and marginalized lives of understanding who I am, both as a human being and as a citizen. This belief continues to shape my writing.

Kavi Yakoob.b: Kavi Yakoob is a prominent Telugu poet, writer, researcher, and singer who has made significant contributions to contemporary Telugu literature. He is also an Associate Professor at Anwarul Uloom College, affiliated with Osmania University, where he combines his academic work with his literary pursuits. A respected voice in Telugu literary circles, Kavi Yakoob is also an Advisory Board Member of the Telugu division of the Kendra Sahitya Akademi. Through his poetry, research, writing, and engagement with the literary community, he continues to contribute to the growth and evolution of contemporary Telugu literature.

Kondepudi Nirmala.b: Nirmala Kondepudi is a noted Telugu poet, short story writer, satirist, and journalist. She has published six poetry collections, two short story anthologies, and numerous socio-political satirical writings celebrated for their sharp social insight and humor. She was the first young woman poet to receive the prestigious Kumaran Asan Award from the Government of Kerala and was also honored by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 2000 for her literary excellence. Beginning her journalism career in 1978 as a Sub-Editor at Andhra Jyothi , she served for over 15 years across print, electronic, and digital media. Her work has focused on women's issues, investigative journalism, and social development. Her writings are widely studied, with several works included in the M.A. Telugu curriculum.

Bandi Narayanswamy.b: Bandi Narayanswamy is a Telugu writer, novelist and a teacher. He won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2019 for his novel Saptabhoomi. He published the novel in 2017 and got the Telugu Association of North America Award for the same.

Maruthi Powrohitham.b: Maruthi Powrohitham is a noted Telugu short story writer and novelist. He has published two acclaimed short story anthologies, Urimarlu and Illidisina Tommidi Kathalu, along with the novel Pranaya Hampi. The novel was translated into Kannada by Kum. Vee, introducing his work to a wider readership.   Maruthi Powrohitham currently serves as a Senior Lecturer at the Government Teacher Training College, Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh.

Vivek Lankamala.b: Vivek Lankamala is a software engineer by profession and a writer by passion. He hails from Kadapa in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh and comes from a rural farming family. His parents continue to pursue agriculture, a background that deeply influences his writing and worldview.   Vivek's literary works reflect the lives, landscapes, and experiences of rural Andhra Pradesh. His published works include Lankamala Daarullo, a travelogue; Valapateddu, a collection of short stories; and Pottelu, a novel. Through his writing, he explores themes rooted in everyday life, culture, and human relationships with authenticity and sensitivity.

Sri Uha S.b: Sri Uha S is a Telugu and English author, social impact leader, and speaker. She is the author of three Telugu short story collections—Isuka Addam, Balkaav, and Sikka. Her writing explores human relationships, women's lives, identity, and resilience. She serves as Director – Rural Development, Government of Telangana, and holds an MBA from IIM Calcutta. She has received several literary honours, including recognition as one of the 50 Inspiring Women of Telangana and the Voice of Telangana Award for her contribution to Telugu literature.

Akkiraju Bhattiprolu.b: Akkiraju Bhattiprolu is a Telugu writer, translator, and literary commentator. He is the author of the acclaimed short story collection Moodu Beerla Tharavata (After Three Beers) and the translator of South vs North: India's Great Divide into Telugu as Uttara Dakshinaalu. He co-edited Kotha Katha 2017, an anthology of emerging Telugu short story writers, and has been an active contributor to online Telugu literary platforms for over three decades. Originally from the Bhadrachalam region of Telangana, Akkiraju worked as a software engineer in the United States before returning to India. His experience in technology, entrepreneurship, and multicultural environments continues to shape his literary perspective.

Kuppili Padma.b: Kuppili Padma is a prominent Telugu writer, columnist, and media professional. She has authored over 162 short stories, published in 10 short story collections, along with three novels, two collections of creative prose, and three poetry collections. Her works have been translated into English, Kannada, and Tamil. A leading voice in contemporary Telugu literature, she has received numerous honours, including the K. N. Y. Patanjali Sahithi Puraskaram (2026) and the Government of Andhra Pradesh Sahitya Puraskaram (2025).

Mohammed Khadeer Babu.b: Mohammed Khadeer Babu is a senior journalist and award-winning writer in Telugu with short stories, anthologies, non-fiction books and movies to his credit. A twotime Katha awardee, his stories have won various prizes at the state and national level and earned him the Govt of AP Achievement Award in 2023.

Dondapati Nagajyothy.b: Dondapati Nagajyothi Sekhar is a Telugu poet, short story writer, and government school teacher from Konaseema, Andhra Pradesh. She is the author of two poetry collections, Reppavaalchani Swapnam and Chigurinche Pageelu. Her poems and stories have appeared in leading literary magazines and have been broadcast by All India Radio, Visakhapatnam. A participant in several national and international literary events, she is listed in the Telugu Book of Records. She has received numerous honours, including the Sirikona Academy Best Debut Book Award, the Ravi Rangarao Sahitya Peetham Award, and the Hasini Ramachandra Literary Foundation Poetry Award, for her significant contribution to contemporary Telugu literature.

Shilalolitha.b: Shilalolitha (Dr. P. Lakshmi) is a distinguished Telugu poet, feminist writer, literary critic, and researcher. She holds M.A., M.Phil., and Ph.D. degrees in Telugu, and her doctoral research on women's poetry in Telugu literature received the Best Research Award (2008). She is the recipient of several honours, including the Ramya Sahithi Award (2005), Hyderabad Bharathi Award (2006), and the Vasireddy Ranganayakamma Memorial Prize from Telugu University (2007). Her notable works include the poetry collections Panjaranni Nene Pakshini Nene, Enthena Duram, Gaaju Nandi, and Nenu Ikkadi Bhumini; the research volumes Kavayitrula Kavithvamlo Streela Manobhavaalu and Telugu Kavayitrula Kavitwam – Pariseelana; and the critical work Naari Saarinchi. Selected as a National Poet by All India Radio for her poem Logili Bayata, she has been a long-time columnist for the feminist magazine Bhoomika and serves on its editorial board. A committed social activist, Shilalolitha's poems have been translated into several Indian and international languages, and she continues to be a prominent voice in contemporary Telugu literature.

R. M. Umamaheswara Rao.b: R. M. Umamaheswara Rao is a distinguished Telugu journalist, writer, and editor. He earned a PhD from Sri Venkateswara University on “Mother in Telugu Short Stories”. Rao began his journalism career reporting for Lawyer Weekly and went on to hold key editorial roles at Eenadu and Andhra Jyothi, including Sunday supplement editor, edition in-charge, news editor, and currently assistant editor. He also served as output editor for HNTV and oversees coverage for Rayalaseema and Nellore districts. His reportage spans grassroots social movements, Naxalite regions, rural distress, and the Telugu diaspora across South and Southeast Asia. An accomplished writer, his short stories—translated into Kannada, English, and Tamil—appear in multiple anthologies. He has authored essay collections like Katha Samayam and Telugu Jadalu and conducted interviews with leading literary figures. Rao received the first Best Rural Telugu Journalist Award in 2007, instituted by journalist Palagummi Sainath, and later accolades from the Andhra Pradesh government and other literary bodies.

Indira Krishnappa.b: Indira Krishnappa is a prominent social worker, writer, and activist based in Bengaluru, Karnataka. She serves as the Honorary Secretary of the Karnataka Gandhi Smaraka Nidhi at Gandhi Bhavan and heads the Prof. B. Krishnappa Trust, actively working to preserve the legacy of her late husband, the renowned Dalit movement leader and writer, Prof. B. Krishnappa.

Sudhakar Unudurti.b: Sudhakar Unudurti is a Hyderabad-based Telugu writer known for his historical fiction, including short stories and novels. Originally from Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, he began his career as a marine engineer in the merchant navy before turning to creative writing after retirement. His works draw on maritime history, India's colonial past, and the Buddhist heritage of the Kalinga-Andhra coastal region. His notable publications include the short story collections Toorupu Gaalulu (2018) and Chalicheemala Kavaatu (2021); the award-winning novels Yaaraada Konda and Chedarina Paadamudralu, which received the American Telugu Association (ATA) Awards in 2020 and 2024; and the co-authored non-fiction book Tathaagatuni Adugujaadalu (2019), which explores historical Buddhist sites around Visakhapatnam. His stories have also been translated into English as East Wind (2023) and into Kannada as Moodana Maarutha (2025). His forthcoming books include Arakappu Allam Tea, a collection of short stories, and Uppugaali Kaburlu, a memoir of his experiences as a marine engineer at sea.

D. V. Guruprasad.b: D. V. Guruprasad is an Indian author and retired Indian Police Service officer who served for 35 years, retiring in 2011 as Director General of Police in Karnataka. A prolific writer with over seventy books in Kannada and English, his works span criminal psychology, police procedures, crime prevention, gender issues, child rights, humour, and travelogues, including bestsellers with multiple reprints and an autobiography detailing high-profile cases and encounters with public figures.   Guruprasad began his career as a journalist after earning a Master of Arts in English literature, later joining the IPS in 1976 while continuing to write extensively, including over 700 articles and ongoing newspaper columns on public safety and social issues. He holds a Ph.D. from Gulbarga University (1993) for his thesis The Letter in Indian Writing in English, which was published and established personal correspondence as a literary genre in Indian English writing. Post-retirement, he focused on full-time authorship and served as CEO of an educational and healthcare trust in Bengaluru, where he resides. His police tenure emphasized community-oriented crime reduction, reflected in books like case studies for officers and guides to criminal law, earning recognition such as the President's Police Medal for distinguished service.

Hampa Nagarajaiah.b: Hampa Nagarajaiah (Hampana) is a distinguished Kannada scholar, researcher, author, and cultural administrator, widely acclaimed for his profound contributions to Kannada language, literature, and Jain studies. Renowned for his rigorous scholarship and literary excellence, he has played a pivotal role in advancing the study and preservation of Karnataka’s rich cultural heritage.   Over a career spanning more than four decades, Hampa Nagarajaiah has devoted himself to teaching, research, cultural administration, and literary organization.
