His extensive body of work has significantly enriched Kannada literary scholarship, particularly in the fields of Jainism, classical literature, and cultural history.   Through his writings, research, and leadership in literary and cultural institutions, Hampanā continues to inspire generations of scholars, writers, and readers, establishing himself as one of the most respected intellectual figures in contemporary Kannada literature.

N. Vadivelan.b: N. Vadivelan is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Tamil, specializing in Tamil Literature, Folklore, and Anthropology. He earned his Ph.D. from Tamil University in 2025 with a dissertation on the history and oral traditions of tea plantation workers in Idukki, Kerala. He has participated in numerous national and international conferences, presenting research on folklore, tribal traditions, plantation workers, and Tamil cultural heritage, and has published scholarly articles in UGC CARE-listed journals.   His research interests include Tamil folklore, oral traditions, anthropology, and the cultural history of marginalized communities. He has also undergone advanced training in research methodology, folklore studies, and Classical Tamil literature, and has delivered invited lectures on the folklore and cultural life of tea plantation workers.

Savitha.b: Savitha (born 24 May 1981) is a Tamil writer, poet, short story writer, and columnist from Dharmapuri district, Tamil Nadu. She holds degrees in Commerce, Business Administration, and English, along with a Diploma in Montessori Education, and also works as a dialogue writer for Tamil television serials. She began her literary career as a poet and has published four poetry collections and a short story collection. Her poems, stories, essays, and literary articles have appeared in several leading Tamil literary journals and online magazines. A member of the Nayagi collective, she actively promotes the recognition of women's achievements through literary and cultural initiatives. Known for her emotionally resonant and socially conscious writing, Savitha received recognition in the 2023 Zero Degree Short Story Competition for her short story Thiral Kani.

Mu. Kulasekaran.b: Mu. Kulasekaran (born 21 July 1961) is a Tamil poet, novelist, short story writer, and essayist. His works explore human relationships, lived experiences, and socio-political realities with depth and sensitivity. Widely recognized as a significant voice in contemporary Tamil literature, he has written poetry, fiction, and essays that have appeared in leading literary journals. Several of his poems and short stories have also been translated into English.

Harisankar.b: Harisankar is a contemporary Tamil writer from Puducherry, known for his novels, short stories, and novellas. He began writing at the age of seventeen, with his children's story series Mayapadagu published in Puduvai Bharathi. His works are deeply rooted in the social and cultural life of Puducherry. He is the author of the novels Paris, Mahe Café, Truths, Lies, Imaginations, and Karappan (2026). In addition, he has published four short story collections and two volumes of novellas. His novel Paris and two of his short stories have been translated into French, earning his work wider recognition beyond Tamil readers.

S. Kayal.b: S. Kayal is a Tamil writer, poet, translator, and academic. She has published six poetry collections and translated three short story collections into Tamil. Her Tamil translation of Nobel laureate Abdulrazak Gurnah's novel Afterlives, titled Porozhindha Vaazhvu (2024), received the prestigious Pollachi Naa. Mahalingam Award for Translation. Her translation of Nermin Yıldırım's Secrets Dreamed in Istanbul, published as Istanbullin Ragasiyak Kanavugal (2025), was honoured with the Arachelvar Seenu Chellappa Award for Translation. Two more translated works are forthcoming. Holding multiple postgraduate and doctoral qualifications, Dr. Kayal has over 27 years of experience in higher education. She is currently an Associate Professor in the Department of Commerce at Muthurangam Government Arts College, Vellore, where she combines her academic career with a distinguished contribution to Tamil literature and translation.

S. A. Vengada Soupraya Nayagar.b: S. A. Vengada Soupraya Nayagar is a distinguished academic, trilingual writer, and literary translator from Puducherry. A pioneer of direct French–Tamil translation, he has translated the works of renowned authors such as Albert Camus, J.M.G. Le Clézio, and Tahar Ben Jelloun, while also translating classical Tamil Sangam literature into French. Formerly the Head of the Department of French at the Kanchi Mamunivar Government Institute for Postgraduate Studies and Research, Puducherry, he holds a Ph.D. in French from Pondicherry University. His contributions have earned him the Romain Rolland Book Prize (2021), the Sparrow Literary Award (2020), and international recognition, including literary residencies and participation in major literary events in France. After retirement, he continues to dedicate himself to literary translation and mentoring aspiring translators.

Siddharthan Sundaram.b: Siddharthan Sundaram is a Bengaluru-based translator, writer, and literary critic from Madurai. Holding an MBA and a PGSCM, he took voluntary retirement in 2014 after more than two decades with leading market research firms, including ORG, ORG-MARG, and Nielsen. A prolific translator, he has translated over 20 books into Tamil, including works by Malcolm Gladwell, Philip Kotler, Harper Lee, J.D. Salinger, Svetlana Alexievich, Vithal Venkatesh Kamath, Subroto Bagchi, Ravi Subramanian, and others. His translations have been published by leading publishers such as Vikatan, NBT, Sixthsense, Ethir, Seermai, Pustaka, and the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation. He received the Kalaignar Karunanidhi Porkizhi Award for Translation in 2018. In addition to translation, he writes on literature, retail, economics, market research, and entrepreneurship for prominent English and Tamil publications.

Sivaprasath.b: Sivaprasath is a noted Tamil writer, editor, and literary speaker with over two decades of contribution to contemporary Tamil literature. His short stories have appeared in leading Tamil print and digital literary journals. He has edited the posthumous collections of contemporary Kannada short stories translated by the late Prof. Nanjundan, including Paal Meesai and Kaatrin Nizhal. Based in Salem, Sivaprasath coordinates the Sorsunai literary forum and frequently delivers lectures on modern literature at academic institutions.

Rayagiri Shankar.b: Rayagiri Shankar (Sankaranarayanan, born 24 January 1980) is a Tamil writer, poet, essayist, and editor. He writes short stories, poetry, and essays, and is recognized as a distinctive voice in contemporary Tamil literature. His notable works include the poetry collection Sudarakalin Madhu, the short story collection Shokalmil Enchupavan, and the essay collection Kamam Seppadhu Kandhu Mozhimo. He is also the editor of the online literary magazine Mayir.

E. Thangamani.b: E. Thangamani is a Tamil writer, reviewer, and avid reader from Dharmapuri district, Tamil Nadu. A farmer by background and a school teacher by profession, he is deeply committed to promoting literature and reading culture. He serves as the Coordinator of Takadur Book Forum, actively organizing literary initiatives and engaging with readers and writers. Passionate about environmental conservation and travel, Thangamani's interests enrich his literary perspective and community work, making him a prominent voice in Tamil literary and cultural circles.

Vignesh Hariharan.b: Vignesh Hariharan is an attorney, literary critic, translator, and public speaker. He holds graduate and postgraduate degrees in Law, along with a postgraduate diploma in Translation and Creative Writing from Ahmedabad University. His Tamil translation of Su. Venugopal's Resurrection was shortlisted for the Mozhi Prize in 2022 and featured in the Mozhi Anthology of Short Stories published by South Side Books. His essays on Tamil literature have appeared in leading literary magazines, including Neeli, Vallinam, Vanam, Vasagasalai, Solvanam, Kalachuvadu, Kaalam, and The Hindu (Tamil Edition). He also runs The Reading Lab, an online initiative that promotes reading among young people, and is a sought-after speaker on Tamil literature.

Sujatha Selvaraj.b: Sujatha Selvaraj is a Tamil poet and short story writer from Tiruchirapalli district, Tamil Nadu, currently based in Bengaluru. A former school teacher with over a decade of teaching experience, she began her literary journey in 2010 with the poem Tholaindhu Ponavargal, published in Ananda Vikatan. She has since established herself as a distinctive voice in contemporary Tamil literature. She is the author of the poetry collections Kaalangalai Kadandhu Varubavan (2014) and Kadalai Kalavaadubaval (2024), and the short story collection Kannimarsamy (2025), published by Kalachuvadu Publications. Her poems and stories have appeared in leading Tamil literary magazines, including Kalachuvadu, Ananda Vikatan, Kanaiyazhi, Uyir Ezhutthu, Amrutha, Kalki, and Kumkumam. She received the Tiruppur Arima Sakthi Literary Award (2014) and the Ezhuthukkalam Literary Award (2025) for her contributions to Tamil literature.

Ra. Kaviyarasu.b: Ra. Kaviyarasu (born 25 December 1986) is a Tamil poet known for his existentialist poetry. His literary journey began with the publication of his first poem in Kalki magazine in 2005, and he has been writing poetry consistently since 2010. His debut poetry collection, Naalai Kaanamal Pogiravar (2020), received critical acclaim. A recipient of the Kanavu Ilakkiya Virudhu (2021), Sengani Pathippaga Virudhu (2021), and Namakkal Tamilsanga Arakattalai Virudhu (2022), he also writes essays on contemporary Tamil poetry through his personal website.

A. Munavarkhan.b: A. Munavarkhan is a retired school principal with over 30 years of experience in the field of education. An avid reader and essayist, he is the author of the essay collection Kaapi Aaruvatharku Mun (Before the Coffee Gets Cold). His essays on a wide range of subjects have appeared in online literary magazines such as Nadugal and Yaavarum.com, while his translated poems and short stories have been published in leading Tamil literary magazines, including Aavanazhi and Kalachuvadu. He currently resides in Salem, Tamil Nadu, and continues to actively contribute to Tamil literary circles.

J. Rajagopalan.b: J. Rajagopalan is a Tamil literary scholar, author, trainer, and management consultant with over 35 years of engagement in Classical, Modern, and Bhakti Tamil literature. He has conducted more than 25 literary workshops across India, Singapore, and Malaysia, and since 2023 has been delivering a comprehensive lecture series on the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham. A faculty member of Jeyamohan's Unified Wisdom programme, he has also served as a manuscript development editor for contemporary Tamil publications. Professionally, he has over 20 years of experience in the banking and insurance sectors and currently heads an L&D consultancy focused on management development for MSMEs. His published books include Ellam Mudivile Inbam, Aattathin Ainthu Viththigal, and the novel Deivanallur Kathaigal. His forthcoming book, Nilaththodu Neere, explores ecological perspectives in Sangam literature.

Swetha Yerram.b: Swetha Yerram is an independent publisher, and the co-founder of Aju Publications, established in 2022. After transitioning from a career in data analysis to full-time publishing, she is dedicated to amplifying Telugu voices for a wider audience. One of Aju Publications' recent fiction novels, Amma Diary lo Konni Pajeelu, has become a national bestseller, captivating Telugu readers worldwide. With a strategic approach to social media, and a commitment to nurturing literary talent, Swetha is at the forefront of modern Telugu publishing, championing regional literature on a larger stage.

Harini Nagendra.b: Harini Nagendra is a distinguished ecologist, author, and public intellectual, currently serving as Professor of Ecology at Azim Premji University. Renowned for her work on nature, urban sustainability, and environmental governance, she is one of India’s leading voices in the field of sustainability studies. Her internationally acclaimed scholarship has earned her several prestigious honours, including the Cozzarelli Prize from the U.S. National Academy of Sciences, the Elinor Ostrom Senior Scholar Award, and the Clarivate Web of Science Award for Interdisciplinary Research in India. Through her research, writing, and public engagement, Nagendra has made significant contributions to understanding the complex relationship between people, cities, and the natural world. A widely respected speaker and writer, Harini Nagendra continues to inspire global conversations on ecology, conservation, and sustainable living, bridging academic research with public discourse and policy-making.

Prajna Neelgund Shanthinath.b: Prajna Neelgund Shanthinath holds an M.Tech from IIT Bombay and began her career as a Software Engineer at Cisco. She later served for over 12 years as Administrator and Trustee of Deenabandhu Trust, leading initiatives in child care, school development, and teacher training. She is the Founder of Studio Bharat, where she designs and conducts workshops that nurture creativity, communication, confidence, and holistic child development through theatre, storytelling, and Indian culture.   A graduate of NINASAM Theatre Institute, Prajna has acted in over 10 theatre productions with more than 120 stage performances. She has written and directed several children's plays and has extensive experience using theatre as a medium for learning and self-expression.   She has authored educational film scripts, published articles on child development and education in Anubhava magazine, and co-authored the paper Supporting Child Caregivers in South Indian Orphanages: Identifying "Ghosts" and Creating "Angels", published in Institutionalised Children: Explorations and Beyond, a peer-reviewed, bi-annual international academic journal.

M.S. Sriram.b: M. S. Sriram is a distinguished academic, author, and Kannada short story writer, celebrated for seamlessly blending scholarly insight with creative expression. Renowned for his contributions to management, finance, and public policy, he has also enriched contemporary Kannada literature through his thoughtful and engaging short stories.   His literary works are marked by keen observation, subtle humour, and profound insights into human relationships and modern society. Through sensitive and elegant storytelling, Sriram captures the complexities of everyday life, making his narratives both deeply relatable and intellectually reflective.   Alongside his literary pursuits, he has held leadership positions in premier academic institutions and has written extensively on economics, financial inclusion, and institutional development. His unique ability to move effortlessly between academia and literature has established him as a distinctive and respected voice in contemporary Kannada letters.

Binod Chaudhary.b: Binod Chaudhary is a renowned industrialist, philanthropist, author, and one of South Asia’s most influential business leaders. As Chairman of CG Corp Global, Nepal’s first multinational conglomerate, he has transformed a family enterprise into a global business group with interests spanning food and beverages, hospitality, banking, real estate, education, healthcare, and renewable energy across multiple continents.   Widely recognized as Nepal’s first billionaire, Chaudhary is a passionate advocate for entrepreneurship, innovation, and sustainable development. Through the Chaudhary Foundation, he has led impactful philanthropic initiatives in disaster relief, education, healthcare, and community development, benefiting thousands of people in Nepal and beyond.   An accomplished author, his memoir Making It Big chronicles his remarkable entrepreneurial journey and leadership philosophy. Through his visionary leadership, resilience, and commitment to social and economic progress, Binod Chaudhary continues to inspire aspiring entrepreneurs and business leaders across the world.

V. Veerappan.b: V. Veerappan is an accomplished industry leader and technology executive, currently serving as the President of ELCITA (Electronics City Industrial Township Authority). With decades of experience in India's technology and manufacturing ecosystem, he has been at the forefront of driving industrial development, infrastructure planning, and collaborative governance in one of the country's largest technology hubs. Under his leadership, ELCITA has championed initiatives in smart urban infrastructure, sustainability, mobility, environmental management, and public-private partnerships, making Electronics City a model for integrated industrial townships. Veerappan is widely respected for fostering collaboration between industry, government, and civic bodies to create a world-class business environment. He is also a strong advocate for innovation, skill development, and the growth of Karnataka's technology ecosystem. His vision and leadership continue to strengthen Electronics City's position as a global destination for technology, manufacturing, and innovation-led economic growth.

Archana Vasudev.b: Archana Vasudev is a storyteller, writer, and founder of Talkative, with experience spanning film, communication, and education. She is the writer of the Malayalam feature film ‘HER’ (streaming on Manorama Max) and the short film “Atmanirbhar” (telecast on MTV). Her debut script earned her the 2024 Kerala State Critics Special Jury Award.

Anupama Raju.b: Anupama Raju is an accomplished poet, novelist, translator, literary journalist, and communications professional whose work has earned widespread recognition in contemporary Indian English literature. She is the author of the poetry collections Bitter Gourd and Nine, and the acclaimed novel C: a novel, with her writings widely anthologized in India and abroad.   Recognized by India Today as one of the leading young Indian poets writing in English, Anupama has collaborated on several interdisciplinary projects that bring together poetry, photography, and performance. Her notable collaborations include the Indo-French projects Surfaces and Depths and Une Ville, Un Lieu, Une Personne with French photographer Pascal Bernard, as well as Nine – Our Circle of Lines, a dance-and-poetry performance created with dancer Dr. Rajashree Warrier.   A Charles Wallace Fellow at the University of Kent, Canterbury, and Writer-in-Residence at Center Intermondes, La Rochelle, France, Anupama also holds a Ph.D. in the use of poetry in leadership communications. She is an alumna of the Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and currently works in Strategic Communications at UST, while continuing to contribute significantly to literature, translation, and interdisciplinary arts.

Preethi Nagaraj.b: Preethi Nagaraj is a distinguished journalist, author, columnist, and theatre practitioner with over two decades of experience in mainstream media. Fluent in both English and Kannada, she has established herself as a prominent voice in journalism and contemporary literary discourse.   As a columnist for Prajavani, Preethi Nagaraj is widely recognized for her insightful writing and compelling narratives that engage with culture, society, and public life. She is also an influential presence in Kannada theatre, contributing significantly to the performing arts through her creative and cultural engagement.   Her literary excellence has been honoured with several prestigious accolades, including the Sarojini Naidu Prize and the Karnataka Sahitya Academy Book Prize. Through her work across journalism, literature, and theatre, Preethi Nagaraj continues to enrich Karnataka’s cultural landscape with her thoughtful perspectives and artistic contributions.

Harish Bhat.b: Harish Bhat is an accomplished marketer, bestselling author, and corporate leader, renowned for his contributions to business, branding, and literature. His diverse body of work spans business history, fiction, poetry, and humour, reflecting his remarkable versatility as a writer.   Four of his books — #Tata Stories, Office Secrets, Tata Log, and Jamsetji Tata: Powerful Learnings for Corporate Success — have been national bestsellers and translated into several Indian languages, earning widespread acclaim among readers across the country.   Harish has had a distinguished career with the Tata Group, serving for nearly four decades in several senior leadership roles, including Brand Custodian at Tata Sons, Managing Director and CEO of Tata Global Beverages, and Chief Operating Officer of the Watches and Jewellery businesses at Titan Company. He currently serves as a director on the boards of several Tata companies.   An alumnus of BITS Pilani and IIM Ahmedabad, Harish Bhat has been recognized as one of LinkedIn’s Top Voices in India. In 2022 and 2023, Forbes listed him among the world’s top ten most influential Chief Marketing Officers. A sought-after keynote speaker, he continues to inspire audiences through his insights on leadership, innovation, branding, and storytelling.

Vineetha Vijayakumar.b: Vineetha Vijayakumar is an Indian entrepreneur, former IT professional, and passionate bibliophile, best known as the founder and Reader-in-Chief of Turning Pages, an independent bookstore, café, reading lounge, and co-working space in Jakkur, North Bengaluru. Driven by her deep love for books and reading communities, Vineetha established Turning Pages as a vibrant cultural space where literature, conversation, creativity, and collaboration come together. Through this unique initiative, she has created a welcoming environment for readers, writers, artists, and professionals to engage with books and ideas in meaningful ways. By blending entrepreneurship with her commitment to nurturing a reading culture, Vineetha Vijayakumar continues to play an important role in promoting independent bookstores and literary communities in Bengaluru.

Chandraiah Shivanna.b: Chandraiah Shivanna is a passionate educator and distinguished literary voice, currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Telugu at Nizam College, Osmania University, Hyderabad, Telangana. His commitment to the preservation and promotion of the Telugu language extends beyond national boundaries, as he facilitates Telugu Diploma programmes for students from various countries. He also contributes actively to academic discourse as a member of the Editorial Board of the journal Nadusthunna Telangana. An accomplished author and editor, Dr. Chandraiah's scholarly contributions include works such as Telangana Cultural Dictionary and Palukubadi, which offer valuable insights into the region's linguistic and cultural heritage. His creative expression is reflected in his poetry collections, including Edari Vasana. Since February 2025, he has been serving as the General Secretary of the Telugu Literary Congress, further strengthening his commitment to the advancement of Telugu literature and culture.

Mohan Talari.b: Mohan Talari is a Telugu writer, translator, and researcher whose work bridges literature, history, and social thought. He is the author of Hostel Life, Life @ Buttayagudem, and Mahad, a research-based work on the historic Mahad Satyagraha. His notable translations include Kulam: Puttuka–Nirmulana, Alexander Pushkin's Masha (The Captain's Daughter), and Naa Peru Bhagat Singh, the Telugu edition of Bhagat Singh's Jail Diary and selected writings. He is currently translating Iconoclast, Anand Teltumbde's acclaimed biography of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

Aparna Thota.b: Aparna Thota is a writer, gender trainer, and social worker whose work focuses on gender equality, inclusion, and social justice. A postgraduate in Social Work from Osmania University, she has collaborated with government institutions, non-profit organisations, and civil society groups on gender rights and education. She is the author of Poorna, the inspiring story of the world's youngest girl to summit Mount Everest, as well as Bold & Beautiful, a collection of short stories, and Jenny, a poetry collection. She has also edited the pioneering Telugu queer fiction anthologies Ade Prema and Love Infinite. Aparna currently serves as Program Manager at the Azim Premji Foundation, where she continues to work at the intersection of education, equity, and social change.

Akkalur Ravi.b: Akkalur Ravi is a Tamil translator, writer, and retired Accounts Officer from BSNL. A postgraduate in Commerce and an MBA graduate, he has been actively engaged in translation since 2008 and has translated 26 books from English into Tamil. His notable translations include Dreams from My Father, Gandhi and Bhagat Singh, The RTI Story, The Tales of Silk Roads, and Brief History of Equality. He received the Nalli ‘Thisaiyettum’ Best Translation Award (2018) for his Tamil translation of Sunil Khilnani’s The Idea of India. His creative work Kanavu Nagaram Kanchipuram presents the historic city through multiple cultural and social perspectives. A native of Akkalur near Mayiladuthurai, he currently resides in Chennai. M.Com., MBA., Retired Accounts Officer, BSNL, active translator since 2008, 26 English-to-Tamil translations, Nalli ‘Thisaiyettum’ Best Translation Award 2018. Native: Akkalur near Mayiladuthurai; currently residing in Chennai. Creative work: Kanavu Nagaram Kanchipuram.

K. Mohanarangan.b: K. Mohanarangan (b. 1967) is a Tamil poet, translator, essayist, and educator, serving as a vocational education teacher in a Government Higher Secondary School. He has published 6 poetry collections, 2 essay collections, 1 short story collection, 1 translated short story collection, and 8 translated poetry collections. His works have been published by Tamilini and Noolvanam Publications. A recipient of several prestigious honours, including the Coimbatore Devamagal Trust Award, Atmanam Trust Award, Jayakanthan Award, and the P.S. Kuppusamy Lifetime Contribution Award, Mohanarangan is known for his significant contributions to contemporary Tamil literature.

R. Kamarasu.b: R. Kamarasu is a renowned Tamil writer, literary critic, folklorist, and academic whose work has significantly enriched Tamil literary and folklore studies. The author of 47 books spanning poetry, literary criticism, folklore, and research, he has also published more than 260 scholarly articles. Currently serving as Professor and Head of the Department of Folklore at Tamil University, Thanjavur, he has guided numerous doctoral and M.Phil. scholars and has held distinguished academic positions, including National Committee Member of the Sahitya Akademi and Dean of the Faculty of Language at Tamil University. His contributions have been recognized with several honours, including the Tamil Nadu Government Literary Mamani Award (2024) and the Sengamalathayar Literary Award (2025).

A. Kalaiyarasi.b: A. Kalaiyarasi is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Folklore and Culture Studies, School of Performing Arts, Madurai Kamaraj University, Madurai. A distinguished academic and researcher, her areas of expertise include Cultural Anthropology, Cultural Identity, Postcolonialism, Feminism, and Cultural Ecology. She has authored three books, edited three volumes, published 36 research articles, and delivered over 40 invited lectures at national and international academic forums.

T. Sivakumar.b: T. Sivakumar is a literary critic, translator, media and communication expert, and master trainer from Puducherry. He served for 33 years in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting as an Indian Information Service Officer and retired as Deputy Director and Head of News, All India Radio, Puducherry. He has authored the books Body as Screen (Udale Thiraiyaga) and Social Communication (Samugath Thodarpiyal), and has published nearly 50 articles in leading Tamil literary magazines. A regular speaker at national seminars, he has conducted workshops on media literacy, literary criticism, film studies, translation, journalism, and gender equality. His areas of interest include visual communication, photography, feminism, and Siddha medicine

Surabhi Shastry.b: Surabhi Shastry is a seasoned marketing and communications leader, brand strategist, storyteller, and exceptional conversationalist, known for fostering insightful and engaging dialogues. With extensive experience in shaping global brands across technology, business, and innovation, she currently serves as Director of Marketing at EvoluteIQ, where she leads strategic initiatives that connect enterprise with purpose. Passionate about leadership, culture, and the transformative power of ideas, Surabhi brings together business acumen and thoughtful storytelling to create meaningful conversations. Her warmth, curiosity, and nuanced moderation style have made her a sought-after host for discussions with leaders across diverse fields. Drawing on her expertise in business storytelling and engaging dialogue, Surabhi will guide a conversation on entrepreneurship, civilizational values, resilience, and the enduring spirit of the Himalayas.

N. Sriram.b: N. Sriram (born 7 August 1972) is a Tamil writer and journalist from Nallimadam, Dharapuram Taluk, Tiruppur district. He has published six short story collections, two novels, and several other literary works. His contributions to Tamil literature have earned him numerous prestigious honours, including the Uyirmai–Sujatha Award, Pudhumaipithan Award, Ilakkiyaveedhi Annam Award, and the Thanjai Prakash Literary Award (2024). He also received the Muthamizh Arignar Kalaignar M. Karunanidhi Porkizhi Award (2025), the Padaipookku Award (2025) presented by SRV School, Tiruchirappalli, and the Ku. Alagirisamy Memorial Award (2026) presented by the Manalveedu Kalari Foundation. He currently resides in Chennai with his wife, Radha, and son, Abhishek Kumar.

Sushil Kumar.b: Sushil Kumar (born January 11, 1984) is a Tamil writer and translator from Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu. His works explore themes of ordinary lives, human beliefs, myths, history, and education. He has published four acclaimed short story collections—Moongil, Sapthaavarnam, Adiyanthiram, and Kannigai—as well as the novel Suntharavanam. As a translator, he has brought important international works into Tamil, including Therukkale Pallikkoodam (translated from Rahul Alvaris' Free from School) and Kanavup Porveeran, a collection of stories by renowned writers such as Anton Chekhov, Guy de Maupassant, Kobo Abe, Raymond Carver, and Isaac Bashevis Singer. In 2021, he received the Best Story Award in the Ka.Naa.Su Memorial Short Story Competition.

Anandh Kumar.b: Anand Kumar (born 22 March 1984) is a contemporary Tamil poet, documentary filmmaker, and photographer based in Coimbatore. A Computer Science graduate, he began his career as a software engineer before moving into education, where he currently works in curriculum development and teaching. Writing seriously since 2020, Anand Kumar made his literary debut with the poem Kutti Veedu in Solvanam magazine. His poetry, known for its simplicity and philosophical depth, explores themes of memory, relationships, solitude, and everyday life. His debut collection, Tip Tip Tip (2021), received the Vishnupuram–Kumaragurubaran Award in 2022, followed by Plum Cake (2025). He has also directed acclaimed documentaries on Tamil writers, including Veedum Veethigalum on poet Vikramadityan and Suzharpaathai Yaathreegan on writer Yuvan Chandrasekar, while actively pursuing photography alongside his literary work.

Mani Maaran.b: Mani Maaran is a renowned Tamil scholar, manuscriptologist, researcher, and author. He serves as Tamil Pandit at the Sarasvati Mahal Library, Thanjavur. He has authored and edited over 40 books on Tamil literature, history, archaeology, and palm-leaf manuscripts. A recipient of several prestigious honours, including the Kalanidhi Award, U.Ve.Sa. Award, and Pathippuchemmal Award, he is also the Founder and President of Yedagam, an institution dedicated to preserving and promoting Tamil language, culture, and heritage.

Vijayanandalakshmi.b: Vijayanandalakshmi is a Tamil writer, poet, essayist, and translator from Chinnamanur in Theni district, Tamil Nadu. She has authored two poetry collections—Udanpattu Veyil and Nizhal Mayakkam—the essay collection Theni: Magarantha Karuvoolam Thedi, the short story collection Mazhaimugam, and several books introducing Sangam classics, including Kalithogai, Malaipadukadam, Pattinappalai, and Kurinjipattu. She has also translated notable works such as Lisa Allathu Prabukkal Illam and O. Henry Sirukathaigal. Through her diverse writings, she has made significant contributions to contemporary Tamil literature and the popularization of Sangam literary heritage.

Rathna Venkat.b: Rathna Venkat is a Tamil poet based in Bengaluru, originally from Pudukkottai, Tamil Nadu. Having lived in New Jersey, New Delhi, and Mumbai, she brings diverse cultural experiences to her writing. She holds an M.Com. and a B.Ed., and writes under the pen name Rathna Venkat, drawing deep inspiration from the richness of Classical Tamil Sangam literature. Her published works include Mullai Muruval, Kaalaatheethathin Suzhal (winner of the Padithurai Trust Best Poetry Collection Award), Meechiru Varamena.., the bilingual Kintsugi (translated into English by N. Srivatsa), Maatralor, Mella Chidharu.., and her latest collection Isali@Dunbar_151 (2026). Through her poetry, Rathna Venkat blends classical aesthetics with contemporary sensibilities, establishing herself as a distinctive voice in modern Tamil literature.

Yuvan Chandrasekaran.b: R. Chandrasekaran, b. 27 June 1961) is one of the most distinguished voices in contemporary Tamil literature. Writing under the pen name Em. Yuvan for poetry and Yuvan Chandrasekar for fiction and other works, he has authored an extensive body of work spanning poetry, novels, short stories, flash fiction, essays, and translations. His acclaimed novels include Kaanal Nadhi, Payanakkathai, Vethaalam Sonna Kathai, Enkona Manithan, Ethirkkarai, and Aaru Tharagaikal. His poetry has been translated into several Indian languages, while his novel Kaanal Nadhi was published in English as Illusory River. An accomplished translator, he has also translated major international literary works into Tamil. His literary achievements have been recognised with the Canada Ilakkiya Thottam Award (2011), SPARROW Literary Award (2019), Vishnupuram Literary Award (2023), Iyal Award (2024), and the Kannadasan Award (2026). He currently resides in Chennai and is working on a new novel

Mahantesh Biradar.b: Mahantesh Biradar is a distinguished physician, journalist, and public relations professional whose multifaceted career reflects a unique blend of medical expertise, media engagement, and public communication. Through his work across diverse fields, he has earned recognition as a versatile and committed professional. Alongside his medical practice, Dr. Biradar has made significant contributions to journalism and public relations, using his communication skills to bridge the gap between institutions and society. His writings and public engagements reflect a deep concern for social issues, public awareness, and community well-being.

Benyamin.b: Benyamin is one of the most celebrated contemporary Malayalam authors, renowned for his powerful storytelling and profound exploration of migration, identity, and human resilience. Hailing from Pathanamthitta district in Kerala, he has established himself as a leading voice in Indian literature through his acclaimed novels and short stories. His landmark novel Aadujeevitham (Goat Days) has received widespread national and international recognition, winning prestigious honours including the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award and the Abu Dhabi Sakthi Award. The novel has been translated into several languages, including English, Arabic, Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, and Odia, and has earned global acclaim through its inclusion in the Man Asian Literary Prize Longlist and the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature Shortlist. Benyamin’s other notable works include Manjaveyil Maranangal, Mullappoo Niramulla Pakalukal (Jasmine Days), and Manthalirile 20 Communist Varshangal, which have also received major literary honours such as the JCB Prize for Literature, Crossword Book Award, and Vayalar Award. Through his evocative narratives and literary excellence, Benyamin continues to be one of the most influential voices in contemporary Indian literature.

P. V. Shaji Kumar.b: P. V. Shaji Kumar is a noted writer and screenwriter associated with the Kochi unit of Mathrubhumi. He has penned the screenplays for acclaimed films such as Take Off, Kanyaka Talkies, and Teacher. Some of his major literary works include Janam, Vellarippadam, Kalichampothiyilekku Oru Half-Ticket, and Maranavamsham. His contributions have earned him numerous honors, including the New York Film Festival Award, the Kendra Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar, the Shanghai Film Festival Award, and the Vayalar Award, among others.

Sandhya Hegde Doddahonda.b: Sandhya Hegde Doddahonda is a distinguished Kannada author, researcher, and academic, widely recognized for her significant contributions to Kannada literary studies and criticism. She serves as the Head of the Department of Kannada at NMKRV Degree College, Bengaluru , where she has been actively engaged in teaching, research, and mentoring students. Dr. Hegde Doddahonda has undertaken extensive research in Kannada literature, with her scholarly work focusing on Shankar Mokashi Punekar’s Gangavva Gangamayi and the broader field of Modern Kannada Literary Criticism: Poetry , for which she was awarded a Ph.D. Through her writings, research, and academic leadership, she continues to enrich contemporary Kannada literary discourse and inspire students, scholars, and readers with her deep commitment to literature and education.

Maya B. Nair.b: Maya B. Nair is a Kannada writer, translator, and retired Karnataka Government officer based in Bengaluru. Holding postgraduate degrees in Sociology, Public Administration, and Rural Development, she has served in several key administrative positions, including Personal Secretary to the Deputy Chief Minister's Secretariat and the RDPR Department, Karnataka Government. She is the author of the Kannada short story collection Ankura and has translated numerous acclaimed Malayalam literary works into Kannada, fostering literary exchange between the two languages. She has also worked as an anchor for the "Karnataka Vahini" programme on Chandana Doordarshan. Her contributions to literature have been recognised with the Change Makers Award 2025 by Suvarna Karnataka Kerala Samajam and the Sneha Rathna Award by Athmashree Kannada Saamskruthika Prathishtana.

Jacob Abraham.b: Jacob Abraham is an accomplished short story writer, novelist, translator and radio professional from Kerala. His literature explores complexities of ordinary human beings. His stories have garnered significant recognition including the Kerala Sahitya Academy Geethahirnayan Award and Kerala Bhasha Institute Karoor Prize and the Mathrubhumi Weekly Short Story prize. His notable books include Vangoginte Kamuki, Kumari, Mindamadam etc. He authored 20 books in different categories. His stories has translated into Hindi, Kannada and English.

Briji K. T.b: Briji K .T is a bilingual writer and artist from Kerala, educated in Chandigarh and Jamnagar, and currently settled in Bangalore. She has authored books in Malayalam and English, published by reputed publishers such as Poornna publishers, Saikatham publishers, Buddha books, Red Cherry books, and the Kerala Gov. Institute for Children's Literature. Briji has won several awards for her writing, including the 'Women Achievers Award' in 2020, 'ONV Puraskaram' by Malayala Bhasha Institute, Santhakumaran Thampi Award, and 'OV Vijayan Smaraka Puraskaram'. She has also conducted several painting exhibitions and is recognized for her poetry, which brings forth the nuances of life.

M.P Lipin Raj.b: M.P Lipin Raj is a Civil Servant and writer who passed the All India Civil Services Examination in 2012. He is a novelist, columnist and short story writer. He is the brand ambassador of the NGO – Walk with a Civil Servant, a free civil service training project. Lipin Raj received UNICEF’s Youth Leadership Award in 2009. His first short story collection is titled Golden Frog. His prominent works include A Phoenix with Broken Wings, Mapini, Aanayum Puliyumillatha Kadha, Elimination Round, Padam Onnu: Athmavishwasam, Thenurumbine Theneechayakkam, Marangal Odunna Vazhiye and latest novel Margareeta. He received the prestigious Padmarajan Award in 2024 as well as the Nooranad Haneef Award 2024.

Sandhya . E.b: Sandhya. E is an accomplished Malayalam writer, poet, researcher, and academic based in Thrissur, Kerala. She serves as an Associate Professor at Prajyoti Niketan College, Pudukad, and has made significant contributions to both literature and education through her scholarly and creative pursuits. A researcher in Statistics, Sandhya has been recognized as a distinguished educator and scientist, receiving honours including the National Award for Best Young Scientist and the Gani Award for Best Teachers from the University of Calicut. Alongside her academic achievements, she has established herself as a prominent literary voice in contemporary Malayalam literature.   Her published short story collection, Padikal Kayarunna Penkutti, has earned critical acclaim, and her stories and poems have appeared in leading Malayalam literary magazines and periodicals. She has received numerous prestigious literary awards, including the Puzha.com Award, Thakazhi Sahithyam Award, Kamalasurayya Award, and the Rashtrakavi Sri Govinda Pai Award for poetry. Through her writing, teaching, and research, Sandhya E. continues to enrich Malayalam literature with her distinctive creative and intellectual contributions.

P. Raman.b: P. Raman is one of the most prominent post-modern poets in Malayalam. His poetry collection Kanam received the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Kanakasree Endowment Award, and Rathri Pantrandarakku Oru Tharattu won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award in 2019. Kavinizhalmala, Thurumbu, Bhashayum Kunjum, and Pinnilekk Veeshunna Kattu are among his other significant works.

Sajay K. V.b: Sajay K. V. is one of the eminent literary critics of contemporary Malayalam literature, renowned for his insightful analyses and profound engagement with modern literary and cultural discourse. Through his critical writings, he has established himself as a significant voice in shaping contemporary literary thought and interpretation.   His major works include Adakkavum Anakkavum, Latin Americayude Kavitha, and Nilaavu Moshtikkunna Kallan, among several other acclaimed publications. Sajay K. V.'s scholarship reflects a deep understanding of literature, poetry, translation, and cultural studies, earning him recognition as one of the leading critics of his generation.   Through his writings and critical engagement, he continues to contribute meaningfully to the advancement of Malayalam literary criticism and contemporary intellectual discourse.

Rahul Radhakrishnan.b: Rahul Radhakrishnan is a notable Malayalam writer who has contributed articles to leading journals. He is the recipient of the prestigious M. Achyuthan Award instituted by the Kerala Sahitya Akademi for his well-acclaimed debut work, Uyirbhoopadangal.

Arshad Bathery.b: Arshad Bathery is an acclaimed Malayalam author, screenwriter, and filmmaker, widely recognized for his compelling storytelling and significant contributions to contemporary Malayalam literature and cinema. His works, known for their emotional depth and social insight, have earned him a distinguished place among the leading literary voices of his generation. His acclaimed writings have received several prestigious honours, including the Swami Vivekananda Yuva Prathibha Award, Mundur Krishnankutty Story Award, Atlas Kairali Story Award, and the Abu Dhabi Sakthi Award. His stories have been translated into Tamil, Kannada, English, German, and Hindi, reflecting their wide literary appeal. Arshad Bathery's notable works include Churam Kayarukayanu Irangukayanu and Meenukalude Aakashavum Paravakalude Bhoomiyum. He has also made significant contributions to cinema by directing the documentary God the Man and writing the screenplay and dialogues for the feature film Chakkaramavin Kombathu. Through his literary and cinematic pursuits, he continues to enrich contemporary Malayalam culture with his distinctive creative voice.

Aash Ashitha.b: Aash Ashitha is a Malayalam author, journalist, and literary translator known for her contemporary fiction, poetry, and translations. Currently serving as Deputy News Editor at The Times of India , Bengaluru, she has authored acclaimed works including Mungamkuzhi , Jenniferum Poochakannukalum , and Mushroom Cats . Her Malayalam translation of Vasudhendra's Mohanaswamy has been widely appreciated, and her writings have been translated into English and German.

Indira Balan.b: Indira Balan is a distinguished Malayalam author, poet, essayist, biographer, and cultural leader based in Bengaluru. She is the daughter of the legendary Kathakali maestro and teacher Vazhenkada Kunju Nair and Lakshmikutty Amma, a recipient of the prestigious Padma Shri award.   Holding a Master's degree in Malayalam, she has authored more than twelve books spanning poetry, short stories, essays, and biographies. Her literary and cultural contributions extend beyond writing, having served as the founding President of Bengaluru Sargadhara, former President of the Writers and Artists Forum, and Chief Editor of Sarthakam News. She has also been a columnist for Kerala Bhushanam daily. A prominent advocate for women's creative and cultural empowerment, she serves as Chairperson of Dhvani, a women's platform, and has held key leadership roles in several literary and cultural organizations. Her works have received numerous literary awards, and she has twice represented Malayalam at the Akhila Bharatha Sahitya Parishad. Through her writing and cultural leadership, she continues to make a lasting contribution to Malayalam literature and the literary life of Karnataka.

K.R. Kishor.b: K. R. Kishor is a Malayalam writer, literary critic, biographer, editor, and theatre practitioner based in Bengaluru. His writings span fiction, literary criticism, biographies, and social thought, with a strong focus on the lives and ideas of influential public figures, including Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Sree Narayana Guru, and journalist Gauri Lankesh. He has also been an active contributor to Malayalam literary journals and magazines for several decades. A committed literary and cultural organizer, Kishor has founded and edited several Malayalam magazines and has played a significant role in promoting literary and cultural activities in Bengaluru through seminars, workshops, and public discussions. His contributions extend to theatre as a playwright, director, actor, and mentor, with decades of involvement in Malayalam drama across Karnataka and Kerala. Through his writing, editorial work, and theatre practice, K. R. Kishor continues to enrich Malayalam literature and foster meaningful literary and cultural dialogue.

M. K. Harikumar.b: M. K. Harikumar is a distinguished Indian literary critic, columnist, journalist, poet, novelist, philosopher, theorist, short story writer, and orator. Renowned for his multifaceted contributions to literature and public discourse, he has established himself as one of the most versatile intellectual voices in contemporary Malayalam literature.   Through his writings across diverse genres, Harikumar has explored literature, philosophy, culture, and society with remarkable depth and originality. His work as a critic, essayist, and public speaker continues to inspire readers and audiences, enriching contemporary literary and cultural conversations with his incisive insights and thought-provoking perspectives.

Rema Pisharody.b: Rema Pisharody is a bilingual poet based in Bangalore, writing in both Malayalam and English. She has authored 11 poetry collections in Malayalam and has also contributed poems to several English-language anthologies. Additionally, the Balasahithya Institute has published her children's novel, Ammuvinte Bhumi.

Santhosh Echikkanam.b: Santhosh Echikkanam is a prominent Indian writer and screenwriter in Malayalam cinema. He is best known for his short stories Komala and Biriyani, and for writing the screenplays of films such as Annayum Rasoolum and Bachelor Party. He has worked as a teacher at Durga Higher Secondary School, Kanhangad, and was also associated with Akashvani. He has received several literary honors, including the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Story, the Padmaprabha Literary Award, the Karur Award, and the Pravasi Basheer Award, among others.

Soman Katalur.b: Soman Katalur is a distinguished scholar, poet, writer and illustrator. He completed his Postgraduate degree in Malayalam language and literature from Govt. Brennan College. He did his postgraduate degree in folklore from Calicut University with first rank. PhD in the subject of sketching and literary appreciation from Sree Shankaracharya Sanskrit University. Authored about twenty-five works. His works include Kanimeen, Puliyan, Nashtappadukal, Enik Nee Marikunnilalo, etc. He received about seven awards, including the Kerala Folklore Academy Award. Currently, he is a Malayalam teacher in the Plus Two section of JNM Government Higher Secondary School in Puthuppanam, Vadakara.

Sonia Cherian.b: Sonia Cherian (Lt. Colonel, Dr.) is a Malayalam writer and retired Indian Army officer, born to P.J. Cherian and M.K. Thresyamma in Perambra, Kannur district, and studied at Vekalam UP School, Santhom High School, and St. Teresa's, Ernakulam. She served as an army doctor and is best known for her memoir Indian Rainbow (2019), a work notable for being among the first military memoirs by a woman in Malayalam, blending the feel of an adventure story with lyrical prose, which has been widely praised and well-received by readers.

T.P. Vinod.b: T.P. Vinod is a Malayalam poet native to Koyyam in Kannur district, Kerala, who works as an Associate Professor of Chemistry at Christ University, Bengaluru. He has published five poetry collections: "Nilaviliyekkuruthulla Kadamkathakal," "Allathenth?," "Sandehangalude Nirdheshangangal," "Gharillaswabhavamulla Oru Khedam," and "Sathyamayum Lokame." His collection "Allathenth?" won the BCV Kavitha Puraskaram, while "Sathyamayum Lokame" earned him multiple honours, including the Mootadi Damodaran Award, the WTP Live Award, the Poorna-R. Ramachandran Award, the Sachi Memorial Award, and — most recently — the prestigious Ayanam–A. Ayyappan Poetry Award (the 13th edition), instituted by Ayanam Cultural Forum, Thrissur, in memory of poet A. Ayyappan.

Prakash Bare.b: Prakash Bare is an Indian theatre and film actor who works in Malayalam, English, and other South Indian language productions, and who also has a parallel career as a technologist and entrepreneur. Born and raised in Kasaragod district, Kerala (grew up in Chirakkal, Kannur district), he completed his B.Tech in Electrical Engineering from NSS College of Engineering, Palakkad, followed by a master's degree in Microelectronics from IIT Kanpur, after which he spent about fifteen years in Silicon Valley, California, working as a technologist and entrepreneur in chip design, including co-founding GDA Technologies Inc. He made his acting debut with the 2010 Malayalam film "Sufi Paranja Katha" and has since appeared in more than 30 films, becoming known for socially relevant, critically acclaimed art-house cinema; he is particularly noted for playing the poet KP Madhavan Nair (based on Mahakavi P. Kunhiraman Nair) in "Ivan Megharoopan," as well as for his roles in "Oraalppokkam" and "Papilio Buddha." Beyond acting, he is a producer under the Silicon Media banner, co-founded the Blue Ocean Theater group, and is a social activist involved with the Endosulfan victims' struggle in Kasaragod as president of the CERV Collectives.

E Santhosh Kumar.b: E Santhosh Kumar has published more than twenty-five books in Malayalam, including novels, short story collections, children’s literature, travelogues and essays. He won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award twice, in 2006 for his short story collection Chavukali, translated by P N Venugopal as A Fistful of Mustard Seeds, Niyogi Books, 2019, and in 2012 for his novel Andhakaranazhi, Mathrubhumi Books, 2011, translated by P N Venugopal as Island of Lost Shadows, Niyogi Books, 2015. He also won Kerala State Children’s Institute award in 2010 and was a special jury mention in the State Film award, 2018. His novel, in English translation, was short listed for Crossword translation award in 2016. Two of his stories have been made into feature films. His works have been translated into English, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Gujarati, German and Bengali.

Anisha Sheth.b: Anisha Sheth is a Bengaluru-based journalist with over 16 years of experience in reporting, editing and teaching. She started her career as a reporter with The Hindu in Mangalore, worked as an editor with The New Indian Express and had a stint at Reuters. She is currently Bureau Head, Karnataka, at The News minute where her reportage focuses on caste, communalism, human rights, and law. She also has an interest in culture, education, labour and health

Lakshmi Narasaiah Guntur.b: Lakshmi Narasaiah Guntur (born 15 June 1961) is a Telugu poet, literary critic, editor, and retired lecturer in English from Andhra Pradesh. A prominent voice in Telugu Dalit literature, he has made significant contributions through poetry, literary criticism, and the editing of landmark Dalit poetry anthologies such as Chikkanavutunna Pata and Padunekkina Pata.   He has authored several acclaimed books, including Dalitha Sahityam – Tatvika Drukpadham, The Essence of Dalit Poetry, Kavitva Nirmana Paddhatulu, Samajika Kala Vimarsha, and Kavitvam – Charchaneeyamshaalu. His work has been recognised with the Andhra Pradesh State Award, two Telugu University Awards, the Mahakavi Gurram Jashuva Award, and several other literary honours. His book Kavitvam – Charchaneeyamshaalu was shortlisted for the Sahitya Akademi Award for two consecutive years.

Prasad Suri.b: Prasad Suri (pen name of Surada Prasad) is a Telugu author, painter, and researcher from Vada Narsapuram village in Andhra Pradesh's Anakapalli district. A graduate in Painting (BFA) from JNAFAU, Hyderabad, he is currently pursuing an M.A. in Archaeology at Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU), Baroda.   He is the author of My Name is Chiranjeevi (2021), Mairavana (2022)—widely recognized as the first authentic Telugu novel on the lives of fishermen—Artist Mohan (2023), an English monograph, and Bachelor of Fine Arts (2024), the first Telugu novel portraying the lives of fine arts students. His work has received wide acclaim, earning the Anvikshiki Publications Ugadi Award (2025) for Bachelor of Fine Arts and the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar (2025) for Mairavana.

Kandarathithan.b: Kandarathithan is a distinguished contemporary Tamil poet and writer, regarded as one of the leading voices in post-1990s Tamil poetry. His work is noted for its unique blend of modern poetic expression with classical Tamil traditions, mythology, and devotional heritage. He is the author of four acclaimed poetry collections—Kandarathithan Kavithaigal (2001), Seethamandalam (2007), Thiruchazhal (2014), and Paadi Koodaram (2023)—and has also edited an anthology on 1990s Tamil poetry. His fifth poetry collection, Erranna Kalavandhulu Thulyabhaga, is currently in print . His literary contributions have earned him several prestigious honours, including the Ananda Vikatan Award (2008, 2016), the Kumaragurubaran–Vishnupuram Award (2018), the Ezhuthukalam Award (2021), and the Vasagasalai Award (2023).

B. Tirusenthalai.b: B. Tirusenthalai (born 1981) is a Tamil poet and short story writer based in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. He began his literary career in 2006 and has since published three short story collections—Veyil Nanban, Vilaasam, and Nerupil Valarpavai—along with the poetry collection Sketches – Sorchithirangal. Known for his lyrical prose and sensitive portrayal of human emotions, his stories often explore the lives of entrepreneurs and traders against the backdrop of Madurai and southern Tamil Nadu. His works have been translated into English and Malayalam, with some included in college curricula. He has received literary honours from organisations such as Puthiya Thalaimurai and SRV, and has participated in literary festivals including the Vishnupuram American Lit Fest.

Samyuktha Maya.b: Samyuktha Maya is a Tamil poet, translator, and banking professional from Theni district, Tamil Nadu. She holds a bachelor's degree in Agricultural Sciences and a postgraduate degree in Environmental Sciences, and is currently based in Chennai. She made her literary debut with the poetry collection Dalhousieyin Orange Iravu (The Orange Night of Dalhousie) in 2016, followed by Thee Nindra Paadham (Feet of Flames) in 2023. In recognition of her poetic achievements, She has been awarded the Thamizhan Award for 'Promising Star - Literature' 2026 by New Generation Media (Puthiya Thalaimurai TV) Her poems have been translated into Telugu, and she continues to contribute to contemporary Tamil literature through poetry and translation while pursuing her career in banking.

K. P. Ramanunni.b: K. P. Ramanunni is an acclaimed Malayalam author, editor, and cultural administrator whose contributions have significantly enriched contemporary Indian literature. Renowned for his evocative storytelling and profound exploration of social, cultural, and spiritual themes, he has established himself as one of the most respected voices in Malayalam literature.   He has served as the Editor of Madhyamam Weekly and as the Administrator of the Thunchan Memorial Trust, playing an important role in literary and cultural initiatives in Kerala. A prolific writer, Ramanunni has authored numerous short story collections, novels, and essay collections that have earned widespread critical acclaim. His outstanding literary contributions have been recognized with several prestigious honours, including the Samastha Kerala Sahitya Parishad Award, Edasseri Award, Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award, and the Vayalar Award. His celebrated novel Sufi Paranja Katha has been translated into multiple languages and adapted into a feature film, further extending the reach of his literary work.

N. Ramachandran.b: N. Ramachandran is an eminent Tamil folklorist, literary scholar, researcher, and author with over three decades of distinguished contributions to folklore studies and Tamil literature. Holding a Ph.D. in Folklore, he served as Associate Professor and Head of the P.G. & Research Department of Folklore at St. Xavier's College, Palayamkottai, and later as Director of the Folklore Resources and Research Centre (2014–2024).   Widely respected for his pioneering research in folk literature, folk performance, folk religion, and ethnography, has authored and edited several influential books, guided numerous doctoral scholars, published over 30 research papers, and presented more than 90 papers at national and international conferences. He has also led major research projects and served as editor of leading academic journals, making a lasting contribution to the preservation and advancement of Tamil folklore and cultural studies.

Prathibha Nandakumar.b: Prathibha Nandakumar is a distinguished bilingual poet, journalist, filmmaker, columnist, and translator from Bengaluru, Karnataka. Writing with equal distinction in Kannada and English, she is widely recognized as one of the leading contemporary literary voices in India.   Her creative work spans poetry, journalism, cinema, and translation, reflecting a deep engagement with literature, culture, and society. Through her evocative writing and multifaceted artistic pursuits, Prathibha Nandakumar has enriched both Kannada and English literary landscapes.   As a poet and public intellectual, she continues to inspire readers and audiences through her insightful reflections, artistic versatility, and enduring contribution to contemporary Indian literature and culture.

Dadapeer Jyman.b: Dadapeer Jyman is an award-winning Kannada poet, short story writer, translator, and activist from Hagaribommanahalli in Karnataka’s Vijayanagara district. He has emerged as a powerful and distinctive voice in contemporary Kannada literature, particularly through his contributions to resistance, protest, and queer writing.   Through his poetry, fiction, and translation work, Jayman engages with themes of identity, social justice, marginalization, and human dignity with remarkable sensitivity and literary force. His writings are celebrated for their bold expression, emotional depth, and commitment to amplifying underrepresented voices.   As a writer and activist, Dadapeer Jayman continues to enrich contemporary Kannada literature by fostering critical dialogue and expanding the horizons of literary and social discourse.

M. R. Kamala.b: M. R. Kamala is a celebrated contemporary Kannada poet, essayist, translator, and educator whose work has made a significant impact on modern Kannada literature. Renowned for her profound exploration of womanhood, identity, and social realities, she has emerged as one of the most influential literary voices in contemporary India.   A distinguished translator, M. R. Kamala has enriched Kannada literature by bringing the works of influential African, Arab, and African-American women writers to Kannada readers. Through her translations, she has fostered meaningful cross-cultural literary dialogue and expanded the horizons of Kannada readership.   Through her poetry, essays, translations, and academic engagement, M. R. Kamala continues to inspire readers and scholars alike, contributing richly to Kannada literature with her intellectual depth, artistic sensitivity, and commitment to social and literary discourse.

Saviraj Anandur.b: Saviraj Anandur is an emerging Kannada author, poet, theatre artist, and engineer, recognized for his creative contributions to contemporary Kannada literature and traditional performing arts. A graduate of Visvesvaraya Technological University, he has successfully balanced his technical background with a deep passion for literary expression and cultural heritage.   Writing predominantly in Kannada, Saviraj Anandur’s work reflects a thoughtful engagement with language, poetry, and storytelling. His artistic pursuits extend beyond literature into theatre, where he actively contributes to the preservation and promotion of traditional performing arts.   Through his multifaceted creative journey as a writer, poet, and theatre artist, Saviraj Anandur represents a new generation of Kannada literary voices that seamlessly bridges modern education, cultural tradition, and artistic innovation.

Nadeem Sanadi.b: Nadeem Sanadi is a well-known Kannada poet, author, and environmental professional based in Belagavi, Karnataka. Renowned for his distinctive literary voice, he has made significant contributions to contemporary Kannada poetry and prose through works that reflect social consciousness, human experience, and cultural sensitivity.   Alongside his literary pursuits, Nadeem Sanadi possesses specialized expertise in waste management engineering, successfully balancing a prominent creative career with a strong professional commitment to environmental sustainability. His unique combination of literary expression and technical knowledge enables him to engage with both cultural and ecological issues in meaningful ways.   Through his poetry, writings, and professional work, Nadeem Sanadi continues to inspire readers and communities, contributing to Kannada literature while advocating for a more sustainable and environmentally conscious society.

Nutan Doshetty.b: Nutan Doshetty is a distinguished Kannada writer and former radio programme executive, widely recognized as a prominent voice among contemporary Kannada women writers. Hailing from Siddapur in Uttara Kannada district, she has made valuable contributions to Kannada literature through her writing and to broadcasting through her work with All India Radio. Her literary works explore contemporary life and human experiences with sensitivity and insight. Through her distinctive voice and sustained engagement with literature and broadcasting, Nuthana M. Doshetty has enriched Karnataka's literary and cultural landscape.

Kavanamaali.b: Kavanamaali is a writer from Nagarkurnool, Telangana, and an IT professional with a Bachelor's degree in Engineering. His literary journey began with lyric writing for short and independent films before expanding into fiction and poetry.   A passionate reader with a personal library of over 8,000 books, his writing explores human emotions, relationships, identity, memory, and philosophical questions. He is the author of seven published works, including the short story collections Manasu Nesina Kathalu and Vaitarini Odduna; the poetry collections Aparajita and Garalakanthuni Gaanam Vinu; the novels Nrukesari and Neelakurinji; and the novella Narudi Brathuku Natana.

Kumaaran Nandan.b: Kumaaran Nandan is a Tamil writer of short stories and poetry. His published works include the poetry collection Pagal Kanavugalin Nadanam and the short story collections Pathimoonru Meengal, Boomiyengum Pooraniyin Nizhal, Nagarap Paadagan, Maha Maya, and Nigazhvugalai Maatri Amaippavan. In recognition of his significant contribution to the short story genre, he received the Pudhumaipithan Award presented by Vijaya Publications.

S. R. Sundaram (Kannan Sundaram).b: S. R. Sundaram (Kannan Sundaram) is a leading Tamil publisher, editor, writer, and cultural commentator. He is the Publisher of Kalachuvadu Publications and Editor of Kalachuvadu, the renowned Tamil monthly on culture and politics. A key figure in contemporary Tamil literature, he co-organised the landmark Tamil Ini 2000 international conference and has participated in several prestigious global publishing programmes. His essays have appeared in The Hindu, The Indian Express, Scroll.in, and Economic and Political Weekly. In 2024, the French Government conferred on him the prestigious Chevalier title in recognition of his outstanding contribution to literature and publishing.

Poovithal Umesh.b: Poovithal Umesh is a Tamil poet, writer, translator, and grammarian who writes in both Tamil and English. Born in Navalai village, Dharmapuri district, Tamil Nadu, his works are known for their lyrical style, emotional depth, and exploration of Tamil identity, ecology, political consciousness, and nostalgia. His poems have been translated into several languages, and he has authored seven poetry collections, more than ten children's books, and a widely acclaimed book on Tamil grammar. He has received numerous literary honours, including the Veral Poetry Award, Thinaigal Poetry Award, and Piramil Poetry Award (Sri Lanka), establishing him as a distinctive voice in contemporary Tamil literature.

Anees C.C.O.b: Anees C.C.O is a Malayalam literary critic, writer, public speaker, content creator, and cultural organiser based in Bengaluru. He has been actively engaged in literary criticism, creative writing, and literary initiatives, contributing to discussions on Malayalam literature, language, and contemporary society. Through literary events, public talks, and digital platforms, he promotes reading, meaningful dialogue, and a deeper appreciation of literature, culture, philosophy, and the arts.

S. Kandasubramaniam.b: S. Kandasubramaniam was born on 15 December 1977 in Uthukuli, Tamil Nadu. He completed his B.Sc. in Physics at PSG College of Arts & Science, Coimbatore (1994–1997) and pursued his Master's degree and research in Tamil Studies at Madurai Kamaraj University (1997–2003). Since June 2003, he has been serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Tamil at PSG College of Arts & Science, Coimbatore. His academic interests include Folklore, Translation Studies, and Social History. He has also worked as a theatre performer with Dr. M. Ramaswamy's Nijanadaga Theatre Movement, participating in three productions with 15 stage performances.

Muhammad Kuningad.b: Muhammad Kuningad is a Malayalam writer, thinker, and orator, actively contributing to contemporary Malayalam literature while also pursuing a successful career in business. He is a Partner at Shopwel Super Market and serves as the Vice President of the Bangalore Malayali Writers and Artists Forum. His published works include the short story collections Theruvil Kandath (2020) and God's Own Chunk (2025), the cultural criticism Vaividhyangalil Nirayunna Saundaryam (2023), and the literary anthology Vaikhari (2026), which he edited. He is also the editor of the forthcoming memoir Ormayil Thodunna Neram (2026).

Ramesh Kalyan.b: Ramesh Kalyan is a Tamil writer and avid literary reader whose passion for reading naturally evolved into writing. He has a keen interest in short stories, poetry, novels, drama, and painting. His short stories and poems have appeared in leading Tamil literary magazines, including Amudasurabhi, Dinamani Kathir, Kanaiyazhi, Thalam, Iruvaatchi, and Vaarthai. His award-winning short stories were published as a collection titled Thisaiyariyap Pul (2019) by Siruvani Publications. His works have also been featured in anthologies such as Ezhuthu (Zero Degree award-winning stories), Maasarupon, and Naan Yen Ezhuthukiren (Sandhya Publications), as well as in Nadagaveli. His literary essays and reading reflections have appeared in online magazines including Solvanam, Aavanazhi, Kanali, Pathagai, Vanam, Yaavarum, and Rasamattam. Holding a bachelor's degree in Physics and a qualification in Management, he works in Bengaluru in the print media advertising and sales sector, focusing on South India. He lives in Hosur with his wife and two children, who share his love for quality literature.

Chaitra Shivayogimath.b: Chaitra Shivayogimath, based in Bangalore and originally from Muddebihal in Vijayapura district, is an M.Tech graduate in Electronics and Telecommunication from Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU). She works as a Cyber Security Engineer in Bangalore. A passionate poet and translator, she published her debut Kannada poetry collection, Petrichor, in 2022. In 2025, she translated selected poems of Pulitzer Prize-winning American poet Mary Oliver into Kannada, published as Akasha Nadi Bayalu. Petrichor received widespread appreciation in Kannada literary circles for its fresh voice and earned several prestigious honours, including the Smt. Sharada Ramalingappa Datti Award from Kannada Sahitya Parishat, the Amma Prashasti (Sedam), the Prarthana Sahitya Prashasti (Manvi), and recognition in the Avva Pustakalaya Annual Awards. Deeply committed to literary translation, Chaitra is passionate about bringing poetry from other languages into Kannada. Her poems and translations have been published in several literary magazines.

Anupama K. Benachinamardi.b: Anupama K. Benachinamaradi hails from Benivada village in Belagavi district. A postgraduate in engineering, she is also a creative writer and columnist. She has authored 11 children’s books and is the founder of Awwa Pustaka, a publishing house dedicated to children’s books in Kannada and English. She is also the winner of 'Deccan Herald Changemeker 2026' by Deccan Herald media and winner of 'Women to Watch 2026' by PrintWeek media. Anupama has been a speaker and panelist at numerous literary festivals and events across India, addressing thousands of students both offline and online. A passionate nature lover, she spends her free time observing the world of birds and insects with children—answering their curious questions and cherishing every moment of wonder.

Abhijith A.P.C.b: Abhijith A.P.C. is a homoeopathic physician, organic farmer, naturalist, arachnologist, and science communicator based in Mysuru, Karnataka. He is a founding member of Team SAALIGA, a citizen science initiative dedicated to spider research, conservation, and public awareness. An accomplished researcher, he has documented spider behaviour extensively, co-discovered several new spider species, and co-authored over 50 scientific publications. He has also led exhibitions, workshops, and outreach programs promoting biodiversity and ecological awareness across Karnataka. Dr. Abhijith manages a biodiverse organic farm that nurtures more than 3,000 plant species, providing a thriving habitat for birds, reptiles, insects, and spiders. He is the author and co-author of books including Backyard Spiders – A Field Guide to Common Spiders, Ambaradoladuva Kichuganaguttu, and Halasu Bidisidaaga, and regularly writes nature columns in Kannada newspapers and digital platforms. His contributions to conservation and science communication have been recognized with the Deccan Herald "20 in 2020 – DH Changemakers" award, recognition from iNaturalist, and a TEDx talk in 2023.

Chandra Keerthi.b: Chandra Keerthi is a theatre practitioner, performative storyteller, educator, and teacher trainer with over 25 years of experience in the performing arts. He holds an M.Sc. in Electronic Media from Bangalore University. He has acted in 37 staged plays, conceptualised and performed over 10 stories for children, and appeared in more than 450 shows. His diverse practice includes acting, directing, storytelling, theatre education, facilitation, and teacher training. He is the Founder and Creative Director of Theatre Artistree, through which he has initiated innovative projects such as Theatre at Your Doorstep, RangaAkshara, and Kitchen Stories. He has also directed The Caucasian Chalk Circle, which was staged at META (Mahindra Excellence in Theatre Awards), New Delhi. A recipient of the GCU Puraskar 2024, Chandra continues to explore the possibilities of theatre and storytelling across performance, education, and community engagement.

Prabha S.b: Prabha S. is a distinguished library educator, children's literature advocate, and Chief Library Officer with the Department of School Education and Literacy, Government of Karnataka. Currently serving at DSERT and the State Educational Resource and Information Center (SERIC), she has played a pivotal role in strengthening school libraries and promoting reading culture across Karnataka. As a State Resource Person, she has trained educators in library development, classroom libraries, and the use of E-Granthalaya library management software. She has also presented research on the role of school libraries at the NCERT National Conference on School Libraries (NCSL 2025) and has led initiatives to transform school libraries into vibrant learning spaces. A passionate promoter of children's literature, Prabha is a picture book writer, storyteller, translator, and creator of a storytelling YouTube channel. Her work also includes editing a Kannada School Library Manual, contributing to digital educational resources, and championing community initiatives that promote literacy, sustainability, and lifelong learning.

Niharika.b: Niharika is a visual artist, art educator, and children's book illustrator whose work celebrates the beauty of everyday life. Inspired by mundane moments, waterscapes, trees, and the vibrant energy of places and people, she brings warmth, imagination, and subtle humour to her artistic practice. Known for her distinctive visual storytelling, Niharika's illustrations are infused with whimsy, absurdity, and dark humour, creating engaging experiences for readers of all ages. Through her work as an illustrator and educator, she continues to nurture creativity while inspiring young minds to see the extraordinary in the ordinary.

Vani Salimath.b: Vani Salimath is a Bengaluru-based artist and illustrator who studied at the Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath. Her creative practice spans illustration and handcrafted terracotta jewellery, reflecting her passion for art, craftsmanship, and design. Through her distinctive artistic expression, she blends traditional techniques with contemporary aesthetics, creating works that celebrate creativity and handmade artistry.

Madhuri Keta.b: Madhuri Keta is an entrepreneur, author, translator, and podcaster based in Bengaluru. She is the Founder and CEO of Lemon Yellow Crayon, a content agency. An agriculture science graduate with management education from IIM Ahmedabad, she has over 15 years of corporate experience. Her Telugu debut novel, Panakam On the Rocks (2024), a suspense thriller set in and around Bengaluru, received critical acclaim. She is currently translating an IAS officer's memoir from Telugu to English, based on his experiences in the tribal regions of Khammam district (present-day Telangana). Her short story also appears in the corporate-themed anthology Login Tales (2026). Beyond literature, Madhuri is a passionate advocate for women’s empowerment and child safety, and hosts a podcast dedicated to these important social issues.

Divya Kalavala.b: Divya Kalavala is an academic and literary translator. She was awarded the Charles Wallace India Trust Translation Fellowship for the year 2023–24 at the British Centre for Literary Translation at the University of East Anglia, UK. In the subsequent year, she was awarded the UEA Archives and Collections Visiting Fellowship (2024–25) at the Sainsbury Centre for Visual Arts for her project, ‘Mithila Art from India’.  She holds a doctoral degree in Film Studies from The English and Foreign Languages University and has been teaching at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Bengaluru. Divya translates from her mother tongue, Telugu, into English and is primarily interested in translating literary texts from the margins as a form of political solidarity.

Shilpa Kalyan.b: Shilpa Kalyan is an academic, media educator, and researcher, currently serving as the Head of the Department of Liberal Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences at MAHE Bengaluru . With over two decades of experience in Media and Mass Communication, she has played a pivotal role in establishing and strengthening media, humanities, and social sciences programmes at leading institutions. A recognized expert in media literacy, journalism, and communication studies, Dr. Kalyan is the South India Lead for the Global Journalism Trauma Literacy Project (JETREG) . She is a UNESCO Top Scholar Award recipient for her research on Trauma Literacy and has served as a trainer with the Google News Initiative India Training Network and BBC Young Reporter India , conducting workshops on media literacy, digital verification, and journalism for students and media professionals. Her research focuses on Trauma Literacy, Artificial Intelligence, and Communication Technologies , with publications in leading international journals. Through her academic leadership, research, and public engagement, Dr. Shilpa Kalyan continues to contribute significantly to media education and contemporary communication studies.

Iswarya. V.b: V. Iswarya is a freelance translator and critic based in Bengaluru.
