She teaches English literature at the Manipal Institute of Liberal Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, India. She has written essays on Tamil film culture for popular publications as part of her social media campaign Calling Out Stalking. She was a South Asia Speaks Fellow for Translation in 2024, working under the mentorship of Arunava Sinha. Her first book-length translation of a memoir by Perumal Murugan, Students Etched in Memory, was published by Penguin Random House India in 2025. Her own critical essays and her translations of Jeyamohan’s political essays have previously appeared in the Frontline magazine. Her latest translated book is Jeyamohan's One Million Footsteps (2026).

Natesh Hegde.b: Natesh Hegde is one of the most distinctive voices in contemporary Kannada cinema, celebrated for his deeply rooted, socially conscious, and visually evocative storytelling. Hailing from coastal Karnataka, he brings an intimate understanding of rural life, landscapes, and human relationships to the screen, crafting films that are both poetic and politically resonant. His critically acclaimed debut feature Pedro premiered at leading international film festivals and earned widespread recognition for its nuanced exploration of caste, faith, and identity. His latest feature, Vagachipani, continues his commitment to telling powerful stories that emerge from the margins, blending realism with striking cinematic language. Drawing inspiration from literature, folklore, and lived experiences, Hegde has established himself as an important filmmaker in India's independent cinema movement. His work reflects a rare balance of artistic excellence and social engagement, making him one of the most compelling directors shaping the future of Kannada cinema today.

Rasheed Kidwai.b: Rasheed Kidwai is a distinguished Indian journalist, author, and political analyst, widely recognized for his incisive commentary on Indian politics, governance, and public affairs. A Visiting Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) , he has established himself as a respected voice in political journalism and contemporary public discourse. With extensive experience covering the Indian government, political parties, community affairs, and Hindi cinema, Kidwai is a frequent commentator on leading news platforms, including News18, Times Now, ABP News, and NDTV . Through his books, journalism, and media appearances, he continues to offer insightful perspectives on India's evolving political and social landscape.

G.B. Vinay Kumar.b: G.B. Vinay Kumar is the Founder and Director of Insights IAS, one of India's most influential civil services mentoring institutions, renowned for transforming the landscape of UPSC preparation through innovation, mentorship, and a student-centric approach. A graduate in Genetics, he began his career as a Panchayat Development Officer before pursuing his vision of democratizing quality guidance for civil services aspirants. Under his leadership, InsightsIAS has mentored thousands of successful IAS, IPS, and other civil servants while reaching millions of learners across India through pioneering initiatives in answer writing, ethics, essay preparation, and personality development. Beyond education, Vinay Kumar has emerged as an active voice in public life, bringing his experience in governance, youth empowerment, and policy discourse into politics. His journey reflects a deep commitment to leadership, public service, and nation-building, making him a compelling participant in conversations on democracy, governance, education, and India's evolving political landscape.

Krishanu Kundu.b: Krishanu Kundu is a contemporary Bengali author known for his compelling horror and horror-fantasy fiction. Blending supernatural narratives with real-life historical events, his works explore pressing social issues such as corruption, acid attacks, and human trafficking, using popular fiction as a powerful medium for awareness and reflection. After a successful two-decade career in Human Resources with global banking institutions, Krishanu turned to full-time writing, pursuing a lifelong passion for Bengali literature. His novels have consistently featured among publisher bestseller lists, earning him recognition as an emerging voice in the genre. Influenced by literary greats such as Rabindranath Tagore, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, Sunil Gangopadhyay, and Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay, Krishanu Kundu continues to captivate readers with stories that combine suspense, folklore, history, and social commentary.

Kanishka Gupta.b: Kanishka Gupta is one of South Asia’s most influential literary agents and a leading voice in contemporary publishing. As the founder of Writer’s Side, he has transformed the literary landscape by building the region’s largest literary agency, representing over a thousand authors, translators, journalists, artists, and public intellectuals across genres. For more than a decade, he has championed path-breaking books, debut writers, and globally acclaimed voices, helping shape the journeys of works that have gone on to receive prestigious honours, including the International Booker Prize and the Booker Prize shortlist. A writer and publishing commentator himself, Gupta is widely respected for his sharp insights into the evolving world of books, rights, and readership. His work has expanded opportunities for South Asian authors on the global stage while strengthening the publishing ecosystem at home. At #BBLF-2026, he brings a rare insider’s perspective on discovering talent, building literary careers, and the future of publishing in India and beyond.

Mehdi Khawaja.b: Mehdi Khawaja is a distinguished writer, translator, and editor whose work has significantly enriched the landscape of South Asian literature in English. Renowned for bringing contemporary Kashmiri writing to a wider global audience, he has earned recognition for translations that combine literary sensitivity with linguistic precision. He is the recipient of the prestigious Armory Square Prize for South Asian Literature in Translation and the English PEN Presents x SALT award, honours that celebrate exceptional emerging translators. His English translation of Akhtar Mohiuddin’s acclaimed Kashmiri novel To Each Their Own Hell introduces one of Kashmir’s most important literary voices to international readers. Khawaja’s writings and translations have appeared in leading literary journals and anthologies, reflecting his deep engagement with language, identity, memory, and place. At #BBLF-2026, he brings valuable perspectives on literary translation as a creative act, the richness of Kashmiri literature, and the power of translation in fostering dialogue across cultures and languages.

Rajalakshmi N.K..b: Rajalakshmi N.K. is a distinguished English academic, translator, and literary scholar whose work has significantly enriched the dialogue between Kannada and English literature. An Associate Professor of English at University College, Mangaluru, she has devoted decades to teaching, research, and mentoring students while championing the art of translation. Her scholarship reflects a deep engagement with Indian writing in English, regional literatures, and cross-cultural literary traditions. As a translator, Rajalakshmi has played an important role in bringing Kannada literary voices to wider audiences, preserving the nuances of language, culture, and lived experience with remarkable sensitivity. She believes translation is not merely a linguistic exercise but a creative bridge that connects diverse worlds and expands literary horizons. At #BBLF-2026, she brings her rich academic insight and translator's perspective to conversations on language, literature, and the transformative power of stories across cultures.

Jayanta Boral.b: Jayanta Boral is a Bengali poet, lyricist, composer, and engineer whose literary journey has flourished alongside a distinguished career in the Indian automobile industry. A Production Engineering graduate from Jadavpur University , he brings together technical precision and artistic sensitivity through his writings, music, and cultural pursuits. His acclaimed Bengali poetry collection, Moner Pakhna , reflects thoughtful observations on life, relationships, society, and spirituality. In addition to poetry, he has written and composed devotional and contemporary songs, enriching Bengal's literary and musical traditions. A long-time resident of Bengaluru, Jayanta Boral remains deeply connected to Bengali culture and has actively participated in Rabindra Sangeet choral productions and community initiatives. Through his poetry, music, and cultural engagement, he continues to celebrate literature as a living dialogue that inspires reflection, empathy, and meaningful human connection.

Chandrani Chakraborty.b: Chandrani Chakraborty is a Bengali author, poet, entrepreneur, and human resources professional whose life and work embody resilience, creativity, and social purpose. A double postgraduate in Human Resource Management and Tourism Management, she has built an accomplished career while nurturing a deep commitment to literature and the arts. Having overcome the profound loss of her parents at a young age, she transformed adversity into a lifelong pursuit of learning, expression, and service. Her literary works, including Raktim Laharir Itikotha, Alo Aadhari, Phire Dekha Rupkothara, and Dhushar Canvas, explore themes of memory, identity, history, human relationships, and hope with remarkable emotional depth. Beyond writing, Chandrani is an accomplished singer, classical dancer, and active social contributor, reflecting her belief in the transformative power of culture. Her contributions have been recognized with honors such as the Karnataka Excellence Award, Bongo Sreshtho Bhushan Award, and Woman Empowerment Award. At #BBLF-2026, she brings a voice that celebrates literature's ability to heal, inspire, and build meaningful human connections.

Bindu Sajiv.b: Bindu Sajiv is a poet, writer, and journalist from Kozhikode, Kerala, who has been living in Bengaluru since 2000. With several years of experience in journalism and media, she has also established herself as a poet and writer, with her works appearing in leading literary periodicals and various print and digital media platforms. She has participated in literary and poetry events and received the Thalassery Raghavan Memorial Poetry Award in 2018. Her debut poetry collection, Ira Paditham, has been well received. She currently works as a Malayalam linguist, contributing to Natural Language Processing (NLP) projects for Google Assistant.

Vishnumangalam Kumar.b: Vishnumangalam Kumar is a Malayalam writer, journalist, and social activist from Nadapuram, Kerala, who has lived in Bengaluru for over three decades. A writer with the Kerala Sabdam Group, his articles and literary works have appeared in leading Malayalam magazines. He has authored nine books across genres, including essays, short stories, memoirs, journalism, and fiction. He is the founder of the Deepthi Welfare Association and has served in leadership roles with the Bangalore Malayali Writers and Artists Forum and the Sargadhara Cultural Committee. His debut novel, Snehasandram Ravinivesham, set in Bengaluru, has been translated into Kannada and English.

Siva Racharla.b: Siva Racharla is a media personality, political analyst, writer, and independent researcher with a keen interest in Indian history and culture. An avid traveller, he has extensively explored historical sites across India, using his journeys to deepen his research and writing. His work focuses on the Vijayanagara Empire, the Kakatiya dynasty, and the Palegar system of Rayalaseema, bringing lesser-known historical narratives and regional heritage to a wider audience through insightful articles and commentary.

Maya Sharma.b: Maya Sharma is an acclaimed journalist, author, and one of India's most respected television anchors, with over three decades of experience chronicling the nation's political, social, and cultural transformation. Renowned for her incisive reporting, balanced journalism, and engaging storytelling, she has covered landmark elections, governance, public policy, natural disasters, and human-interest stories from across India. Her latest book, Good News, Bad News: A Life in Television, is a compelling memoir that traces the evolution of Indian television news through her remarkable career, offering an insider's account of the changing newsroom, the pursuit of truth, and the challenges facing contemporary journalism. The book is both a personal narrative and a reflection on the rise and transformation of television news in India. At the Book Brahma Literature Festival 2026, Maya Sharma brings her unique perspective on media, democracy, and storytelling, enriching conversations on journalism's enduring role in shaping public discourse.

Anusha Ravi Sood.b: Anusha Ravi Sood is an accomplished journalist, editor, and media professional whose work has consistently focused on politics, public policy, governance, gender, and social change. With extensive experience across leading national news platforms, she has built a reputation for incisive reporting, sharp editorial judgment, and nuanced storytelling that places people at the heart of complex issues. Over the years, she has reported on elections, legislative developments, and socio-political transformations, bringing clarity and depth to contemporary public discourse. Her journalism is distinguished by rigorous research, balanced analysis, and a commitment to amplifying diverse voices from across India. As a moderator and interviewer, Anusha is known for facilitating insightful conversations that encourage informed debate and meaningful engagement. She brings her rich experience in journalism and public affairs to conversations on media, democracy, literature, and the evolving role of storytelling in shaping an informed and inclusive society.

N. Sukumaran.b: Sukumaran is a Tamil poet, writer, translator and editor. He has published 8 volumes of poems, 2 novels, 6 collections of articles on art, literature and social issues, and compiled and edited 4 volumes of pioneers in modern writing. As a translator, he has published 11 books from Malayalam and 7 from English. His translations include the works Pablo Neruda, Gabriel Garcia Marquez, AllasandroBarricco and AyferTunc. His poems have been translated into Malayalam, Hindi, Bengali, Gujrathi, Marathi Punjabi, English, German and French languages. He has served as editor in print and television media for more than a decade. He is now working as the Executive Editor of Kalachuvadu, Tamil magazine for art and ideas. He was awarded the Iyal Award by The Tamil Literary Garden, Canada, in 2017 for his overall contribution to the literary field

Devadevan( P. Kaivalliam).b: Devadevan (pen name of P. Kaivalliam, born 5 May 1948) is an eminent Tamil poet, writer, and literary thinker from Thoothukudi (Tuticorin), Tamil Nadu. Writing since the 1970s, he has published 123 poetry collections, making him one of the most prolific voices in contemporary Tamil poetry. His body of work also includes a book on poetic dialogue, a play, a short story collection, essays, speeches, and Religion of Poetry . A founding president of the Darsana Film Society in Thoothukudi, Devadevan participated in the All India Poets' Seminar at Bharat Bhavan, Bhopal, in 1990. His contributions to Tamil literature have been widely recognized through numerous awards, a documentary on his poetry, and the critical study Tamil Poetry of Modernism with Devadevan as the Focal Point by noted writer and critic Jeyamohan. He currently lives in Bengaluru with his family.

M. Gopalakrishnan.b: M. Gopalakrishnan is a distinguished Tamil author, translator, poet, and literary critic, widely recognized for his significant contributions to contemporary Tamil literature. His body of work spans novels, short stories, poetry, and literary criticism, reflecting a deep engagement with society, culture, and human experience. He is particularly acclaimed for his powerful portrayals of the social and human consequences of industrialization in the Tiruppur region, making him an important voice in modern Tamil fiction. In addition to his original writings, he has translated literary works from English and Hindi into Tamil, enriching the Tamil literary landscape through cross-cultural exchange. Through his diverse literary contributions, M. Gopalakrishnan continues to shape contemporary Tamil literature with his insightful storytelling, critical perspective, and commitment to literary excellence.

Imayam.b: Imayam, the pen name of V. Annamalai, is one of the most distinguished voices in contemporary Tamil literature. Renowned for his unflinching realism and profound humanism, he writes compellingly about rural Tamil Nadu, caste, gender, labour, and the lives of marginalized communities. His acclaimed debut novel Koveru Kazhuthaigal established him as a major literary force and remains a landmark in modern Tamil fiction. His other notable works include Arumugam, Pethavan, Sedal, and Selladha Panam, each reflecting his deep engagement with social realities and the complexities of human relationships. Imayam's fiction is celebrated for its emotional intensity, authentic characters, and understated yet powerful narrative style. His contributions to Tamil literature have earned him numerous honours, including the Sahitya Akademi Award. Widely translated into several Indian and international languages, his works continue to resonate with readers across cultures, affirming literature's power to illuminate lives often left unheard.

Kadarkarai.b: Kadarkarai Mathavilasa Angatham is a Tamil poet, researcher, journalist, and author with over three decades of experience in literature and more than 25 years in leading Tamil media. Born in Virudhachalam, Tamil Nadu, and based in Chennai, he is widely recognized for his pioneering literary journalism and extensive research on Subramania Bharathi, A.K. Chettiar, and Tamil cultural history. An acclaimed scholar, he received the Ananda Vikatan Award (2016), the Tamil Perayam Bharathi Award from SRM University (2024), and several other literary honors. His major works include the landmark research volumes Bharathi Vijayam, Yaamarindha Pulavan, Gandhi Padukolai: Pathirikai Pathivugal, and an authoritative study on the classic film Parasakthi. He has also published six poetry collections and several acclaimed books on literature, history, and cinema.

Salma.b: Salma is one of the most celebrated voices in contemporary Tamil literature, acclaimed for her fearless exploration of gender, identity, desire, and the lived experiences of women. A distinguished poet, novelist, and public intellectual, her writings challenge social conventions with remarkable sensitivity and literary depth. Her acclaimed novels, The Hour Past Midnight (Irandaam Jaamangalin Kathai) and Women, Dreaming (Manaamiyangal), along with her powerful poetry collections, have been translated into several Indian and international languages, earning her global recognition. Salma's life and work were also chronicled in the internationally acclaimed documentary Salma, directed by Kim Longinotto. Beyond literature, she has made significant contributions to public life, serving as a Member of the Rajya Sabha from Tamil Nadu and advocating for women's rights, education, and social justice. Blending literary excellence with public engagement, Salma continues to inspire readers through her courageous voice, nuanced storytelling, and unwavering commitment to equality and human dignity.

Anuradha Anand.b: Anuradha Anand is a Tamil writer, poet, and literary translator with ten published books, including eight collections of translated poetry, one collection of translated short stories, and her original short story collection Mayirpeeli, which won the Jayanthan Award for Best Creative Fiction (2025). Born in Chennai, she graduated in Physics from Stella Maris College and holds a postgraduate degree in Computer Applications. Her translations of works by poets such as Emily Dickinson, Sylvia Plath, Nicanor Parra, and Sappho have introduced major international voices to Tamil readers. She has received the Aathmanaam Award (2018), Vikatan Award (2019), and Vaasagasaalai Award (2021) for translation. Her writings have appeared in leading Tamil literary journals and magazines, and she was among the 40 poets selected to read at the Semmozhi Maanadu organized by the Government of Tamil Nadu. She currently divides her time between Chennai and London.

Jogi (Girish Rao Hatwar).b: Jogi (Girish Rao Hatwar)  is a celebrated Kannada writer, journalist, novelist, and screenwriter, widely recognized as one of the pioneering voices of neo-literature in contemporary Kannada. Renowned for his evocative storytelling and insightful exploration of society, culture, and human relationships, he has made a lasting impact on Kannada literature and journalism. Through his novels, essays, screenplays, and journalistic writings, Jogi has consistently expanded the boundaries of modern Kannada writing, earning widespread acclaim for his distinctive literary voice and narrative style. His works seamlessly blend literary depth with contemporary relevance, making them accessible to a broad readership. A respected public intellectual and cultural commentator, Girish Rao Hatwar continues to enrich Kannada literature through his multifaceted contributions, inspiring readers and writers alike with his creativity, critical insight, and enduring commitment to the language.

Balasaheb Lokapur.b: Balasaheb Lokapur is a distinguished Kannada writer, novelist, researcher, and academic, widely recognized for his significant contributions to contemporary Kannada literature. A leading voice in Post-Modernist (Navyottara) writing, his works are celebrated for their intellectual depth, literary innovation, and critical engagement with society and culture. Through his extensive contributions as an author, scholar, and researcher, Dr. Lokapur has enriched Kannada literary discourse and inspired generations of readers and academics. His enduring commitment to literature and scholarship has earned him widespread acclaim, including the prestigious Karnataka Rajyotsava Award conferred by the Government of Karnataka. With a career dedicated to literary excellence and academic inquiry, Balasaheb Lokapur continues to be an influential figure in Karnataka's literary and cultural landscape.

A. Mohan Kuntar.b: A. Mohan Kuntar is a distinguished scholar, researcher, and academic whose work has significantly contributed to the fields of translation studies, comparative literature, culture, and Yakshagana. With academic qualifications in Malayalam, Tamil, and Telugu, he has established himself as a leading voice in South Indian literary and cultural studies.   His major published works include Kerala Kathan, The Kannada Heritage of Communities, and The Kannada–Malayalam Translation Process, among several other influential books. His research articles, including Kannada Translation Literature and Gender Perspectives in Communities, have received wide recognition for their scholarly depth and critical insight.   Through his extensive research and publications, Dr. Kuntar continues to enrich the understanding of language, literature, cultural traditions, and the dynamic processes of translation across South Indian literary landscapes.

Prashanth P. K. M.b: Prashanth P. K. M. is an Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer and administrator, currently serving as the Managing Director of Karnataka Soaps & Detergents Limited (KSDL) , the state-owned enterprise renowned for its iconic Mysore Sandal Soap . Known for his leadership in public administration and sustainable resource management, he has played a key role in strengthening one of Karnataka's most celebrated heritage brands. With extensive experience in forest conservation, environmental governance, and institutional leadership, Dr. Prashanth has contributed significantly to public service through innovative management practices and a commitment to sustainable development. His work reflects a strong focus on preserving natural resources while promoting excellence in public sector enterprises.

Dennis Paul.b: Dennis Paul, a native of Kozhikode, is a well-known cultural figure among the Malayali community in Bangalore. He has been actively involved in cultural initiatives since moving to Bangalore in 1974 and joining Indian Telephone Industries (ITI) in 1976. He holds diplomas in Mechanical Engineering from M.E.I. Polytechnic and in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from ITI. A founder member and core activist of the Karnataka Progressive Arts Club (CPAC), Dennis has been a central presence in the cultural activities of Kerala Samajam Dooravani Nagar. He has served in key roles including General Secretary and Chairman of the Literary Committee, and currently continues to serve as the General Secretary of the Samajam. An accomplished playwright and director, Dennis has written and staged numerous plays under the CPAC banner. His works have received several accolades, including first prizes in Malayalam drama competitions held by organizations such as Bangalore Kerala Samajam, Bell Malayali Association, Kalavedi, and Madras Keralam Samajam. He currently resides in Udaya Nagar, near Dooravani Nagar, Bangalore."

Suchitra Ramachandran.b: Suchitra Ramachandran is an acclaimed bilingual writer, literary translator, and neuroscientist whose work bridges the worlds of science and literature. Writing original fiction in Tamil and translating literary works between Tamil and English, she has earned recognition for bringing contemporary Tamil literature to a wider readership while fostering meaningful cross-cultural literary exchange. Her writing is marked by intellectual depth, narrative sensitivity, and a keen understanding of human experience. Through her original fiction, translations, and interdisciplinary perspective, Suchitra Ramachandran continues to make significant contributions to contemporary Indian literature and literary translation.

K. Srinivas.b: K. Srinivas is a distinguished journalist, editor, author, and public intellectual whose contributions have significantly shaped contemporary Telugu journalism and literary discourse. With a career spanning over three decades, he has served in key editorial roles at leading Telugu newspapers and media organizations, earning widespread respect for his incisive political analysis, thoughtful commentary, and commitment to ethical journalism. His writings explore politics, governance, culture, literature, and social transformation with depth, clarity, and intellectual rigor. Beyond journalism, Srinivas is an accomplished author whose essays and books reflect a profound engagement with democracy, public life, and the evolving cultural landscape of India. As a speaker and moderator, he is known for fostering informed and meaningful conversations on issues of national importance. His work continues to inspire journalists, readers, and students alike through its integrity, analytical insight, and literary sensibility, making him one of the most respected voices in contemporary Indian media and public discourse.

Gopal Hosur.b: Gopal Hosur is a distinguished Indian Police Service (IPS) officer whose career reflects exemplary commitment to public service, integrity, and social responsibility. With decades of experience in policing and administration, he has held several important leadership positions. He is widely respected for his contributions to strengthening law enforcement, maintaining public order, and promoting people-centric policing. Known for his professionalism, compassion, and strategic approach, Gopal Hosur has played a significant role in advancing community engagement and institutional excellence within the police force. Beyond his distinguished service in policing, he has been deeply connected to art, literature, and culture. A passionate advocate for creativity and intellectual dialogue, he has supported initiatives that celebrate Indian heritage, languages, and artistic expression. His appreciation for literature, music, and cultural traditions reflects his belief in the transformative power of art in society. Through his multifaceted contributions, Gopal Hosur continues to inspire a meaningful dialogue between public service and cultural enrichment.

Sathish Thottassery.b: Sathish Thottassery is a Bengaluru-based writer, cultural organiser, and theatre enthusiast originally from Ayalur, near Nemmara in Palakkad. A former Admin Manager at Hewlett-Packard, he has held leadership roles in several cultural organisations including the Deccan Cultural Society and Kerala Samajam Bangalore South West. Active in theatre and literary circles, he writes short stories and poems and won first prize in a short story competition by United Writers Bangalore. His debut book is Anubhava Narma Nakshathrangal

Anil Dyani.b: Anil Dyani is a Telugu poet from Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. He is the author of three poetry anthologies—Enimidorangu, Speling Mistake, and Gandharivana. A recipient of several literary awards, he has also written numerous essays on Telugu poetry. He is the co-founder of HORU Publications, which is dedicated to publishing Telugu poetry and inspiring young readers and writers through the promotion of contemporary poetry.

Rahul A. R.b: Rahul A. R. is a technology professional, editor, publisher, and bibliophile from Kozhikode, Kerala, who has been based in Bengaluru for over 15 years. He serves as a Senior Delivery Manager at a US-based technology company, specializing in IT and Digital Employee Experience (DEX). Alongside his technology career, Rahul is deeply committed to Malayalam literature. He is the Managing Editor of Miracle Books, a Malayalam publishing house, and the founder of Pusthakasadya, Bengaluru's first exclusive Malayalam bookstore. A passionate reader and editor, he has edited several books and actively supports emerging writers while promoting Malayalam literature and reading culture beyond Kerala.

Chukki K. R.b: Chukki K. R. is a theatre artist, actor, choreographer, theatre educator, and photographer associated with Sanchari Theatre , where she has spent over 15 years contributing as a performer, facilitator, and mentor. Trained in Kathak at the Abhinava Dance Company and holding a Diploma in Theatre, she has performed in acclaimed productions and collaborated with some of India's leading theatre practitioners. A passionate advocate of theatre education, Chukki has led children's theatre workshops, directed productions, and currently heads "Nali Mana," a theatre and mental health initiative for children in collaboration with Sanchari Theatre. Alongside acting and choreography, she is an accomplished theatre photographer and has participated in prestigious national and international theatre festivals. Through her multidisciplinary practice, Chukki continues to explore the transformative power of performance, creativity, and storytelling.

Vinutha Budihal.b: Vinutha Budihal is a renowned Kannada folk and classical singer, celebrated for her significant contributions to Karnataka's musical and cultural traditions. Trained in Carnatic classical music and holding a postgraduate degree in Kannada Folk Literature , she has established herself as a respected performer, educator, and cultural ambassador. She is also a B High Grade Artist of All India Radio in the Bhavageethe category and has previously served as a Radio Jockey with AIR FM Rainbow . A sought-after performer, Vinutha has graced prestigious platforms including the Mysuru Dasara , Vishwa Kannada Sammelana , Akhila Karnataka Sahitya Sammelana , Janapada Lokotsava , and Hampi Utsav , besides performing across India. She is the founder of Anika Cultural Trust , where she mentors aspiring musicians in Carnatic and light music, nurturing the next generation of artists. In recognition of her contributions to Kannada music and literature, Vinutha Budihal has received several honours and is fondly known by titles such as "Gayanashri" and "Kavya Ganga." Beyond music, she has also contributed to acting, choreography, costume design, and documentary filmmaking, reflecting her multifaceted artistic journey.

M. Bhuvana Rani.b: M. Bhuvana Rani is an artist and Assistant Public Prosecutor whose creative journey seamlessly complements her distinguished career in public service. A lifelong painter, she has nurtured her passion for art since childhood and has earned recognition at the state, national, and international levels for her artistic excellence. Trained in law, sociology, psychology, and criminology, Bhuvana Rani brings a unique interdisciplinary perspective to her work. Her artistic practice spans traditional Indian art forms such as Kalamkari, Warli, and Tanjore painting , reflecting her commitment to preserving and promoting India's rich cultural heritage. Balancing the worlds of law and art with equal dedication, M. Bhuvana Rani continues to inspire through her creativity, cultural advocacy, and unwavering pursuit of excellence.

Pooja Sagar.b: Pooja Sagar is an educator, professional storyteller, children's author, and family counsellor dedicated to nurturing a love for stories and reading. As the founder of Sinchana Centre for Storytelling in Bengaluru, she conducts storytelling sessions for children and adults while training educators and enthusiasts in the art of storytelling. An accomplished writer, Pooja regularly writes short stories and picture books for children. Her book Something's Hiding , published by Karadi Tales , reflects her passion for creating engaging stories for young readers. She is also deeply committed to library education and has established a children's library to encourage reading among children. With a background in biotechnology, teaching, and counselling, Pooja brings a unique interdisciplinary approach to education. She currently serves as a librarian and teaches Environmental Management at Ohana School, Bengaluru , where she combines storytelling, learning, and counselling to foster creativity, confidence, and holistic development in children.

Pa. Sagadevan (Palani Krishnaswami).b: Pa.Sagadevan’s novel ‘Anthimam’  (2023) looks at Koramangala from a migrant’s point of view. It observes both the changing topography and the unchanging nature of humans, nonchalantly, over four decades. As an academic researcher he identified the versatility of folk religion in offering stiff resistance to vedic religion through a comparison of two folk epics, Maleya Madeshwara (Kannada) and Annanmar Kathai (Tamil). So fascinated by the earthly nature of religion he attempted to  trace the history of Syrian Christians of Keralam right from the days of St. Thomas. Fanatical about the power and range of contemporary Kannada literature, he translated the works of Purnachandra Tejaswi, Banu Mushtaq and K Y Narayanasamy into Tamil. Tejaswi’s work fetched him the Central Sahitya Akademi award. He is currently Professor Emeritus, Christ (Deemed to be) University, Bengaluru.

Allam Narayana.b: Allam Narayana is a prominent Indian Telugu journalist, poet, and grassroots writer who contributed significantly to the Telangana statehood movement. Over his career, he served at major media houses like Andhra Prabha, Prajatantra, and Andhra Jyothy. He later became the foundational Chief Editor of the Namasthe Telangana daily newspaper in 2011. As a literary figure, he is widely celebrated for his fiery columns like Pranahitha and Vennela Konallo, written in the authentic Telangana dialect. Narayana is the founder-president of the Telangana Journalists Forum. He also served as the first Chairman of the Media Academy of Telangana, championing working-class socio-economic struggles.

Geetha Bhat.b: Geetha Bhat, the founder of Center for Revival of Indigenous Arts, is a multifaceted artist, educator, and cultural ambassador with a diverse background in traditional arts, including Origami, Ikebana, and Chittara painting. She has been working with the Deevaru Community for over two decades on their art form Chittara. Through her fieldwork, she has conducted numerous introductory workshops on Chittara in several educational institutions across the country. Chittara Murals have also been commissioned in various public spaces, such as South Western Railways, Spicmacay Resource Center, Indira Gandhi National Center for Arts (IGNCA), Indian Music Experience, and more. Her research has also led her to present papers about Chittara at international conferences in Japan.

Anil Thirumangalam.b: Anil Thirumangalam is a theatre practitioner, playwright, and director, and the Founder-Director of Lockdown Artworks, an independent theatre collective based in Bengaluru. Over the years, he has written and directed numerous short and full-length plays, with productions staged across Bengaluru as well as in Chennai and Thiruvananthapuram, including as the opening performance at the prestigious Soorya Festival. Writing primarily in Malayalam, while also working in English and Hindi, Anil's theatre explores the possibilities of intimate performance in urban spaces and reflects the richness of multicultural experiences. Deeply committed to theatre as a powerful medium of artistic expression and human connection, he continues to create works that celebrate dialogue, diversity, and the unifying spirit of performance.

Joseph John.b: Joseph John is a theatre director, actor, acting trainer, writer, and cultural educator with over 38 years of experience in theatre, cinema, puppetry, and arts education. Born in Champakulam, Kerala, he has trained at prestigious institutions including Abhinaya Theatre Research Centre, Ninasam, Kerala Kalamandalam, Rangayana Mysore, and Odin Teatret, Denmark, where he worked under renowned theatre director Eugenio Barba. He has directed 60+ plays, acted in 80+ productions, and performed in 500+ street plays, blending traditional Indian performance forms with contemporary theatre. Joseph is the founder of Jo Act Academy and Golden Dolls Puppet Theatre, and has conducted theatre and teacher-training workshops across India. A bilingual writer in Malayalam and Kannada, he has authored the short story collection Sakkada and the poetry anthology Kausani . He continues to mentor aspiring artists while promoting theatre as a powerful medium for education and cultural expression.

Sameera.b: Sameera works as a Development sector professional with more than a decade of experience in Education, Computational Thinking, Career and Gender. She also has a deep interest in Arts and Culture having diverse experiences participating in film/cultural festivals, filmmaking, film criticism, theatre, choirs and more. Her keen interest in preserving Telugu literature, led her to participate in the Tilt workshop, a joint effort by Telugu publishing houses Aju and Chaaya Publications, a first-of-its-kind 6-month translation workshop led by famous French translator Ros Schwartz in 2024. Over the years, she has translated several short stories and one novel from Telugu to English.

Challapalli Swaroopa Rani.b: Challapalli Swaroopa Rani is a distinguished Telugu Dalit feminist poet, writer, scholar, and academic. She is a Professor at the Centre for Buddhist Studies, Nagarjuna University, Andhra Pradesh. Widely recognized as a pioneering Dalit feminist voice in Telugu literature, her poetry and essays explore caste, gender, social justice, and the lived experiences of Dalit women. A Buddhist scholar and historian, she brings together academic insight and personal experience to highlight the struggles and resilience of marginalized communities. She has authored more than a dozen books and is regarded as one of the most influential contemporary voices in Telugu literature.

Selvakumari.b: Selva Kumari is an academic, researcher, and Kannada scholar, currently serving as Professor and Head of the Department of Kannada at Smt. VHD Central Institute of Home Science, Bengaluru. With decades of experience in higher education, she has made significant contributions to Kannada language and literary studies through teaching, research, and academic leadership. A dedicated researcher and mentor, Selva Kumari has guided doctoral scholars and has published research in academic journals. She has served as Chairperson and member of the Board of Studies (BOS) and Board of Examiners (BOE) at several autonomous institutions and universities, including Maharani Cluster University, and has contributed as a textbook editor, paper setter, and evaluator for Bengaluru University and other academic bodies. Beyond academics, she has actively promoted literary and cultural activities through her roles as convenor of Kannada Sangha, cultural committees, and college publications. Through her scholarship, teaching, and institutional leadership, Selva Kumari continues to make valuable contributions to Kannada education and literary discourse.

Kruthi R. Purappemane.b: Kruthi R. Purappemane is a Kannada writer, researcher, and Yakshagana artist whose work bridges literature, cultural studies, and traditional performing arts. Widely recognized for her insightful critical writing, she has contributed extensively through columns and essays that explore literature, society, and the evolving role of cultural traditions. With a deep engagement in Yakshagana, Kruthi's research examines its aesthetics, performance practices, and social dimensions, bringing fresh perspectives to one of Karnataka's most celebrated art forms. Through her writing, scholarship, and artistic practice, she continues to make meaningful contributions to Kannada literature and the preservation and understanding of coastal Karnataka's rich cultural heritage.

Cheemanahalli Ramesha Babu.b: Cheemanahalli Ramesha Babu is an acclaimed Kannada novelist, poet, and short story writer whose works explore contemporary social realities with literary depth and sensitivity. A research scientist by profession, he has authored several acclaimed poetry collections, novels, and short story anthologies, including Tyresami , Balihara , and Hada . His contributions to Kannada literature have earned him numerous honours, including the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Book Award , the Masti Novel Award , and the Bendre Grantha Bahumana

N.C. Mahesh.b: N.C. Mahesh is a Kannada writer, playwright, theatre critic, and academic from Benachanahalli in Bengaluru Rural district, Karnataka. He holds a Master's degree in Kannada from Bangalore University and has worked with Kannada Prabha and Prajavani before joining academia. He is currently an Assistant Professor at Surana College, Bengaluru. A passionate literary and theatre personality, Mahesh has authored short story collections, a novel, and over 15 plays. His acclaimed plays Sala Teerisu Ghalib, Sakutande Rumi, and Summaniru Diogenes have received prestigious awards in state-level playwriting competitions. He has also contributed as an editor, translator, and columnist, with his writings on theatre, literature, and culture appearing in leading Kannada publications. Mahesh is a four-time winner of the Prajavani Deepavali Story Competition and continues to make significant contributions to Kannada literature and theatre.

K. M. Chaitanya.b: K. M. Chaitanya is an acclaimed filmmaker, documentary maker, and theatre director whose work has made a significant impact on contemporary Kannada cinema. Known for his realistic storytelling and nuanced screenplays, he has earned widespread recognition for creating films that explore human emotions and social realities with authenticity, while consciously avoiding the glorification of violence. With a strong foundation in theatre and documentary filmmaking, Chaitanya brings a distinctive artistic vision to his work, blending cinematic craft with thoughtful narratives. Through his contributions to film and theatre, he continues to enrich Kannada's cultural landscape as a filmmaker committed to meaningful and socially relevant storytelling.

Sathish Shetty Vakwady.b: Sathish Shetty Vakwady  is an author and finance professional based in Bengaluru, originally from Vakwadi, Kundapura. Serving as a General Manager in a private firm, his creative pursuits encompass short stories, essays, and sports writing. A former reporter for Canara Times and co-founder of the magazine Chiguru, his works have been featured in Vijaya Karnataka, Sangatha, AIR Mangaluru, and various regional publications. He is the author of the story collections `Ajja netta halasina mara’, `koneya yeradu yesethagalu’. His upcoming novel, `Suli’, a novel is currently poised for release.

Mala Kumar.b: Mala Kumar is a children’s book author and editor. Her books include 'The Missing Rocks of Hampi', 'Travelling Treasures' and 'Travelling Treasures 2.0' and several picture books including a biography of Sir M Visvesvaraya.

Meenu Sivaramakrishnan.b: Meenu Sivaramakrishnan is a professional storyteller, improv practitioner, theatre facilitator, Carnatic vocalist, voice artist, and educator. After a decade-long corporate career leading clients across the Asia-Pacific region, she founded KATHA GALATTA – Unleash Your Joy Through Stories, using oral storytelling as a powerful tool for learning, creativity, and personal growth.   A member of the Federation of Asian Storytellers, Indian Storytelling Network, and Bangalore Storytelling Society, Meenu has trained students, educators, professionals, and communities through storytelling and theatre. She has served as a resource person for the Tamil Nadu Government’s Naan Mudhalvan program and as a visiting faculty at the Manipal Academy of Higher Education, where she facilitated storytelling-based courses for management students.   Meenu has performed at leading national and international storytelling and literature festivals, including the Morocco Marrakech Storytelling Festival, Bangalore Literature Festival, and Bookflix Children’s Fest. She also conducts storytelling workshops for schools, corporates, government organizations, and senior citizens, and has presented research on storytelling at the 6th Nadi Utsav (2025) organized by the Ministry of Culture.

Ayushi D. Nag.b: Aayushi is a 16 year old, who is extremely interested in writing poetry and reading about history and politics. She has written and published 3 books - one of which she has co-authored. She is passionate about human and animal rights and tries to create empathy towards the human condition through her poetry. She can often be found reading her favorite books, practicing classical music, or creating crochet goodies.

Arni C.N.b: Arni CN  8th STD KLE BASVA RESIDENTIAL GIRLS SCHOOL Arni has a published book of poetry — 'ECHOES FROM MY JAR' a collection of poems that teach you to live life to the fullest . She started reading from an early age and began writing by the tender age of 9 to process her tumultuous feelings. To connect with something deeper, not just with herself but the entire world around her. She makes her vulnerability her greatest strength by painting a new picture of the world, finding beauty every where; even in imperfections

Austin Ajit.b: Austin Ajit is a young writer, nature enthusiast, and one of India’s most promising literary prodigies from Bengaluru. A Grade 8 student at Wolsey Hall Oxford (UK), he has authored and translated 12 books, including novels, short story collections, and science fiction works, with a strong focus on nature and environmental conservation. His short story collection The Ray of Hope has been translated into German.   At the age of 12, Austin received the prestigious Times of India & Reliance Foundation Unstoppable21 Award for his contributions to nature conservation through literature. He also completed the IIT Madras–IISc Bengaluru Basic Course in Ornithology with an Elite Silver grade, becoming one of the youngest participants to excel in the program.   Austin actively contributes to citizen science through bird surveys, butterfly expeditions, and nature conservation initiatives. He made his acting debut in the Kannada film September-13 (2022) and has received several accolades, including the Kerala Bala Sahitya Academy Bala Prathibha Award (2024), the Sueños International Children’s Book Award (2025), and the Panorama International Literature Prodigy Award (2023). Recognized by Harvard World Records London and the India Book of Records, Austin continues to inspire young readers by combining literature, science, and environmental stewardship.

M Bairegowda.b: M. Bairegowda is a folk scholar, playwright, singer, poet, organiser, publisher, and book promoter. Born in Krishnapura, Ramanagara Taluk, he holds a Ph.D. in Folklore Studies. He has contributed to folklore research, theatre, poetry, and literature, and has acted in more than 50 plays. He has also showcased his talent through Yakshagana and solo performances. He has received several honours, including the Karnataka Sahitya Academy Award, Karnataka Nataka Academy Award, and G. Narayana Janapada Loka Award. He has performed music and theatre both in India and abroad and has served as a Kannada professor for several years. As a publisher, he has published more than 860 books, making a significant contribution to Kannada literature and folk culture.

Krishna Prasad.b: Krishna Prasad is one of India's most respected journalists, editors, and public intellectuals, known for his incisive writing, editorial leadership, and deep engagement with contemporary politics, governance, and society. Over a distinguished career spanning more than three decades, he has held senior editorial positions at leading national publications, shaping public discourse through thoughtful reportage, sharp analysis, and fearless commentary. His work is marked by intellectual rigor, historical perspective, and a commitment to independent journalism. Beyond the newsroom, Krishna Prasad is a sought-after speaker and moderator, bringing nuance and clarity to conversations on democracy, media ethics, public policy, and India's changing socio-political landscape. His ability to connect current events with broader historical and cultural contexts has earned him widespread respect across academic, literary, and journalistic circles. Through his writing and public engagements, he continues to contribute meaningfully to debates on governance, citizenship, and the role of the media in a rapidly transforming world.

Sidharth Varadarajan.b: Sidharth Varadarajan is an award-winning journalist, editor, and one of India's foremost voices on politics, democracy, and media freedom. He is the Founding Editor of The Wire, an independent digital news platform widely recognized for its investigative journalism and in-depth analysis of public affairs. Over a distinguished career spanning more than three decades, he has worked with leading publications including The Times of India and The Hindu, where he served as Editor. His reporting and editorial leadership have consistently championed constitutional values, accountability, and independent journalism. Varadarajan is also the co-editor of Gujarat: The Making of a Tragedy (2002), a landmark volume examining the 2002 Gujarat violence through essays by leading scholars, journalists, and public intellectuals. A sought-after public speaker, he regularly engages in discussions on media ethics, democracy, foreign policy, and the challenges facing journalism in the digital age. His work continues to shape informed public discourse in India.

T. N. Seetharam.b: T. N. Seetharam is a renowned Kannada filmmaker, television director, screenwriter, and actor, widely recognized for his significant contribution to Kannada cinema and television. Known for his thought-provoking storytelling, he has created works that engage deeply with social issues, human relationships, and contemporary life. Through his distinctive narrative style and compelling characters, Seetharam has become an influential figure in Karnataka’s cultural landscape. His work across film, television, and theatre reflects a sustained commitment to meaningful storytelling and has earned him a lasting place in Kannada popular culture.

Sunetra Pandit.b: Sunetra Pandit is a prominent Kannada actress and dubbing artist, widely recognized for her memorable contributions to Kannada cinema and television. She is best known for her iconic portrayal of Vishalu , the quirky and much-loved secretary in the classic ETV Kannada sitcom Silli Lalli , a role that earned her widespread popularity and endeared her to audiences across Karnataka. With a career spanning television and film, Sunetra has built a reputation for her versatile performances and exceptional voice artistry. Through her work as both an actor and dubbing artist, she continues to be a respected and familiar presence in the Kannada entertainment industry.

Prasanna Sagara.b: Prasanna Sagar is a NSD & NINASAM graduate, who wears many hats. Besides directing, designing and writing, he is also an acting tutor. Among his several directorial/design projects, are his Peer Gynt  by Henrik Ibsen which received critical reviews. He has translated and adapted into Kannada, several plays such as,  The Rape  by Franca Rame,  Yarma  by Lorca,  Peer Gynt  by Ibsen and  Baby  by Vijay Tendulkar. He has designed and executed sets for several theatre productions nationally and internationally, including Actors Ensemble India Forum’s Ultimate Kurukshetra which ran to full houses at the Esplanade in Singapore. He has done the art direction for the internationally acclaimed and multi award-winning Hindi feature film –  Ghode Ko Jalebi Khilane Le Ja Riya Hoon , directed by Anamika Haksar.

Omshivaprakash H L.b: Omshivaprakash H L is a Digital Archivist and Entrepreneur with a passion for building linguistic tech and archival initiatives focused on art, history, culture, and literature. He is a co-founder of the #ServantsOfKnowledge initiative, which has been instrumental in digitizing and making accessible various books, manuscripts, and magazines across India, helping to preserve the nation's rich literary heritage. Through his ventures, he specializes in developing language technology solutions for Kannada and other Indian languages.  A dedicated Wikipedian and Mozillan, Omshivaprakash is committed to open knowledge, open access, and community-driven projects. He also co-founded Sanchaya (https://sanchaya.org), a platform enhancing Kannada literary research through technology, and the Sanchi Foundation (https://sanchifoundation.org), which digitally documents Kannada art, history, culture, and literature. Notably, Vachana Sanchaya (https://vachana.sanchaya.net) has had a lasting impact by making research accessible to the public. His work continues to inspire and impact communities locally and globally, reflecting his deep commitment to the Kannada language and culture.

K. M. Vasundhara.b: K. M. Vasundhara is an administrator, poet, author, and public servant, currently serving as the Managing Director of LIDKAR (Dr. Babu Jagjivan Ram Leather Industries Development Corporation Ltd.), Government of Karnataka. A senior Karnataka Administrative Service (KAS) officer, she has held key leadership positions across the Departments of Agricultural Marketing, Tourism, and Social Welfare, and is recognized for her contributions to public administration and institutional development. Alongside her administrative career, Dr. Vasundhara is an accomplished Kannada writer and poet. She has published poetry collections including Maretu Bittaddu , Kannada Kavi Kavya Kusuma Male–40 , and Nepathyada Niluvugannadi , and has authored over 750 short stories, besides numerous poems, articles, and essays. Her literary works have been featured in leading Kannada publications, and her poems have been included in the undergraduate curriculum of the University of Mysore. A recipient of the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award, Mantralaya Sri Parimala Award, and Nari Samman 2026, Dr. Vasundhara is also a sought-after speaker, mentor, and advocate for youth development, continuing to make meaningful contributions to Kannada literature and public life.

Sri Divya.b: Sri Divya is the Co-founder of Jhansi Publications, an independent Telugu publishing house committed to discovering, nurturing, and promoting new voices in Telugu literature. She has been actively working to make quality Telugu books more accessible to readers while creating opportunities for emerging writers to publish their work. Through publishing initiatives, literary events, and collaborations, she aims to build a vibrant reading community and strengthen the contemporary Telugu literary ecosystem.

Madhuri Palaji.b: Madhuri Palaji is an author, publisher, and screenwriter whose work celebrates the power of stories to connect people and ideas. She is the author of Uniki and the founder of Lilac Books, an independent publishing house committed to championing contemporary voices in literature. A literary reviewer and script consultant, she actively engages with books, storytelling, and the creative arts. An IIM Kozhikode alumnus, she also has over 18 years of experience in people leadership, bringing together the worlds of literature, creativity, and human connection.

Umesh Raman.b: Umesh Raman is a senior media professional with over 25 years of experience in journalism and the news industry. He serves as the Editor of News Bengaluru.com, a Bengaluru-based online news platform known for its coverage of current affairs and public issues. Originally from Kasaragod, Kerala, Umesh Raman is a keen social observer and an ardent lover of literature. His work reflects a deep engagement with society, culture, and contemporary issues, combining journalistic insight with a strong appreciation for literary thought.

K. Shivalingappa Handihalu.b: K. Shivalingappa Handihalu is a Kannada children's writer, translator, editor, and educator from Handihalu village in Ballari district. A primary school teacher by profession, he has made significant contributions to children's literature through his poems, stories, novels, translations, and editorial work, inspiring young readers with engaging and imaginative writing. His notable works include Naanu Mattu Kannadaka , The Young Scientist , Tiffin Box , and Notebook , while his translations for the National Book Trust and other institutions have introduced children to diverse literary works. He has also served as the founding editor of the children's magazine Balapa and has actively contributed to literary and cultural organizations in Karnataka. A recipient of several prestigious honours, including the Sahitya Akademi Bal Sahitya Puraskar (2025) for Notebook , K. Shivalingappa Handihalu continues to enrich Kannada children's literature through his writing, research, translation, and unwavering commitment to nurturing young readers.

Gademane Sudha.b: Gademane Sudha is an accomplished Chittara artist and a dedicated practitioner of one of Karnataka's most distinctive indigenous art traditions. With over three decades of experience, she has played a significant role in preserving and promoting Chittara through her paintings and eco-friendly handicrafts, including the traditional Battada Torana (paddy torans) and Karadada Kaddi, a unique grass-crafted hair accessory. Beyond her visual art, Sudha is also an accomplished folk singer and dancer, embodying the rich cultural heritage of rural Karnataka. As an artist associated with CFRIA, she has conducted Chittara workshops at the Museum of Art and Photography (MAP), exhibited her works at the Language of Lines exhibition at the Bangalore International Centre (BIC) in 2025, and contributed to the muraling team at the Indian Music Experience (IME). Her work reflects a deep commitment to sustaining traditional knowledge and celebrating Karnataka's vibrant folk arts.

Suhasini B. V..b: Suhasini B. V. is a Bharatanatyam artiste, a B-High Grade artiste of Doordarshan Kendra, Bengaluru, and the Founder and Director of Kala Sharadhi Center for Performing Arts. Passionately committed to preserving and promoting India's rich performing arts traditions, she works across education, performance, research, and cultural documentation. Her interdisciplinary approach brings together heritage, storytelling, and strategic communication, making traditional knowledge meaningful and accessible to contemporary audiences. As the Book Sales Consultant at the Centre for Revival of Indigenous Art (CFRIA), she has played a key role in strengthening the organisation's digital outreach and expanding the readership of the acclaimed Deevara Chittara publication. Through her work as an artiste, cultural advocate, and communicator, Suhasini continues to create meaningful connections between India's artistic legacy and present-day cultural discourse. She will moderate the session, drawing on her deep engagement with the performing and visual arts.

Dimpesh Bhatewara.b: Dimpesh Bhatewara is an IT professional with over 12 years of experience in the technology industry and a passionate advocate for resilience, inclusion, and human potential. While building a successful career in technology, he has consistently championed the values of perseverance, empathy, and partnership through his personal journey. In 2026, Dimpesh accompanied his wife, Priyanka Agarwal, on an inspiring expedition to Everest Base Camp, where they became India's first inter-abled couple to complete the iconic trek together. Their achievement stands as a powerful testament to courage, mutual trust, and the belief that determination transcends physical limitations. Dimpesh brings a compelling perspective on overcoming adversity, the strength found in companionship, and the transformative power of stories rooted in lived experience. His journey inspires audiences to challenge perceived boundaries and embrace life's summits with optimism, resilience, and an unwavering spirit.

Priyanka Agarwal.b: Priyanka Agarwal is a Product Manager with over 15 years of experience spanning information technology, banking, stock broking, and telecommunications. A passionate advocate for accessibility and disability inclusion, she is also a motivational speaker who encourages individuals and institutions to view inclusion as a shared social responsibility rather than an accommodation. In April 2026, Priyanka became the first visually impaired woman from Karnataka and the second blind Indian woman to trek to Everest Base Camp. Alongside her husband, Dimpesh Bhatewara, she also became part of India's first inter-abled couple to complete the iconic journey, demonstrating that courage, preparation, and determination can transcend perceived limitations. Her work extends beyond personal achievement through mentoring visually impaired students in assistive technology, conducting accessibility awareness programmes, and speaking at national and international forums. At the Book Brahma Literature Festival, Priyanka brings an inspiring narrative of resilience, inclusion, and the limitless possibilities of the human spirit.

K. Satyaranjan.b: K. Satyaranjan is a retired banking professional and an accomplished literary translator who has made significant contributions to Telugu literature by translating influential works from across the world. His extensive body of translations spans memoirs, political thought, social justice, history, and contemporary global literature. Among his notable translations are I Am Malala by Malala Yousafzai and Christina Lamb, Halla Bol: The Death and Life of Safdar Hashmi by Sudhanva Deshpande, The Man Mao by Quan Yanchi, The Final Journey by Gabriel García Márquez, Periyar: A Political Biography by Bala Jeyaraman, I Could Not Be a Hindu by Bhanwar Meghwanshi, Listen to My Case by Justice K. Chandru, and The Bolivia Diary by Che Guevara. His translation of Ibtisam Azem's The Book of Disappearance gained international recognition when the novel was featured on the 2025 International Booker Prize Longlist. Through his thoughtful and accessible translations, K. Satya Ranjan has played an important role in introducing Telugu readers to diverse global voices and critical ideas, enriching the literary and intellectual landscape of the language.

Shaswata Gangopadhyay.b: Shaswata Gangopadhyay is one of the prominent voices in contemporary Bengali poetry, having begun his literary journey in the mid-1990s. His poems have been translated into 7–8 languages and published in more than 150 international journals and anthologies across six continents. His published poetry collections include Inhabitant of Pluto Planet (2001), Offspring of Monster (2009), Holes of Red Crabs (2015), In the City of Myth and Mushroom (2023), Rhododendron Café (2023), and Poems of Shaswata Gangopadhyay (2023). He has been invited to read his poems at literary festivals and poetry events in the United Kingdom, the United States, France, Australia, South Africa, Colombia, Portugal, as well as in London, Paris, Vienna, and Frankfurt. In 2024, he received the Sparkling Soul Award from Chile, participated in the renowned Gateway Lit Fest in Mumbai, and was honoured with the prestigious Voice of Kolkata Award. In July 2026, he was invited to represent Bengali poetry at the World Poetry Festival – Global Vision Summit (European Edition) in Athens, Greece.

Rajani Radhakrishnan.b: Rajani Radhakrishnan is an acclaimed poet, editor, and literary curator whose work explores memory, identity, displacement, and the complexities of contemporary life. She is the author of three acclaimed poetry collections—Water to Water, Duplicity, and No Way Home—each distinguished by lyrical precision and emotional depth. A nominee for the Pushcart Prize and the Best of the Net Award, Rajani has earned recognition for her distinctive poetic voice and her contribution to modern English-language poetry. She is also the co-founder of Alt Poetry, a vibrant multi-platform initiative dedicated to reading, writing, discussing, and promoting poetry through workshops, conversations, and community engagement. Passionate about nurturing new voices and expanding the reach of poetry, Rajani has played a significant role in building inclusive literary spaces that encourage dialogue and creative expression. Her work continues to inspire readers and writers alike, making her an important voice in India's contemporary literary landscape.

Namratha Varadharajan.b: Namratha Varadharajan is a Bengaluru-based poet whose writing thoughtfully explores identity, gender, emotional resilience, and the complexities of contemporary life through a lens of empathy and keen observation. A nominee for the Best of the Net and Touchstone Awards, her poetry has appeared in leading literary journals and anthologies, including Rattle, Only Poems, The Yearbook of Indian Poetry in English, The Usawa Literary Review, Muse India, The Hooghly Review, haikuKATHA, and Gulmohar Quarterly. She is the co-founder of Alt Poetry, a vibrant literary collective that fosters poetry through readings, workshops, and conversations in both online and offline spaces. A former poetry reader at Only Poems, she also curates the newsletter Poetic Adventures with Namy, connecting readers with the evolving world of poetry. Her debut collection, On Cultivating Loudspeakers and Quilts, is forthcoming, marking an exciting new chapter in her literary journey and contemporary Indian poetry.

Nandita Bose.b: Nandita Bose is a poet, novelist, reviewer, and literary critic whose writing traverses the intimate landscapes of memory, relationships, and the human spirit. Poetry serves as both refuge and reflection in her multifaceted literary life, and her second poetry collection, Longitudes of Light, follows the acclaimed Dewed in exploring the interconnectedness of people, places, and emotions with lyrical sensitivity. As a novelist, she is the author of Something Borrowed Something Blue, Everglow, Shadow & Soul, If Walls Could Weep, The Perfume of Promise, and Tread Softly, works that examine the challenges women navigate within families, workplaces, and society. A respected book reviewer, critic, and frequent literary panellist, Nandita has also worked in academia and the human resources sector. Based in Bengaluru, she continues to enrich contemporary Indian literature through her thoughtful storytelling and evocative poetry, bringing compassion, insight, and intellectual depth to every page.

VamsiKrishna.b: Vamsikrishna is a well-known poet, short-story writer, and critic in Telugu. So far, he has authored 8 poetry collections, 3 short-story anthologies, and 3 books of film criticism. He has written several columns on Indian poetry and international poetry in print and electronic magazines. He has extensively translated poetry and stories into Telugu and has received numerous awards.

Goravinakallu Nagaraju.b: Goravinakallu Nagaraju hails from Kadadarahalli village of Challakere and is actively shaping the literary landscape as a voice of the new generation.

B.G. Gujjarappa.b: B.G. Gujjarappa (Gujjar) is a veteran Indian cartoonist, illustrator, and painter from Karnataka, celebrated for his powerful political cartoons and outstanding contributions to children's literature. He began his career as a history lecturer before becoming a founding cartoonist of Lankesh Patrike, later working with leading publications such as Deccan Herald and Prajavani. A founding member and trustee of the Indian Institute of Cartoonists, Bengaluru, Gujjar has illustrated over 1,000 children's books and authored several of his own. His socially conscious cartoons, election awareness campaigns, and expressive artworks in ink, digital media, and acrylic have earned him wide recognition in the fields of journalism, art, and illustration.

Shinjini Kumar.b: Shinjini Kumar is a writer, financial-services leader and entrepreneur whose work brings together the worlds of business, society, gender and contemporary India. With three decades of experience, she has held senior leadership roles at the Reserve Bank of India, PricewaterhouseCoopers, Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Citibank, and was the founding CEO of Paytm Payments Bank. She later co-founded SALT, a financial platform focused on helping women build financial independence. Her literary debut, Busy Women: Building Commerce and Culture in Middle India, published by Penguin Business in 2026, explores the lives, aspirations and entrepreneurial journeys of women across India’s Tier-II cities. Drawing on conversations with hundreds of women, the book examines how economic agency is reshaping family, work, ambition and social structures in contemporary India. With master’s degrees in English Literature and Public Policy, Kumar brings an unusual combination of literary sensibility, institutional experience and social observation to her writing.

Vijaya Bhandaru.b: Feminist writer Vijaya Bhandaru, hailing from Warangal in Telangana, has worked as a writer, columnist, editor, and professionally as a librarian, constantly portraying the inner turmoils of women in her literature. Many of her works have earned special acclaim in Telugu literature.

Mohan Babu.b: Mohan Babu is a well-known Telugu publisher and writer. He founded Chaya Publications, which has been bringing out significant Telugu works as well as translations of world literature. He recently published Konni Pustakalu – Chinna Parichayalu, featuring introductions to more than 70 books. Through his contributions to publishing and literature, he has created a distinctive presence in the Telugu literary world.

Usha Rani Rao.b: Usha Rani Rao is an educationist, translator, poet, literary critic, and Professor of Hindi. She heads the Department of Hindi at Baldwin Women's Methodist College, Bengaluru. She has authored three poetry collections, two books on literary criticism, and four translated works, besides publishing over 75 research papers. Her acclaimed Hindi translation of Girish Karnad's autobiography, Khel Khel Mein Beeta Jeevan, is a significant contribution to Indian literature. A recipient of several prestigious literary honours, Dr. Rao continues to strengthen the literary and cultural bridge between Hindi and Kannada through her teaching, research, and translations.

T. S . Goravara.b: T. S. Goravar is a Kannada writer, journalist, editor, and researcher from Rajur village in Gadag district. He holds a postgraduate degree in Mass Communication and Journalism from Karnatak University, Dharwad, and a Ph.D. from Hampi Kannada University. He has worked extensively in journalism and literature, bringing together his experience as a journalist with a strong commitment to Kannada writing. His published works span several genres, including short stories, novels, experiential narratives, prose poetry, life writing, and plays. His notable works include Bhrame , Kudari Master , Mallige Hoovina Sakha , Aadu Kaayo Hudugana Dinachari , Rotti Mutagi , Gayagondive Tuti Ninnave Pada Haadi , and Hasiru Towel . He has also edited Baravanigeya Taalimu and written plays including Mallige Hoovina Sakha and Chavari . Dr. Goravar has received several honours, including the Karnataka Sahitya Akademi Award, D. R. Bendre Book Award, Basavaraj Kattimani Award, and recognition from literary and journalism institutions. His stories, experiential writings, and articles have been included in the curricula of undergraduate programmes at Karnatak University, Mangalore University, and Bengaluru University. He worked as a Sub-Editor at Vijaya Karnataka for eight years. In 2018, driven by his vision of independent journalism, he founded the literary monthly magazine Akshara Sangata and continues to serve as its editor.

Sanjay Gubbi.b: Sanjay Gubbi is among India's leading conservation biologists and a widely respected voice in wildlife conservation. Over the past two decades, his work has transformed the protection of tigers, leopards and their habitats through scientific research, conservation policy and landscape restoration. As Programme Head of the Holématthi Nature Foundation, he has helped safeguard nearly 3,000 square kilometres of protected forests in Karnataka. An acclaimed author and recipient of the prestigious Whitley Award, Gubbi continues to shape the future of conservation through science, advocacy and public engagement.

Bijoy Venugopal.b: Bijoy Venugopal is a Bengaluru-based writer, editor, and nature educator with over 25 years of experience in content strategy, editorial leadership, and corporate communication. A former journalist and travel writer, he has contributed to numerous well-known publications and now runs his own storytelling venture. He began birding in his teens and has since watched birds in over 20 countries. A columnist, cartoonist, and photographer, he is also the founder-editor of The Green Ogre, an independent nature storytelling project.

N. Ravi Shankar.b: N. Ravi Shankar is the Founder and CEO of Aim High Consulting, one of India's leading public relations and brand consulting firms. With over 23 years of experience in strategic communications, branding and entrepreneurship, he has mentored countless start-ups and industry leaders while also serving as an author, columnist, guest lecturer and angel investor. Bringing his rich expertise in communication and storytelling, he will moderate the panel discussion, guiding engaging conversations and insightful exchanges throughout the session.

Aaditya G. Tili.b: Aaditya G. Tili is a passionate wildlife photographer, explorer and storyteller with an enduring love for the natural world. Ever since his first encounter with a wild bird at the age of 13, he has been drawn to forests, mountains and wetlands in search of wildlife and the stories they hold. By profession, he works in corporate communication, but his heart belongs in the wild. Through Wings, Woods & Wanders, his debut book, Aaditya hopes to inspire readers to embrace adventure, connect with nature and become advocates for its conservation.

Indira Chandrasekhar.b: Indira Chandrasekhar is a former scientist who has established herself as a distinguished fiction writer, literary curator, editor, and publisher. She is the founder, publisher, and principal editor of the award-winning literary journal Out of Print, a respected platform dedicated to publishing writing connected to the Indian subcontinent. Celebrating a decade of its remarkable journey, the journal's commemorative anthology was published in 2020, showcasing its enduring contribution to contemporary literature. Indira is the author of the acclaimed short story collection Polymorphism, published by HarperCollins, and the novella Aqua Vita, a thought-provoking exploration of the impact of urban development on water bodies. She is also an accomplished translator. Her English translation of Dadapeer Jyman's Neelakurinji marked her debut in literary translation, and she has recently completed translating Atrocity, the powerful novella by noted Dalit writer Guruprasad Kantalagere. Her work seamlessly bridges literature, translation, and editorial excellence.

Bhavya Kabbali.b: Bhavya Kabbali is a Kannada poet whose writing is celebrated for its emotional depth and lyrical simplicity. Originally from Kabbali village in Channarayapatna, Hassan district, she transitioned from a career as an electrical engineer to coffee cultivation in Kodagu, where she continues to pursue her passion for poetry. Her poems have been featured in leading Kannada literary platforms, including Avadhi and Book Brahma, as well as prominent Kannada newspapers. Her work has earned recognition through initiatives such as Poet of the Week by Avadhi and the Valentine Kavi Award presented by the Kajana literary group. Her acclaimed poetry collection, Devara Terigu Gaaligalu Beku, has received prestigious honours including the Dr. G. S. Shivarudrappa Poetry Award from the Shivamogga Kannada Sangha and the Suman Somashekhar Somwarpet Endowment Poetry Award from the Kannada Sahitya Parishat, establishing her as a distinctive voice in contemporary Kannada poetry.

N.A.M. Ismail.b: N A Mahamed Ismail is a media professional with more than two decades of experience. His career spans print journalism, digital journalism, entertainment television, and OTT platforms. He is also a accomplished writer and translator who has extensively covered ICT and its impact on society.

Premachandra U.b: Premachandra U is the Executive Director of Navakarnataka Publications. He retired as Deputy General Manager (DGM) from NLC India Limited (NLCIL) after a distinguished career in the public sector. An engineering graduate from UVCE, Bengaluru , he brings together technical expertise, administrative experience, and a deep commitment to Kannada publishing and literature

Sanket Patil.b: Sanket Patil builds data and AI products for a living. He is part of the founding team at DataWeave where he leads AI strategy and innovation. A computer scientist with a PhD in network science, he continues to engage with academia through research collaborations and teaching as Adjunct Faculty at IIIT-Bangalore. Outside of tech, Sanket is deeply interested in language, literature, culture, society, sustainability, and their interplay. He is part of the Tamarind Valley Collective—a community centered on sustainable living and regenerative farming.
