A writer and translator, his Kannada translation of Peggy Mohan’s Wanderers, Kings, Merchants: The Story of India through its Languages was published in 2025 (ಅಲೆಮಾರಿಗಳು ಅರಸರು ವರ್ತಕರು: ಭಾಷೆಗಳ ಹಾದಿಗುಂಟ ಭಾರತದ ಕಥನ). He runs a small Kannada literary and cultural newsletter called Konaru (ಕೊನರು) that has developed into an interesting literary space for serious readers.

Vanamala Vishwanath.b: Vanamala Viswanatha is a bilingual scholar and award-winning translator who spent more than four decades teaching English literature at premier institutions in Bengaluru. She has made an exceptional contribution to bridging Kannada and English through her translations of modern and medieval Kannada literature. Her works include translations of contemporary authors such as U.R. Ananthamurthy, P. Lankesh, Tejaswi, Vaidehi, Sara Aboobacker, and Gulvadi Venkata Rao, as well as classical works such as the 13th-century Harishchandra Kavyam (The Life of Harishchandra, Murty Classical Library, 2017) and Kuvempu’s epic novel Malegalalli Madumagalu. Beyond translation, she has held several influential positions, including Honorary Director of the Sahitya Akademi’s Centre for Translation and a member of the advisory board of the National Translation Mission.

N.S. Gundur.b: N.S. Gundur is a literary historian whose work explores Kannada literary cultures, intellectual history, and the institutional foundations of literature. Raised in an agricultural family in North Karnataka, he pursued his higher education at Karnatak University, Dharwad, before beginning his teaching career at the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla, Pune. He is currently Professor of English at Tumkur University. A bilingual scholar, Gundur writes extensively in English and Kannada for academic journals and leading publications, including The Economic and Political Weekly, The Hindu, The Indian Express, The Wire, Atlantis, and Prajavani. He has translated Michel Foucault into Kannada and authored Vartamanada Itihasakara: A Critical Introduction to Michel Foucault (2017). A recipient of the NIF Translation Fellowship (2022), his English translation of D.R. Nagaraj's Allama Prabhu and Śaiva Imagination, published by Permanent Black and SUNY Press, has earned international acclaim. Distinguished scholar Sheldon Pollock has hailed it as "a remarkable contribution to literary and historical scholarship.

Sushma Shankar.b: Sushma Shankar is a distinguished Kannada scholar, bilingual author, poet, translator, and educationist from Kannanalloor, Kollam, Kerala. She earned her Ph.D. in Kannada from Dravidian University, Kuppam, and has dedicated her career to fostering literary and cultural connections among the Dravidian languages. As President of the Dravida Bhasha Translators Association (DBTA), Chief Editor of the children's magazine Thodalnudi, and Managing Trustee of Sree Saraswathi Education Trust, she has played a pivotal role in promoting language, literature, and education. For the past 17 years, she has voluntarily taught Kannada to adult learners, enabling more than 4,000 people to acquire proficiency in the language. Dr. Shankar has authored over 20 books spanning poetry, fiction, translations, and short stories, reflecting her versatile literary voice. Her outstanding contributions have been recognized with numerous honors, including the Dubai Karnataka Rajyotsava Award, S.L. Bhyrappa Award, Rashtrakavi Govinda Pai Award, Bhasha Shree Award, Kannada Payaswini Award, O.N.V. Memorial Award, and Bharat Sevak Ratna Award.

Balappa Eerappa Chinagudi.b: Balappa Eerappa Chinagudi is a noted Kannada writer, researcher, educationist, and resource person from Dharwad, Karnataka. With a lifelong commitment to Kannada language and culture, he has made significant contributions to literary scholarship, education, and research. His writings explore a wide range of subjects, including Kannada literature, cultural heritage, history, folklore, and educational thought, reflecting both academic depth and social relevance. Over the years, he has authored several books and scholarly works that have enriched Kannada studies and served as valuable resources for students, researchers, and readers alike. As an educator and mentor, Dr. Chinagudi has actively participated in seminars, workshops, and literary forums, encouraging critical engagement with language and culture. His dedication to promoting Kannada literature and preserving its intellectual traditions has earned him widespread appreciation among scholars and literary circles. He continues to inspire learners and researchers through his scholarship, public lectures, and enduring commitment to education and cultural preservation.

B. S. Shivakumar.b: B. S. Shivakumar is a distinguished Professor of Kannada at Dravidian University, Kuppam, with more than 22 years of experience in teaching, research, and academic leadership. A respected scholar of Kannada, Tulu, Translation Studies, and Dravidian Languages, he has made significant contributions to interdisciplinary research and language studies. He has presented over 60 research papers at national and international conferences, authored and translated several important books, and guided eight doctoral scholars to successful completion. Beyond his academic pursuits, Dr. Shivakumar has held several key administrative positions at the university, contributing to institutional development and the promotion of higher education. His commitment to scholarship and language has earned him widespread recognition, including the Kannada Rajyotsava Award (2019) conferred by the Chennai Karnataka Sangha for his outstanding contribution to Kannada language and literature. Through his research, teaching, and mentorship, he continues to strengthen the study and appreciation of Dravidian languages.

A. P Ashwin Kumar.b: A. P Ashwin Kumar completed his early schooling at St. Joseph’s Indian High School in Bengaluru and went on to earn a Master’s degree in English Literature from Bangalore University. He pursued his doctoral research at the Centre for Study of Culture and Society (CSCS) in Manipal, where he was awarded his Ph.D. He began his professional career as a Research Coordinator at CSCS, Manipal. Later, he served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of English at Tumkur University. Currently, Dr. Ashwin Kumar is a Professor at Ahmedabad University.

Tony Xavier.b: Tony Xavier , is a writer and the Chief Learning Officer of one of India’s oldest test-prep firms. His test-prep book,  Bell the CAT , was published by Penguin Random House India in 2024. His poems have been published in the online journal  Hakara.  His translation of E. Santosh Kumar’s short story  Pavakalude Veedu  (House of Dolls) was published in The Bombay Literary Magazine. He is currently in the process of translating E. Santosh Kumar’s latest novel,  Tapomoyude Achan, for Simon & Schuster. His secret passion is to translate iconic ghazals into English while maintaining fidelity to the refrain and the rhyme scheme that gives the form an intoxication of its own.

Rajashekara Halemane.b: Rajashekara Halemane is an award-winning Kannada writer, critic, and Lecturer at SDM College, Ujire. Recipient of the 2019 Vardhamana Emerging Literary Award, he has authored three books, represented Karnataka at the Sahitya Akademi conference, and won awards in major story competitions including Vijaya Karnataka and Karmaveera .

Beluru Ramamurthy.b: Beluru Ramamurthy  is a veteran Kannada writer and celebrated humorist from Mysuru with over 40 years of literary service. Author of over 800 stories and essays, 21 novels, and numerous humor collections, his popular short story collections include Katha Kusuma and Katha Bimba . A prominent media contributor for AIR and TV serials, he is a recipient of the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award , Goruru Award , and Kuvempu Award , among others.

Shridhara Banavasi.b: Shridhara Banavasi is an award-winning Kannada author with 15 published works across short stories, poetry, novels, and translations. Renowned for books like Ammana Autograph and British Bungalow , his novel Beru won the Central Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar, Kuvempu Award, and Karnataka Sahitya Academy Award. He has also been a featured speaker at various national Sahitya Akademi forums.

Pavitra Jayaraman.b: Pavitra Jayaraman is co-founder at The PARC, a social enterprise that provides multidisciplinary training programmes in mental health for all healthcare workers, mental health professionals and caregivers. She previously headed editorial at White Swan Foundation, a non-profit that created a multilingual online and offline repository to democratise access to mental health information. As a journalist she has worked with NDTV and Mint and continues to write independently.

Ravi Ainapur.b: Ravi is a passionate reader and admirer of Kannada literature with a deep interest in the works of renowned writers like S. L. Bhyrappa, D. R. Bendre, and K. Shivaram Karanth. His love for Kannada language and culture is reflected in his continuous exploration of literature, philosophy, and translation. He strongly believes in preserving and sharing the richness of Kannada thought across generations and languages. Along with his literary interests, he is also enthusiastic about creativity, technology, and community activities. Known for his thoughtful nature and eagerness to learn, Ravi enjoys meaningful conversations and collaborative work. His personality beautifully combines cultural depth with modern curiosity and innovation.

Jayaramachari.b: Jayaramachari is a contemporary Kannada writer, publisher, and independent filmmaker from Mysuru. Balancing his literary pursuits with filmmaking, he is known for exploring diverse themes through both the written word and visual storytelling, reflecting a deep commitment to Kannada literature and creative expression. As an author and publisher, Jayaramachari has contributed to contemporary Kannada writing through works such as Nannavvana Biography, Preethili Bidda Papaskalli, Hamsakshara, and Kilig. Alongside his literary endeavors, he creates independent short films, bringing together storytelling, literature, and cinema in a distinctive and engaging manner.

Kusuma Ayarahalli.b: Kusuma Ayarahalli is a Kannada writer, columnist, and media professional whose work reflects a deep engagement with literature, rural life, and contemporary society. Hailing from a farming family in Ayarahalli, Mysuru, she began her media career with All India Radio and has since built a distinguished career across radio, television, and print journalism. She has worked as a dialogue writer for television serials with acclaimed filmmakers and writers, including T. N. Seetharam and Girish Kasaravalli, and served as a columnist for Vijaya Karnataka for eight years. As a media professional, she has also produced programmes for entertainment and news channels and held leadership roles as a Content Head. An accomplished author, Kusuma Ayarahalli has written essays, novels, and short stories that have earned critical acclaim. Her contributions to Kannada literature have been recognized with several prestigious honours, including the H. M. Nayaka Award, the Kittur Rani Chennamma Award from the Government of Karnataka, and the Lakshmidevamma Story Award from the Karnataka Lekhakiyara Sangha.

Mahesha Araballi.b: Mahesha Araballi is a Kannada writer and IT professional with over two decades of experience in the technology industry. His writing reflects a unique blend of analytical thinking, technological insight, and creative expression, offering thoughtful perspectives on life and contemporary society. His debut memoir, Nenapina Dubbi, marked his entry into Kannada literature and established his distinctive narrative voice. An active participant in literary forums such as " Kathekoota" , Mahesh continues to explore new forms of storytelling and is currently working on an innovative novel. Through his literary pursuits, he brings together the precision of technology and the imagination of creative writing.

Karki Krishnamurthy.b: Karki Krishnamurthy is a Kannada writer and engineer from Bengaluru who seamlessly balances his professional career with a deep passion for literature. Currently associated with Bengaluru International Airport, he explores the many facets of human life through his thoughtful and engaging writing. His literary contributions include short stories, novels, and columns, reflecting a keen understanding of contemporary society and everyday experiences. Through his distinctive storytelling and insightful observations, Karki Krishnamurthy has carved a unique place for himself in contemporary Kannada literature.

Manu Baligar.b: Manu Baligar is a distinguished Kannada writer, poet, translator, and former civil servant who has made significant contributions to literature, public administration, and cultural leadership. A former President of the Kannada Sahitya Parishat, he also served in several key positions in the Government of Karnataka, including as Commissioner of the Department of Kannada and Culture, playing a pivotal role in promoting the state's literary and cultural heritage. A prolific author, Dr. Baligar has written extensively across genres including poetry, short stories, essays, biographies, literary criticism, and drama. He has also translated over 200 poems of Rabindranath Tagore into Kannada, while several of his own works have been translated into English and other Indian languages. His writings reflect a deep engagement with literature, culture, and society, earning him widespread acclaim. In recognition of his outstanding contributions to Kannada literature and public service, Dr. Baligar has been conferred the prestigious Nadoja honor by Kannada University, Hampi, an Honorary Doctorate from Karnatak University, Dharwad, and numerous literary awards, including the Ranna Sahitya Award, Betageri Krishna Sharma Award, and Kempegowda Literary Award. Through his lifelong dedication to literature and culture, he remains one of the most respected voices in contemporary Kannada letters.

Vasanthi Hariprakash.b: Vasanthi Hariprakash is an award-winning journalist, anchor, writer, media entrepreneur, and one of Karnataka’s most engaging conversationalists. With a career spanning print, radio, television, podcasts, and digital media, she has worked with The New Indian Express, NDTV 24x7, All India Radio, Radio City 91.1 FM, BBC World News, and Deccan Herald. She is the Founder and CEO of Pickle Jar Media, a storytelling platform that helps brands, institutions, and changemakers craft compelling narratives through podcasts, events, and strategic communication. A former recipient of the Radio Excellence Award as India’s Best English Radio Jockey, she has also received the Laadli Media Award for Gender Sensitivity in Journalism. Widely admired for her warmth, curiosity, and multilingual fluency, Vasanthi is an accomplished moderator, interviewer, and public speaker. Her deep interest in travel, culture, and people’s stories has made her a distinctive voice in contemporary Indian media and an inspiring presence at literary and public forums.

P. K. Murugan.b: P. K. Murugan is the Executive Vice President and Head of Commercial & Corporate Strategy at JSW, where he plays a pivotal role in driving strategic growth, partnerships, and business transformation across the Group. With decades of leadership experience spanning manufacturing, infrastructure, and corporate strategy, he is widely respected for combining business acumen with a deep appreciation for the transformative power of art, literature, and culture. A passionate patron of the creative ecosystem, Murugan believes that cultural engagement strengthens communities, inspires innovation, and enriches society. His vision aligns closely with the JSW Group's enduring commitment to nurturing India's artistic and literary heritage through initiatives that support museums, public art, cultural festivals, education, and heritage conservation. Under the leadership of Sajjan Jindal, JSW has consistently championed the belief that sustainable development must be accompanied by investments in culture, creativity, and the humanities, making Murugan a natural advocate for meaningful cultural collaborations.

Pranesh Siravara.b: Pranesh Siravara is a distinguished publisher, editor, mentor, and visionary whose contribution to Indian publishing spans nearly five decades. A postgraduate in Mathematics from Bangalore University, Shri Pranesh began his career as a lecturer before moving into pharmaceutical marketing and later research at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences. In 1977, he entered the publishing industry, and in 1991 founded PRISM , which has since grown into one of South India's respected publishing houses. Under his leadership, PRISM pioneered affordable Indian editions of internationally acclaimed medical and engineering textbooks and later expanded into school education, higher education, children's literature, self-development books, and regional language publishing.

Sanghamitre Nagaraghatta.b: Sanghamitra Nagaraghatta is a poet, editor, and artist hailing from Tiptur, now lives in Mysore. Born to N.K. Hanumanthaiah and Shilaja Nagaraghatta, she holds a Master’s degree in English Literature and possesses a deep passion for line drawing, music, and the literary arts. She serves as the editor of Himapakshi , a digital literary magazine on Facebook, and has published two notable poetry collections: Bennigelliya Kannu and Elladaru Hadaviddare .

P. Pragadeeswari.b: P. Pragadeeswari is a student speaker and representative from Mangayarkarasi College of Arts and Science for Women, Madurai, Tamil Nadu , participating in the Book Brahma Literature Festival 2026 (BBLF2026) under the NEWZEN stage.

B. H. M. Manasapriya.b: B. H. M. Manasapriya is a psychologist, researcher, and mental health educator, currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Mental Health Education at the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru. A gold medalist in M.Sc. Psychology from Mangalore University, her academic and research interests focus on child and adolescent psychology, mental health education, and psychological well-being. An active researcher and public speaker, Manasapriya has presented papers at numerous national and international conferences and has contributed to published research. She has engaged with diverse audiences through radio talks, panel discussions, and workshops for students, parents, and educators, promoting practical approaches to mental health awareness, memory enhancement, and psychological well-being. Her contributions have been recognized with several accolades, including the Young Researcher Award for her work in psychology, a national-level essay award on mental health, and recognition for her creative contributions to mental health awareness. Through her research, teaching, and outreach initiatives, B. H. M. Manasapriya continues to advance the field of psychology and mental health education.

V. Sriram Kumar.b: V. Sriram Kumar is the Chief Executive Officer of ELCIA (Electronics City Industries Association), bringing more than three decades of leadership experience in manufacturing, automation, and industry development. Having spent a significant part of his career at FANUC India and served ELCIA in several leadership roles, he has been instrumental in strengthening collaboration between industry, academia, government, and the startup ecosystem to advance India's electronics and semiconductor sectors. A firm believer in inclusive growth and institution-building, Sriram champions innovation alongside community development. Beyond his professional commitments, he is deeply interested in art, literature, culture, and philosophy, often drawing inspiration from great literary works and reflective writing. He believes that technological progress is most meaningful when it is complemented by a vibrant cultural ecosystem that nurtures creativity, empathy, and critical thinking.

Gopini Karunakar.b: Gopini Karunakar is a Telugu short-story writer and novelist from Pileru village in Chittoor district, now based in Hyderabad. He also works as an Associate Director in Telugu cinema. His writing draws deeply from the oral storytelling tradition of his blind grandmother and the dream-filled nights of rural childhood. Marked by quiet emotional depth, lyrical observation of ordinary lives, and a seamless movement between poetry and fiction, his stories have been translated into English and Hindi. He has received national awards twice and the 2012 Katha Kokila Award for Bharatam Bommalu – Marikonni Kathalu. Major works include the poetry collection Poddunne Vachchina Vaana, story collections Deepam Cheppina Kathalu and Maa Tirupati Konda Kathalu, and the novels Sri Balaji Talkies Prema Prabandham and Parijatapaharanam.

K. N. Shanth Kumar.b: K. N. Shanth Kumar is a veteran media professional, editor, publisher, and Director of The Printers (Mysore) Pvt. Ltd., publishers of Deccan Herald, Prajavani, Sudha and Mayura. Associated with the organization since 1983, he has played an important role in shaping its editorial and publishing journey. He has served as Editor of Deccan Herald and Prajavani. He has held leadership positions in the media industry, including Chairman of the Audit Bureau of Circulations and Chairman of the Press Trust of India. He has also served on the Executive Committee of the Indian Newspaper Society. Beyond journalism, Shanth Kumar has a deep engagement with literature, art, photography, culture and public discourse. He is the President and Founding Trustee of the Bangalore International Center (BIC), a significant platform for conversations on literature, arts, culture, society and ideas. His association with BIC reflects his commitment to nurturing Bengaluru’s intellectual and cultural ecosystem.

A. Jayakara Hegde.b: A. Jayakara Hegde is a respected entrepreneur and the guiding force behind Bhavani Industries, with a deep-rooted passion for literature, art, and culture. Beyond his professional pursuits, he has consistently nurtured a strong appreciation for the creative traditions and cultural heritage of Karnataka. His special affection for the folk and performing arts of Coastal Karnataka, particularly Yakshagana, reflects his commitment to preserving and celebrating the region’s rich cultural identity. For him, Yakshagana is not merely a traditional performance but a vibrant synthesis of literature, music, dance, theatre, costume,e and storytelling. His interest in the art form stems from an admiration for its ability to connect generations and keep the oral and cultural traditions of the coast alive. He believes that literature and the arts enrich society by fostering imagination, dialogue,ue and a deeper understanding of our roots. Through his support and engagement with cultural initiatives, A. Jayakara Hegde continues to contribute to the wider ecosystem of literature, art, and heritage.

Vishwas Mudagal.b: Vishwas Mudgal is a Bengaluru-based serial entrepreneur, bestselling author, angel investor, and motivational speaker, known for combining technology, entrepreneurship, and storytelling. An alumnus of R.V. College of Engineering, he began his entrepreneurial journey at 18, setting up an initiative to educate students in rural Karnataka. He later co-founded GoodWorkLabs, a technology and innovation company, and GoodWorks CoWork, building successful businesses through a strong focus on innovation, community, and leadership. Writing is Mudgal’s parallel passion. His debut novel, Losing My Religion, inspired by his own experience of facing the collapse of an internet venture, became a bestselling book and was translated into Hindi and Kannada. His second novel, The Last Avatar – Age of Kalki, blends Indian mythology with science fiction. At the intersection of business, technology, and literature, Mudgal continues to inspire young readers, entrepreneurs, and dreamers through his ideas and storytelling.

Yash Koppikar.b: Yash Koppikar is the co-founder of 3rdSpace, a distinctive cultural space that brings together a concept library, café, and community, creating room for reading, music, conversation, and the exchange of ideas. He is also the founder of DoItSilly Studios, a Bangalore-based creative practice. With over six years of experience in strategy and advertising across London, Mumbai, and Bangalore, Yash has worked with leading brands including Heinz, CureFit, Uniqlo, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Taco Bell, Budweiser, AM/NS India, and the Indian Super League. His work has won recognition at Cannes Lions Grand Prix, Afaqs, Kyoorius, and ET Times Shark Awards. Today, Yash brings his instinct for human insight into building communities and cultural spaces. At the heart of his work is a simple belief: ideas become meaningful when people have the space to encounter, question, and share them.

Paroma Chatterjee.b: Paroma Chatterjee is a seasoned Banking, Fintech and Digital Consumer Business professional with more than 2 decades of experience working with some of the leading Global and Indian organisations. She spent the first phase of her career in banking, launching cards and digital payments for banks like ICICI Bank & Kotak Mahindra Bank in the 2000’s. Since then, she has been at the forefront of the Digital and Fintech revolution in India, starting with launching the first mobile wallet for the leading telecom company - Airtel Money - back in 2010. Paroma has since launched and scaled several flagship digital businesses - including the marketplace business for the e-Commerce behemoth Flipkart. After that she led the scale up of the Indian FinTech company Lendingkart to a USD 400 million book. She joined Revolut in April 2021 to take charge as the CEO of Revolut India. Revolut India is a wholly owned subsidiary of London headquartered global Fintech company, Revolut Group, which is the UK’s fastest growing private tech company and one of Europe’s largest FinTechs. In her capacity as India CEO, Paroma has made Revolut one of just two global companies to obtain the necessary licenses and authorisations from the RBI, to build and launch the first of its kind integrated app in India that combines digital wallets with domestic UPI payments, along with prepaid Visa cards for both local and multi-currency international spending. In recognition of her professional accomplishments and contribution to industry, Paroma has been bestowed with several prestigious awards. She has been featured in the FinTech Magazine’s list of Top 100 Women in FinTech four years in a row 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. She was bestowed with the prestigious Global Indian of the Year award in the House of Commons, London, in 2023 - for her accomplishments in upholding the pride of India on the international stage. Paroma is also a member of IAMAI's governing council and FICCI’s fintech committee. She has been felicitated as the CEO of the Year 2023 by the AI 100 Awards, apart from being featured among the Top Women CEOs of 2021 by Entrepreneur India, and being named one of the Top 25 Women Leaders in Financial Technology of Asia for 2020
